title: Code research: object properties, triggers, rendering, audio and editor-to-game mapping

facts.title: Four unnamed MAMech keys are the 'Standard' damage type of the shield table
facts.fact: A loop over 5 damage-type names (Standard, Energy, Ballistic, Explosive, Flame; name table at 0x459970, stride 0x100) formats %sDamageAbsorbed, %sDamageFactor, %sRecoveryDelay and %sDamagePassedOn. Write and read functions are 0x186A44 and 0x186EA5 (vtable 0x478B90). The Standard versions are the keys 34F74FCC StandardDamageAbsorbed (0.0), 67759A78 StandardDamageFactor (1.0), DCC47761 StandardRecoveryDelay (2.5) and 56E328C5 StandardDamagePassedOn (flag).

facts.title: MATriggerCounter CheckType compares the count
facts.fact: CheckType: 0 means fire when the count equals CounterValue, 1 when greater, 2 when less, and any other value when not equal (code 0x14FD36-0x14FD7B).

facts.title: Camera path timing fields
facts.fact: MACameraProperty pathDurationType: 0 means the time comes from the path, 1 from the controller (editor enum registered at 0x1C9369). Its 'flags' field: 0 means times are counted from the beginning, 1 from the end.

facts.title: MAWaypointGroup TraverseType 2 makes a closed loop
facts.fact: TraverseType 2 makes the patrol route a closed loop (code 0x183E95, 0x185EAE, 0x1860C1). 1 is the constructor default. The code read does not distinguish 1, 3 and 4.

facts.title: Start vehicles need their exact body files in [Assets] (verified)
facts.fact: For every container MARoot references, the editor now walks container → MAPlayerConfiguration → unit and ships Corporal3DObj, TransitionModel and AbandonedModel from the first archive that holds the exact name, without the _low variants (Battle Armor from cinema_5_4.mgf: powerarmor.node, PilotToPowerArmor.node, AbandonedPowerArmor.MGMODEL; Rommel from mission_05.mgf: VMil_RommelMK2.MGMODEL). On a mission_09b base, the Battle Armor and Rommel starts then spawn the player, who can move and fire. Without the files there was no player.

facts.title: Mechs outside the Base's culled set board fine
facts.fact: Neutral Stiletto, Ymir, Wendigo, Nova Cat and Loki placed on a Bogged Down base all board with a Q tap and can walk and fire (runs BRD2_*/BRD3_*). Nothing is needed beyond the owner controller and the unit's own files. This settles the open Stiletto (124691) plus config (124694) question: the culled set does not matter.

facts.title: Without an owner controller a unit cannot be boarded
facts.fact: A unit with StartAbandoned 1 and m_bAIEnabled 0 but no MAOwnerController child (the editor's 'Player can climb in' unticked) shows no prompt, and Q does nothing (run LOCK0).

facts.title: Terrain detail and micro-detail tiling values are repeats across the whole map
facts.fact: The base-map UV spans the whole terrain (u 0.1, v 1.0, set in the ctor sub_002A54C0). TerrainDetailMult, TerrainDetailMult1 and TerrainMicroDetailTiling0/1 multiply that UV: uv_detail1 = uv_base*Mult, uv_detail2 = uv_base*Mult1, uv_micro_i = uv_base*Tiling_i. So they are repeats across the whole map, not per block or per metre. Metres per tile = (samples-1)*WorldScale/Mult: Mission_02 (257 samples, scale 8, 2048 m) gives 32 m for detail 1 (64), 21.3 m for detail 2 (96) and 8.5 m for micro (240). sub_000F6F20 copies the properties into the terrain object (+0x8B4 Mult, +0x8B8 Mult1, +0x8BC DetailBlend, +0x8C0/+0x8C4 Tiling0/1, +0x814 WorldScale, +0x818 CellSize). With two detail maps the multiply is a vertex-shader constant (Mult,Mult,0,1) / (Mult1,Mult1,0,1) bound per draw by sub_0006FEF0; the single-map path bakes uv1 = Mult*(uv0 - blockOriginUV) into the vertex (sub_002A69B0).
facts.how_to_use: The vertex-shader multiply itself is inferred from its constants (the VS microcode was not decoded); the baked single-map path and the whole-map base UV were read. Retail range: Mult 32.145, Mult1 32.128, micro 96.1280; the 8192 m maps all use Mult 32.

facts.title: TerrainCellSize is cells per mesh block side; WorldScale is metres per cell
facts.fact: Each terrain render block has (CellSize+1)^2 vertices (CellSize 16 in all 60 worlds). TerrainWorldScale (8 in 59 worlds, 2 in 3DLobby) is world units per height-field cell, so vertex x = col*scale, z = row*scale, and a block is 128 units across. Height fields are 129, 257 or 1025 samples square.

facts.title: Terrain colour map and detail textures combine in an NV2A register-combiner shader
facts.fact: sub_002A7AB0 picks the material: DETAIL_BLENDED with two detail maps, DETAIL with one, BASE with none, SOLID as fallback. In DETAIL_BLENDED, T0 = colour map, T1 = TerrainDetailMap, T2 = 'TerrainDetailMap 1', V0 = vertex colour (presumably the lighting), and pixel-shader constant c0 = DetailBlend. mix = lerp(T2, T1, T0.a), so colour-map alpha 1 shows detail 1 and 0 shows detail 2. TerrainDetailModulate 0 (shader 0x4A4760): out = 2*V0*lerp(T0, mix, DetailBlend). TerrainDetailModulate 1 (shader 0x4A4940): out = 2*V0*(2*T0*saturate(2*mix*DetailBlend)). DetailBlend is not TFACTOR and does not fade with distance. With fog on (flag [0x50C7A0]) the fog variants 0x4A4670/0x4A4850 add a fog ramp on T3.
facts.how_to_use: The x2 output shift (bit 16) and the final-combiner passthrough were not checked against an XDK header. The single-detail DETAIL shader was not decoded.

facts.title: Terrain micro detail is a second multiply-2x pass that fades to neutral grey
facts.fact: Micro detail is drawn only when both TerrainMicroDetailMap0 and 1 exist. sub_000620A0 sets it up as an extra pass over the base pass with blend DESTCOLOR*src + SRCCOLOR*dst, i.e. out = 2*src*dst, where grey 0.5 is neutral. Its shader (0x4A3D90) averages the two micro maps 50/50, m = 0.5*T0 + 0.5*T1, then src = lerp(m, 0.5, T2). T2 was read as a distance fade, but traces show no fade: the pass is drawn only on blocks within about 128 m (terrain-near-block-passes) (a VS constant 0.02 is set at 0x621A1). DetailBlend does not apply to micro detail, and there is no mask.
facts.how_to_use: The distance-fade reading of T2 is inferred. The KillingField trace shows out = dst*lerp(M0, 2*M0*M1, 0.5)*2, which disagrees with this static decode; use the traced form (kf-paving-is-terrain-micro). The UV x5 there fits Tiling/WorldScale-style repeats, not checked.

facts.title: material_water parameters: offsets, ranges and retail values
facts.fact: The water material is parsed by sub_0004EC40 (model XML) and sub_0004B930 (.mat). It holds wavetexture (+0x68, plus sampler state), an optional reflectiontexture (+0x80, a sky env map), wave_factor (+0x98, 0.64.1.0), distort_factor (+0x9C, 0.5.0.85), fresnel_max (+0xA0) and fresnel_min (+0xA4) (0.1.1.0), and deep_color (+0xA8) and shallow_color (+0xB8) as 0.255 ints scaled by 1/255 and stored in reverse order. There is no scroll-speed or animation-rate parameter. Retail: Env_Water1000x1000(_CityNight) wave 0.85, distort 0.85, fresnel min/max 0.77/1.0, deep 100,122,101, shallow 137,137,97; swamp 0.64, 0.5, 0.2/0.6; Hesperus oil 1.0, 0.7, 0.1/0.1. All use Water_006_NewWater.tif; only CityNight has a reflection map. The draw (sub_000547F0) picks one of 6 routines by the mode byte [0x50C720] and pushes NV2A vertex programs; the renderer object (sub_000541B0) creates the lookup textures Z2WLookup0 (256x64) and PrecisionLookup (1024x1).

source.file: generated recomp_0008.c (made at install time, not in the repository)

facts.how_to_use: Parsing, offsets and retail values are code-confirmed; the draw-time formula is verified by frame trace in t15.

facts.title: Custom Scenarios hold [0x50CA4A]=1 so custom missions skip SPIntro
facts.fact: Custom Scenarios mode zeroes profile+0x90 (campaign index), so every custom mission passed the SPIntro test in sub_002439B7 and played the intro. ma2_scenario.c now holds [0x50CA4A]=1 while custom mode is on and restores it on leaving. Verified in test42: Custom Scenarios to mission in 1.3 s with no SPIntro; the real Campaign still plays Movie\60\English\SPIntro.bik.

facts.title: Editor hidden start activated its window and stole keyboard focus
facts.fact: The game's hidden mode (RECOMP_FB_HIDDEN) never changes the foreground (0 events in 3 runs). The fix belongs in the editor (add SWP_NOACTIVATE); open until the editor owner ships it.
facts.how_to_use: Log foreground changes with editor/tools/fglog.py while launching.

facts.title: 'To the Rescue' is Mission_05
facts.fact: campaign0.ini section LEVEL100 has file = missions\Mission_05.wdf, titleid 524787 and descriptionid 524788. In text.mgf (interface/Text/English/Mission.mgText) 524787 is 'To the Rescue'. The world is Missions/Mission_05.wdf in common.mgf, with 1,354 objects.

facts.title: Campaign reinforcements are mostly dormant unit sets switched on by a trigger
facts.fact: Mission_05 ('To the Rescue') keeps its reinforcement units placed in the level from the start, with IsActive 1 and m_bAIEnabled 0, grouped in a MoeEntitySet. At start-up, MATriggerTimer 74702 'TT - StartUp' (TrgTimerDuration 0) hides each set with MAActionShow Enable 0, EnableTree 1, AISet <set>. Later a trigger shows and wakes them with child actions: MAActionShow Enable 1 + EnableTree 1, MAActionAI EnableAI 1 and usually MAActionNation (5 hostile, 6 friendly), all on the same AISet. Example: MATriggerCuboidalVolume 125707 'TB - 2nd Wave Catch' (VolumeWidth 250, PlayerEntitesOnly 1, TypeOfCheck 3, TriggerAutoReset 0) fires 157381 Show, 125822 AI, 125821 Nation 5 on set 125717 (MATank 125696/125698 Partisan, template 116804; MAMech 141346 Cougar, template 27265). Across the 22 campaign missions: 187 EnableAI-1 and 78 Show-1 actions on units, 49 start-up hides; 521 of 1,008 units start with AI off.
facts.how_to_use: Editor 'Spawn units' recipe: put the units in a new MoeEntitySet with m_bAIEnabled 0. Hide the set at start-up (Show Enable 0 under a 0-second timer; REQUIRED, verified in game: see dormant-units-need-startup-hide).

facts.title: Triggered MASpawner reinforcements: NULL corporeal > spawner > unit
facts.fact: The second pattern is a MACorporeal on template 32093 'NULL' (IsActive 1) holding a MASpawner with Enabled 0 and TriggerEnableID = the trigger UID, holding the unit (Nation 5, AttackPilot 1, m_bAIEnabled 1). In Mission_05, MATriggerRadius 126257 'TR - Return from 3' (EncounterRadius 500) enables spawners 141817 (Cougar), 126237 and 126240 (Partisan tanks), each MaxSpawners 1, MaxActiveSpawners 1, SpawnRate 0, SpawnDelay 0. Spawner 157338 repeats cargo copters (MaxSpawners 10, MaxActiveSpawners 2, SpawnRate 15), enabled by volume 125991. Across 22 missions there are 167 spawners; 157 are Enabled 0 with a TriggerEnableID, triggered most by MATriggerRadius (45), MATrigger (34) and MATriggerCuboidalVolume (22).
facts.how_to_use: Use for 'N units over time'; for a one-off wave, the dormant-set pattern is the common one.

facts.title: Dropship and swap-set actions are rare and cinematic in the campaign
facts.fact: MAActionDropShip appears 3 times (missions 04, 05, 07). In Mission_05 the Icarus dropship MAFlyer 131758 (IsDropShip 1) is woken by MAActionAI and lands 6 s later (125626 Land 1) as staging; it delivers no units. MAActionAddCargo is never used. MAActionSwapSetIn is used 4 times, only in 06b and 11a (5 MASwapSet objects).

facts.title: Editor palette: 801 placeable templates, 279 have no model on any disc
facts.fact: From the editor's --dump-palette over GlobalEntities, 801 templates are placeable. 279 have no model in any disc archive (cut content). The rest the editor groups as 'Foliage & Natural' (112) and 'City & Man-made' (390) by category path and name keywords. These groups are editor-made, not engine data.

facts.title: Template-name prefixes and faction codes
facts.fact: Inferred from category paths and names: BldCom = civilian/commercial building, BldMil = military, BldInd = industrial; VMil / Vciv = military / civilian vehicle; Pep_Civ = civilian person; Bb_/Bd_ = 'Building Base Textures' ground plates (NNxNN = size); LP = low-poly; MP = multiplayer variant; WOB = Word of Blake; DAN/HES/NOR/THE/TER = Dante/Hesperus/Northwind/Thestria/Terra.

facts.title: Template-name suffixes: _CS/_WS/_DS are destroyed states; others unclear
facts.fact: _CS: a MABuilding in a 'Collapsed States' category that is the CorporalDestroyed target of the base template (e.g. BldMil_Icarus_LaunchPad_CS 125902 for 124311); read as 'collapsed state' (role data-confirmed). _WS: also destroyed husks (BldCom_Office07_WS 124224, BldMil_HES_MechFactory_WS 125374; models named *_WS_CS); a WS Talon dropship is a live crashed building in Mission_02, so perhaps 'wreck state' (inferred). _DS: wreck of scenery, vehicles, turrets and civilians (221 MACorporealDestroyed templates; Env_TunnelC_DS 124437 is a building). 'No CS': BldInd_CityGenerator - No CS (36767) has no destroyed variant while 36632 has one, though Vmil_Dropship_Talon (No Adv CS) has one. _BV: collidable, indestructible copies (Env_PedBridgeB_BV 32467 vs a destructible base; Env_TER_BossBV 126168, 17 uses), perhaps a blocking volume (inferred). Canal_Wall _QTR/_HLF probably quarter/half lengths; _CP and _ST unknown. _Vert (BldMil_ResearchCenter_Vert, Canyon_Home_Vert) are unused variants; meaning unknown.
facts.how_to_use: Safe for the editor: show _CS/_WS/_DS as 'destroyed' variants; keep the others under their official names.

facts.title: Far objects: frustum + far plane + model LOD, all automatic; no per-object cull data
facts.fact: The scene renderer (sub_0008C5B0/sub_0008C870) frustum-culls every node: vfunc +0x4C (sub_000836D0) tests the node's bounding sphere against 6 planes (sub_00257740). The far plane (camera+0x80, sub_00044BE0) comes from the camera template's CameraFarPlane (default 475, retail 150.4000), scaled by the PC DrawDistance setting. NodeSwitchLod (sub_000848E0) hides a model beyond radius^2*1.21 of its own .NODE LOD data and fades between LODs. There is no per-class or per-object cull radius, no sectors or portals and no occlusion; bounds come from the model and the placed transform at run time. Fog (FogStart/FogEnd) only colours. So a custom scenario gets the same treatment as retail with no editor-set property: a city in the far corner is not drawn until it is inside the far plane and its models' LOD range.
facts.how_to_use: Per level, the editor can tune FogStart/FogEnd and the camera far plane; set ForceUseLowDetail where only _low models ship.

facts.title: SDS sphere tree is built at run time from node positions and radii
facts.fact: Strings show an 'SDS' binary sphere tree (NodeAdd id,(x,y,z),radius; GetVisibleNodes; GetNearbyNodesSphere; GetNearbyNodesRay) created by the scene manager in sub_0008ED20. Membership is computed at run time, nothing is baked at export. Which queries the renderer uses versus collision is not traced.

facts.title: Campaign AI freezes when no player is within its range
facts.fact: Every 1.0.1.4 s think cycle (sub_00183345 > sub_0016A806 > sub_0016AE44) an AI unit may run only if some player is within max(actor config range at [actor.vt+0x200]+0x1D0, player body radius). Otherwise comp+0x144 |= 0x60 zeroes its velocity and skips its step. Bypasses: flag [sub_18F10]+0x69 and bit 8 of [actor+0x80]. Far units in a custom scenario therefore sleep automatically; no per-object property is needed.

facts.title: Dormant reinforcements must be hidden at start-up, or they stand visible
facts.fact: In game (PC Release 5508c574, a mission_05-based scenario), units saved with m_bAIEnabled 0 but no start-up hide stand visible from the start (two Cougars 90 m ahead, AI asleep). With a start-up MATriggerTimer (duration 0) running MAActionShow Enable 0, EnableTree 1, nothing is visible and no radar dots show. Per-unit actions with ActionEntity work in place of a MoeEntitySet with AISet. Wake-up verified on a map whose only enemies were the two reinforcement Cougars: when a MATriggerRadius fired per-unit MAActionShow Enable 1, MAActionAI EnableAI 1 and MAActionNation 5, two enemy radar dots appeared at once and the units attacked the player with lasers and autocannon.
facts.how_to_use: Editor 'Spawn units': always emit the start-up hide; per-unit ActionEntity or one set with AISet both work.

facts.title: MAPointLight LightMap=1 adds a disc to the 512x512 ground light map
facts.fact: The per-frame 512x512 ground light map covers a camera-placed window at about 4 m per pixel. Each MAPointLight with LightMap=1 adds one disc of diameter 2*LightMapRadius in LightMapColor.rgb at alpha 0x60, blended SRC_ALPHA,ONE. Measured: 49.2 px for R=100 and 98.4 px for R=200; draw colour 60436363 for LightMapColor FF436363. Correction: the map is a camera-placed window about 2 km square, not the whole terrain (ground-lightmap-is-camera-window).

facts.title: Water without a reflectiontexture reflects MAEnvironment EnvironmentMapName
facts.fact: When the water model's material has no reflectiontexture, the water reflection pass uses the level's MAEnvironment EnvironmentMapName cube. Models use the same cube. The old .mat 'type = WATER' form (waves=, fresnel_min/max, deep/shallow) feeds the same 5-pass water renderer.

facts.title: Swamp moss is a separate alpha-blended DETAIL-material corporeal
facts.fact: The moss on swamp water (Bogged Down) is a separate MACorporeal whose model has a DETAIL material with blending=alpha: rgb = lerp(base, detail, 0.5)*2*light, alpha = base.a*detail.a. It is not part of the water material.

facts.title: Editor: water wave texture decodes as a 32^3 volume and the env map as 6 cube faces
facts.fact: The editor's models library already decodes Water_006_NewWater.tif as a 32x32x32 volume and EnvMap_Sky_CityNight_sm.tif as 6 frames. Uploading them as Texture3D and TextureCube works with no decoder change; the 3D Morton unswizzle is already in texture.cpp. Visual check only.

facts.title: Editor: road markings come from the COMPLEX .mat colorshift colours plus the mask
facts.fact: Legacy INI road .mat files (type COMPLEX) carry colorshift0_color and colorshift1_color. Adding mask.G*colorshift0 + mask.B*colorshift1 after lighting gives the blue dashed centre line and yellow kerb dots in the editor, and a mirror sampler fixes the jumbled texture. Visual check only.

facts.title: node_light inner/outer angles are probably half-angles
facts.fact: Reading light_inner_angle/light_outer_angle as half-angles gives Env_Highway_Light a 12.5 m pool at 15 m height, which matches its lightmap min_radius 12. Supports the half-angle reading; not traced. UPGRADE 2026-10-24: now code-confirmed (see spot-cone-half-angles-confirmed).

facts.title: Open render unknowns from editor pass 8
facts.fact: Open: (a) cube-map face order (editor assumes D3D +X,-X,+Y,-Y,+Z,-Z) (the wave volume's channel order is now answered: blue = up, see water-normal-volume-channels); (b) the water thickness LUT scale (editor uses vertical depth / 4 m); (c) the 64x64 ground falloff texture 80679000's curve (editor uses smoothstep); (d) the spot-light direction axis in node space (editor assumes -Y) and what lightmap min_color/max_color do. Answered: lightmap channels (terrain-lightmap-channels). The 512 px ground map is a camera-placed window (ground-lightmap-is-camera-window), and MAPointLight's ground disc uses LightMapRadius, not LightRadius (see pointlight-ground-splat). Not cheaply traceable now: RECOMP_TEX_DUMP stops after 64 first-use textures in this build. Update: cube face order answered (cube-face-order), falloff curve answered (radial-falloff-lut), lightmap min/max fields laid out (node-light-lightmap-fields). Still open: spot axis in node space, min/max_color reader.

facts.title: Mech damage/heat/shield overlays are hidden meshes shown only in that state
facts.fact: 'Mech models carry additive, self-lit overlay meshes that the game hides at rest: cracks_* (atl_cracks, mad_cracks, mech_crack_glow) appear when damaged, heat_lleg/heat_rleg/heat_back (mech_heatsink) when overheated, and shield* (target_jamming material_distort, Wpn_Shields_Anim) when shielded. A viewer should hide them by default. Editor pass 8 confirmed from model data: in a plain renderer these show as white blocks on Atlas, Ymir, Catapult, Loki and MadCat; mech_heatsink is additive with selfillum 255 and an .mtb heat tint.

facts.title: material_env glass: 2*V0*base + base.a*cube.a*tint at constant-alpha opacity
facts.fact: mech_glass (material_env) has diffuse 0, opacity 0.5.0.75, reflectivity 0.5 and alpha blending. Combiner: out = 2*V0*base + base.a*cube.a*tint, blended at the material opacity through CONSTANT_ALPHA.

facts.title: COMPLEX material: glow mask, tint variant, detail gated by 1-mask.a, constant-alpha translucency
facts.fact: COMPLEX materials add glow mask.g*colorshift0 + mask.b*colorshift1 after lighting. A tint variant instead multiplies the light by colorshift1 under mask.b (selected by colorshift1_diffuse=true, see complex-colorshift1-diffuse). An optional detail layer is gated by (1-mask.a), and translucency is the opacity through CONSTANT_ALPHA blending. Correction: the glow is not added after lighting; out = 2*(light*lit + mask.g*C0 + mask.b*C1), see complex-glow-doubled.

facts.title: material_specular_mask: 2*V0*base + mask.r*cube.a*spec_color
facts.fact: material_specular_mask draws out = 2*V0*base + mask.r*cube.a*spec_color: the mask's red channel gates an environment-cube specular in spec_color.

facts.title: Coplanar DETAIL decals draw with depth EQUAL
facts.fact: Coplanar DETAIL decals (KillingField paving) are drawn with depth test EQUAL over the surface below: out = lerp(base, 2*base*detail, 0.5)*2*light. CORRECTED by editor pass 8: the KillingField depth-EQUAL 'paving' draw is the terrain micro-detail pass (see kf-paving-is-terrain-micro), not a decal object.

facts.title: Levels without a ground light map light terrain and water by vertex colour
facts.fact: On levels with no ground light map (NewRiverCity), terrain and water lighting is the vertex colour V0, and the terrain also adds V1. New River City's MadCat uses model_low/madcat.mgmodel with the materials above.

facts.title: Env_Highway_Light's bulb, cone and spot light sit under an .mtb-hidden 'lightbulb' node
facts.fact: In Env_Highway_Light the lightbulb mesh (material_color_shift), the additive cone mesh and the spot node_light all sit under the node 'lightbulb', which the lamp's .mtb hides with MAModSubObjectShow (turned_on true). The game shows them lit at night. The editor draws .mtb-hidden subtrees that hold a node_light when Scene lights is on. Open: what drives the rule (night flag or a lights-on event). A candidate is MAActionLights (LightSet, LightAction 2 = on, 3 = off; 14 uses), not checked. NOTE 2026-10-24: any claim that bulbs are lit at night is unverified; see lamp-bulb-no-runtime-switch. UPDATE 2026-10-24: resolved in favour of hidden-by-default (highway-lamp-mtb-hides-bulb).

facts.title: Lamp ground-pool radius lerp is unclamped, with height measured from the terrain
facts.fact: Mission_02 street lamps stand about 26 m above the TERRAIN (the streets are plates about 16 m up). The unclamped lerp min_radius + (max-min)*h/max_height = 12 + 8*26/15 = 26 m matches the traced 13.2 px quad. So the node_light lightmap radius lerp is unclamped, and the height is measured from the terrain, not the street plate.

facts.title: material_color_shift visors and lights are dark at rest
facts.fact: material_color_shift visors and lights (e.g. loki_visor) have diffuse 25,25,25, shading material_only, alpha blending and colorshift0_color 0,0,0, so they draw dark at rest, not white.

facts.title: Water_006_NewWater normal volume: blue = up (r,g,b = x,z,y)
facts.fact: The 32^3 wave normal volume stores r,g,b = x,z,y, so blue is up. The other channel orders give no highlights in the editor.

facts.title: MACorporeal with \tmpdev\NULL\NULL.NODE is an invisible placeholder
facts.fact: MACorporeal objects whose model is \tmpdev\NULL\NULL.NODE draw nothing in game (70 in New River City, 2 in Mission_17a; from the editor's object dump). They are logic holders such as spawner parents; editors should draw them as markers, not models.

facts.title: Editor headless --shot before build 23CCAD2C fired before models finished loading
facts.fact: Before editor build 23CCAD2C, the headless --shot saved at frame 10, before the per-frame model budget had loaded everything: unloaded models drew as coloured placeholder boxes and the sky could be missing. Treat older headless editor shots with care.

facts.title: Static lightmap (MAEnvironment LightMapName) is A8L8: L x ambient = L.rgb, A = shadow mask = L.a
facts.fact: The terrain lightmap is not a MATerrain property. It is MAEnvironment LightMapName (key A6B3EE2E, a \Terrain\*.tif; blank in 20 worlds, which then use vertex lighting). Mission_02's is 128x128 swizzled A8L8. Each frame the LightMap Manager (sub_00052F90) draws it into the 512x512 ground map: L.rgb = lightmap.L x LightAmbientColor (C0 = FF1B213B in Mission_02) and L.a = lightmap.A; light splats then add rgb only (colour mask 00010101), so L.a stays the lightmap alpha. Terrain (trace line 1321, T3 = the map) lights with light = V1.rgb*V1.a*L.a + L.rgb and outputs 2*light*albedo. So A is a shadow mask (0 = shadowed) gating V1, and L is a baked ambient/sky term. The asset audit confirmed this with the files: Terrain/*_lightmap.tif is A8L8 (MGIc flags 0x17) and terrain light = sun*max(N.L,0)*A + ambient*L (+ lamp pools); near blocks redo the lighting per pixel (terrain-near-block-passes). The map's extent is built from the camera frustum clamped to the level limits in sub_00052F90, so it may be a moving window rather than the whole terrain.
facts.how_to_use: Editor: light = sun*N.L*lightmap.A + lightmap.L*ambient + lamp splats; albedo per terrain-detail-combine.

facts.title: COMPLEX colorshift1_diffuse picks glow (false) or light tint (true)
facts.fact: In COMPLEX materials colorshift0 is always an additive glow (mask.g*colorshift0_color). colorshift1_diffuse=false makes colorshift1 an additive glow too (mask.b*colorshift1_color); colorshift1_diffuse=true makes it a light tint, light' = lerp(light, light*colorshift1_color, mask.b), used for team/paint colours (pilot 200,43,43; NovaCat/BA 90,90,90). The combiner constants' alpha byte is colorshiftN_bloom. The field is in model XML (colorshift1_diffuse="true|false") and legacy .mat (0/1). Matched Mission_16 trace lines 11974/12779 to BldCom_TER_Structure_01 and Tower_03.

facts.title: Terrain blocks within ~128 m get a per-pixel lighting pass and a micro-detail pass
facts.fact: Terrain blocks whose nearest point is within about 128 m of the eye (6 of 43 blocks in the KillingField frame) draw three passes: (a) the normal 7-stage terrain combiner; (b) an opaque per-pixel lighting pass (PASSTHRU/DOT_PRODUCT/DOT_ST) that REPLACES the colour with (dot(2N-1, 2V0-1)*shadow*DirectionalLightColor + L.rgb) * V1; (c) the micro-detail modulate with depth EQUAL, 2*lerp(M0, 2*M0*M1, 0.5)*dst. facts.title: COMPLEX output = 2*(light*lit + mask.g*C0 + mask.b*C1): glow is doubled, inside the final x2
facts.fact: The COMPLEX combiner's final stage is out = 2 * (light * lit + mask.g * colorshift0 + mask.b * colorshift1), so glow/marking colours are effectively x2, not added after a separate x2 lighting stage. facts.title: MAActionLights: LightAction 0/2 = on, 1/3 = off; point lights toggle LightOn, corporeals toggle flag bits

Non-MACorporeal members (MAPointLight path, sub_0012A230) write LightOn (+0x90) and call slot +0x90 on the attached light at +0xA4: actions 0 and 2 = on, 1 and 3 = off. facts.title: Low-LOD 'Mech bodies are normal-mapped: *_cmplx_low.tif (multitexture slot) drives a per-pixel N.L pre-pass
facts.fact: Mission_15 draws n 2105 and n 2429 (prim 6 strips; n = index count) are the COMPLEX low-LOD 'Mech bodies: Corvus (corvus_body_low, models/Mechs/Light/Corvus/model_low) and Blood Asp (bloodasp_body_low; 2429 is a subset of its body meshes, not pinned). Pass 1: t0 = the material's *_cmplx_low.tif (Texture_Dump/Mechs/bloodasp_body_cmplx_low.tif, corvus_body_cmplx_low.tif; 256x256 DXT1, a tangent-space normal map, the material's multitexture slot, so no normal_map slot is needed); VS constants c112.114 are the tangent basis, V0 carries the per-vertex tangent-space light vector, stage 0 does N.L, stages 1-2 (DOT_PRODUCT, DOT_ST) look up t2 80765000, a 64x64 8-bit LUT (bound only in these draws, not the falloff texture 80679000, no asset found, probably generated at runtime; curve unknown). It writes into the main 640x480 back buffer 0035C000 (not offscreen). Pass 2 is the road-style COMPLEX recipe (t0 = DXT1 multi map, t1 = DXT5 base 0F 256^2, t2 = the 32^2 cube 80A27000) at depth EQUAL, reading the frame buffer as t3 (V0 += FB). Scope: any 'Mech using material_complex at 256^2 (distant AI 'Mechs too), not a player-only or cockpit effect; high-LOD 'Mechs use material_specular_mask instead. bump2.tif is not involved.
facts.how_to_use: Editor R2-12 (1): this is a 'Mech material path, not a world-object one; implement as N.L from the _cmplx_low normal map added to V0, or mark for static placements if the editor draws 'Mechs with high-LOD models.

facts.title: Material detail_blend (additive2x / alphablend / modulate2x) picks the detail shader; detail_blend_level -> C0.a
facts.fact: The .mat string field detail_blend takes additive2x, alphablend or modulate2x (strings at xbe 0x45E240, 0x45E2BC, 0x45E234). COMPLEX parses it in sub_0004CFE0 (mat+0xC8), SPECULAR_MASK in sub_0004DB80 (mat+0x98). The COMPLEX instance ctor sub_00072930 picks the pixel shader: additive2x -> 0x4A4D00 (+0x4A50C0), alphablend -> 0x4A4DF0 (+0x4A51B0), otherwise modulate2x -> 0x4A4C10 (+0x4A4FD0); no detail -> 0x4A4B20 or 0x4A52A0 (flag mat+0x108). detail_blend_level (float, mat+0xD4 -> instance+0x70) is written as C0 = (0,0,0,level) by sub_00072EB0 via sub_0040C2B0, so Mission_05's 0.44 (0x70/255) and the 0.53 at line 3709 are that field. Inferred: additive2x = the signed add base' = lerp(base, base+2d-1, level), alphablend = plain lerp (shaders not decoded against trace line 5489). No .mat text files found outside game_files, so file values are unverified.
facts.how_to_use: Editor: read detail_blend + detail_blend_level from the .mat; additive2x = signed add lerped by level, alphablend = lerp by level, modulate2x = base*2*detail.

facts.title: Spot lights point along +Z of their light matrix (up = +Y); angles are half-angles
facts.fact: Spot render-light ctor sub_0006E450 (vtable 0x461180); orientation struct at light+0x24 (flags 0x203, direction +4, up +0x10, 4x4 matrix +0x1C). sub_0024F4A0 fills direction from matrix row 2 (+Z) and up from row 1 (+Y). The cone test sub_0006EA10 uses dot(direction, p - lightpos)/|d| against the cone threshold, so the lit side is +Z. SetAngles sub_0006E920 runs fsincos on the angles (tan at +0xE8/+0xE4, cone scale from cos), so they are half-angles. sub_00060B20 uploads the matrix as VS constants. Not traced: the caller that passes the node_light world matrix in (SetMatrix, vtable 0x461158 slot 2, sub_0006D5B0), so +Z of the node frame is inferred. CORRECTION 2026-10-24: cone is centred on -dir, so the lit side is probably the opposite sign (see spot-axis-sign). RULING: the code facts describe the RENDER LIGHT's own orientation matrix (direction = row 2, cone centred on -dir) and stand as code. What is NOT proven is that this matrix is the .mtb node's world matrix: the SetMatrix (sub_0006D5B0) caller for node lights was never found. Model geometry plus a same-pose game frame show the beam follows the NODE's local -Y (node-light-spot-beam-direction-is-the-light-nodes-local-minus-y-not-plus-z-geometry-and-game-frame, runtime-observed HIGH). Both hold if the engine applies a basis change from node to light matrix. For editor authoring use node -Y. Editor caveat: it turns light directions by heading only (no pitch/roll; M01b searchlights are pitched 60).
facts.how_to_use: Editor: spot direction = node +Z (not -Y); check against a lamp's cone.

facts.title: Bots --bots 0v1: the human joins Red and gets a RANDOM Red spot per match (verified); the code reading of slot % count was wrong
facts.fact: ma2_scenario.c:1045 test_args parses --bots as <red>v<blue>, then calls ma2_bots_test_config (bots/ma2_bots_ui.c:133). place_humans (ma2_bots_ui.c:338) puts the human on the short side (red<blue -> 0, blue<red -> 1; side 0 is also the default), so 0v1 puts the human on Red. ma2_bots_core.c:370-395 builds the roster. In recomp_0037.c, sub_001665DE (line 4374) walks the player vector 0x50E280.84 and calls sub_00166AD4(slot, team) with slot = index + arg1. 0x50E4D8.DC is ONE begin/end vector of every spot, not a per-team list (this corrects bots-spawn-placement). sub_00166AD4 (line 5193) keeps the spots with spot+0x90 == 0 or spot+0x90-1 == team, in list order, and picks matches[slot % count] (deterministic). If nothing matches, it takes the first spot overall. spot+0x90 = MALevelStart TeamIndex (0 any, 1 Red, 2 Blue). GoCommando.wdf has 36 MALevelStarts at y=95, RandomDistance 2.0: 12 neutral, 12 Red, 12 Blue. If the neutral spots are registered, the human (slot 0) gets 'Start 01' UID 126376 (182.9, 95, 543.5), StartOrientation 1.309 rad. Otherwise it gets the first Red spot in list order, probably 'Red Start 12' UID 120725 (214.9, 95, 840.5), 1.676 rad. Red spots: x 153-218, z 600-890; Blue: x 490-706. Verified in game (5 runs, memory probe): the human is Red (nation 1) and lands on a different Red spot each match: (214.93,95,841.48) yaw 96 [Red Start 12], (215.53,95,786.43) 90, (209.72,95,754.47) 90 twice, (163.08,95,626.32) 89. The 1-6 m offsets match RandomDistance. 'Start 01' (neutral) never appeared, and the spot is NOT deterministic, so the static reading above is wrong somewhere (spots shuffled, or slot is randomized). The player spawns at y=95 and drops to the ground.
facts.how_to_use: Editor/quick-test: any Red MALevelStart can be the human start in GoCommando; to match a run, read the pose with RECOMP_BOT_DIAG=1 ([HUMAN-HP]).

facts.title: Culture generator: count per cell = cellArea*Density*level*1e-6 (Density = instances per 1e6 units^2 at full level); seeded per cell
facts.fact:
Object offsets are the dictionary's reader-relative offsets + 0x20. Ctor sub_0017ED88 sets: GenerationTemplate 0x78; Density 0x7C (default 1000); flags 0x80 Align, 0x81 RandomRot, 0x82 SnapToGrid; RandomScaleRange 0x84; MaxSlope 0x88 (90); MinSlope 0x8C; StartFade 0x90 (200); StopFade 0x94 (300); NearestNeighbor 0x98; GridOffset 0x9C; GridScale 0xA4 (10); GridAngle 0xAC; PrePoolCount 0xB0. sub_001801F6 runs once per integer grid cell:
1. Cell -> world via the matrix at +0x16C (built by sub_00180C16 from GridOffset/Scale/Angle). 2. level = ((texel & mask) >> shift)/(2^NBits-1) from the culture map (sub_0018045F, sub_00189E62, sub_001899C6). Level 0 skips the cell. 3. f = cellArea(+0xD0)*Density*level*1e-6 (constant at 0x4541EC); count = floor(f) + (rand < frac(f)); SnapToGrid clamps it to 1. 4. Position = cell + rand(0.001, 0.999) per axis (cell + 0.001 when snapped); random yaw when RandomRot is set.
cellArea (sub_0017FB4A) is the cross product of the grid axes, so 100 for GridScale 10x10 (inferred). Slope: sub_001804C3 accepts MinSlope <= acos(normal.y) in degrees <= MaxSlope; Align (+0x80) aligns to the slope. Fade: sub_0017FF5E scales StartFade/StopFade by the draw-distance multiplier [0x50C93C+0x78]*[+0x7C], with t = (stop-d)/(stop-start) clamped; the generation radius comes from StopFade (sub_0017FB05). Seed = (cx<<16) ^ entity_id(+0x2C) ^ cy (sub_0001DA00; RNG state +0x1D4; rand sub_0001DBE0), deterministic per cell. Not traced: the RandomScaleRange use (sub_0018063B/sub_001807CE), the NearestNeighbor rejection (sub_00180518), and the exact rand order. The jitter range 0x493AC4/C8 = 0.001/0.999, and 0x4541EC = 1e-6. The yaw max 0x50F4EC and the degree constant 0x50F4F0 are in uninitialised data (set at runtime, probably 2*pi and 180/pi). [v232: see culture-count-formula-field-offset-conflict-density-0x7c-vs-cellarea-0x7c; seed = per culture-map texel, culture-seed-cell-vs-texel-reconciled-.]
facts.how_to_use: Editor scatter: use this formula. Density is per 1e6 world units^2 (per km^2 if 1 unit = 1 m); Density 8000 = 0.8 per 10x10 cell at full level. Fades follow the draw-distance setting.

facts.title: material_detail is fixed-function: modulate / alphablend / colorblend set by texture stages with TFACTOR = level; no framebuffer blend
facts.fact: sub_0004C080 parses material_detail: base mat+0x68, detail mat+0x80, blend_level mat+0x98, blend mat+0x9C (modulate 0, alphablend 1, colorblend 2 from string 0x45E2B0). The instance ctor sub_00070040 (vtable 0x461408) stores level at +0x38, a gray ARGB of the level at +0x3C and the mode at +0x40. sub_00070320 dispatches to sub_000705F0 (modulate), sub_00070860 (alphablend) or sub_000703E0 (colorblend). All three set TFACTOR (state 0x94) to the gray level, and none sets alpha blending. - Modulate, from the code: stage0 MODULATE2X(detail, TFACTOR), stage1 MODULATE(base, current), stage2 MODULATE2X(current, diffuse), giving 4*L*base*detail*V0. This CONFLICTS with the audit's KF slab trace lerp(base, 2*base*detail, L) (mat-detail-blend, line 12101), which may be a COMPLEX or detail_blended draw. Prefer the trace for KF until the draw is identified. - Alphablend: stage0 base (SELECTARG1); stage1 detail with colour op 15, then MODULATE2X with diffuse. Op 15 is BLENDCURRENTALPHA per the runtime header, but since TFACTOR is set and unused, BLENDFACTORALPHA is inferred (about 80%): 2*V0*lerp(base, detail, L). - Colorblend: op 11 ADDSMOOTH, then MODULATE2X with diffuse. The pixel shaders 0x4A4760/0x4A4940/0x4A4670/0x4A4850 belong to sub_0006F8C0 = material_detail_blended (3 textures), not plain material_detail. Resolution (audit #3): the KF slab material base_concrete_gray.mat uses detail_blend = modulate2x, level 0.5. That is the COMPLEX/detail_blend key, not plain material_detail's 'blend'. Its trace lerp(base, 2*base*detail, L)*2*light equals 4*base*detail*light at L = 1. The M13b trunks show the same shape at L = 0.8. So the trace path is the shader path (complex-detail-shader-modes modulate2x, C0.a = level), and the fixed-function 4*L*base*detail*V0 applies only to plain material_detail with blend=modulate. These agree at L = 1 and differ below it. the two are different material types, not a contradiction. Not yet confirmed: that a plain blend=modulate draw in a trace shows 4*L*b*d*V0.
facts.how_to_use: Editor: alphablend detail = 2*V0*lerp(base, detail, level). Modulate: follow the trace for the KF slab, and note the code path gives 4*L*base*detail*V0.

facts.title: CORRECTED: KF trace line 10034 is a material_detail near-model draw (the KF pad family), not the terrain micro-detail pass
facts.fact: Correction (audit #3, 2026-10-22): KF trace line 10034 is program n46 (prog 08021, 5 stages), not terrain micro detail. Textures: t0 80C0A000 128x128 fmt 0E (base), t1 807A5000 128x128 fmt 0C (detail), t3 = the 640x480 frame copy (pre-pass light). z func EQUAL (202) after an untextured pre-pass of the same n46 (tex off, line 10882). Combine: s0 R0 = 2*T0*T1; s1 T0 = lerp(T0, R0, C0.a = 0.5); s2 R1 = V0 + T3; s3 R0 = 2*T0*R1; s4 R0 += R1.a*C0.rgb (C0 = 626266, specular/glow; R1.a = T0.a*T3.a). So out = 2*lerp(M0, 2*M0*M1, 0.5)*(V0 + FB) + R1.a*626266. Pixel 320,330 history: terrain n738 (the same program as UC line 831: T0 mask, two layers, light map) gives (26,17,13); the n46 pre-pass gives (95,74,67); this n46 material draw gives (61,46,42). The KF probe never hit a terrain micro pass (the UC line 1193 blend 306/300 tex0 x60 draw). The KF near terrain is n738 and carries the same detail combine as UC. A bare-terrain KF pixel has not been traced yet (audit #3 game shot pending). Superseded: the earlier 'terrain micro pass' label and the 'out = dst*lerp(.)*2' formula from pass 8 round 3.

facts.title: Water reflection pass: framebuffer alpha = fresnel weight lerp(C0.b, C0.a, sat(N.V)); it is NOT the env cube's alpha (M05 E9)
facts.fact: Combiner decode of the 2-stage reflection pass (M05 trace about line 7845, prog 64621, ctl 00011102; the render target is t0 80230000, the frame holding the normal-pass output). Stage 0: rgb icw 48440000 = A expand(T0) x B expand(V0); ocw 000820D0 = AB_DOT into R1 with blue-to-alpha, so R1.a = dot(N, V), where N = the normal-pass texel and V0 = the per-vertex view vector, encoded 0.1. Stage 1: rgb icw CB200000 = T3 (32x32 cube, DOT_RFLCT_SPEC) x 1 -> R0.rgb. Alpha icw 1DD1C13D = R1.a(unsigned, so clamped 0.1) x C0.a + C0.b x (1 - R1.a) -> R0.a, with stage constant C0 = C4FFFFFF (a 0.77, b 1.0). Blend is off, so the frame gets rgb = cube sample and alpha = fresnel weight: 1.0 at N.V = 0 (grazing), 0.77 at N.V = 1. The M05 probe E9 (0.913) implies N.V ~ 0.37. The 5-stage composite then reads this destination alpha as R.a. Same constants in M07 (fresnel 0.91 there too).
facts.how_to_use: Editor water: do not use the cube texture's alpha (the editor reads 0). Compute w = mix(C0.b, C0.a, clamp(dot(N, V), 0, 1)) with C0.a = 0xC4/255 and C0.b = 1.0, and use it where the composite uses R.a. Inferred: with w = 0 the composite falls back to the darker tint*scene term, which may be the whole reason the editor needed ~1.6x ambient; drop that boost once w is computed and re-check.

The implied light-map value is src ~(0.24,0.22,0.29), B/R 1.22, Correction (audit #3, line 19508): the light draw is out = fb*2*L with L = V0.rgb*V0.a*T.a + T.rgb, V0 = (0.353,0.282,0.341, a 0.56); the measured L is (0.239,0.220,0.293). facts.title: 5-pass water composite (M05/M07 traces): out = lerp(lerp(C1,C0,thick)*scene, 2*R*light, R.a*thickA); shared constants, fog differs
facts.fact: M05 water at the teleport view (probe 200,350) uses the same constants as M07: deep C0 = 3F647A65, shallow C1 = 3F898961, fresnel C0 = C4FFFFFF. Only the fog colour differs (A0A0A0 vs B0B0B0). Probe: ground (66,66,63); normal (125,129,255); cube sample R (130,130,143) with alpha E9; composite (82,79,78). Composite: tint = lerp(C1, C0, thick)*scene; out = lerp(tint, 2*R*light, w), with w = R.a * the thickness alpha. light = V0*G.a + G.rgb, with V0 only (0.114, 0.091, 0.068), so light is about 0.3. The water env cube is neutral grey at these view angles, not sky-coloured. Stage decode (audit #3, line 7901, rcdec): s0-s1 tint = lerp(C1, C0, T1.a)*T1.rgb (T1 = scene copy); the thickness alpha R1.a is scaled x4 on the alpha path. s2 light = V0*T2.a + T2.rgb (T2 = the 512 ground map). s3 refl = 2*T0.rgb*light (T0 = the reflection-pass colour; this is the only x2), T0.a = T0.a*R1.a. s4 out = lerp(T1*tint, refl, T0.a). The final combiner adds fog: final = FOG.a*R0 + (1-FOG.a)*FOG.rgb (fog colour A0A0A0, coefficients 2/-1). There is no further x2 after the lerp. T0.a is the fresnel weight (see water-reflection-fresnel-dst-alpha). The final composite is fogged like terrain (f = 1 - oFog.x, linear); see audit18-m05-water-distance.
facts.how_to_use: Editor water: use this composite; reflection = 2*cube*ground-map light, not raw sky colour.

facts.title: Fixed-function linear fog: f = px + oFog*py - 1; distance coefficients map to metres (KF 750-950, UC 400-950); 2/-1 = pre-normalised oFog (f = 1 - oFog)
facts.fact: Runtime fog unit (kit/source/game/src/kernel/nv2a_pb_exec.c fog_factor, mode 2601 = LINEAR): f = px + d*py - 1, where d = the vertex program's oFog.x and f = 1 means no fog. Frame-trace counts of fog-enabled draws: KF 308 draws with 5.75/-0.005, so f = 4.75 - 0.005*d, fog from d = 750 (f = 1) to 950 (f = 0). BD composite 2.636/-0.001818 (350-900 m, colour A6BBBA). UC 209 draws with 2.727/-0.001818, so f = 1.727 - 0.001818*d, fog from 400 to 950. Generally, start = (px-2)/(-py) and end = (px-1)/(-py), with d in metres (eye distance or w, as the vertex program writes it). Coefficients 2/-1 give f = 1 - d, so those programs write an already-normalised fog amount (0 = clear, 1 = fully fogged). Only 2-3 draws per level use 2/-1 in KF and UC (likely the water), but in M05 780 of 901 fog draws do. Other sets seen: black-fog 2/-0.5 or a different range, and colour 80808080 draws. Inferred: the water program's oFog is probably (eyeDist - start)/(end - start) for the level's fog range; on M05 (150-500 m), f = 0.756 at the far probe would put that pixel ~235 m from the eye (UNVERIFIED estimate, not measured). The vertex program code was not read. Editor state (pass 11, 2026-10-22): water and terrain fog use fg = (dist - 150)/(500 - 150) with dist measured from the orbit target; at --cam 1801,244,15,-82,8 all visible water is under 150 m, so fg = 0 and far-water fog was not exercised. M05 probe pose (audit #3): m05w and m05w2 are the same run/frame; player (1800.87,5.36,243.85), heading -82 deg (looking toward -x); chase camera an estimated 10-15 m behind (higher x) and a few m up, not measured. Probes near 200,350 / far 450,210 on the 640x480 surface (shot 400,700 / 900,420). World xz and eye distance of the probes are not in the trace (only the quad's first, off-screen vertex is printed); the editor's depth at those pixels can settle it. Pass-11 follow-up (2026-10-22): the editor's water fog works (fg ~0.6 at range from a higher cam, audit21), but the M05 game probe pose is not matched. --cam 1801,244,15,-82,8 puts the editor eye only ~2 m up (15*sin 8 deg) vs the game's chase camera (est. 5-8 m up, 10-15 m behind), and all visible water there is under 150 m (fg = 0). There is no per-pixel distance hook (water hook 13 shows fg only). Open: measure the game chase-camera height/offset, then repeat with a matched --cam. BD stage probe: fog coordinate 13.85 -> factor 1.611 = 2.636 - 0.001818*13.85 - 1, confirming that on the BD water composite oFog = eye distance in metres (verified). M05 NEAR probe (200,350) fog factor = 0.758, measured by stageprobe3. So the near pixel (82-83,79-80,78-79) is itself fogged ~24%. The earlier fit assumed the near pixel was unfogged; it is superseded, and the far-brightening fit (f 0.756 at 450,210) needs redoing with real per-probe factors.
facts.how_to_use: Editor: measure fog distance from the eye, not from the orbit target. For distance-coefficient draws use start/end as above. For 2/-1 draws, use the level's fog start/end on eye distance.

facts.title: Audit18 M05 water: near crop matches (68,64,68 vs 65,62,60); the game brightens and neutralises with distance, the editor stays flat and lilac
facts.fact: Audit18 (editor) vs the game on M05 water. Near crop: editor (68.1,63.5,67.9) vs game (65,62,60). Brightness was fixed by taking thickness along the view ray. Far water: the game rises from near (84,81,80) to far (99-103,96-100,99-103); the editor is flat at ~63-70. Hue: the game's cube B/R is 1.07 far vs 1.10 near, near-neutral; the editor stays 7-10% lilac. two terms in the traced composite grow with distance and would give both the brightening and the neutral hue. (a) The final-combiner fog, FOG.a*R0 + (1-FOG.a)*A0A0A0, blends toward neutral grey 160. (b) The fresnel weight w = mix(1.0, 0.77, sat(N.V)) goes to 1.0 at grazing views, weighting the brighter reflection 2*R*light. The cube also samples brighter and more neutral at horizontal reflection vectors (second probe). Fog caveat (audit #3): both water composite draws have fog enable 1, mode 2601, colour A0A0A0, coefficients 2/-1. Other levels behave as fog.a = c0 + c1*w (UC 2.727 - 0.001818*w, KF 5.75 - 0.005*w). Read that way, the water's 2/-1 gives fog.a = 0 (pure grey 160) at w ~1911, which contradicts the traced (101,97,99). So the water fog input is not plain w; likely the water vertex program writes its own fog value (oFog), which the trace does not log. The fog hypothesis is unproven until a two-probe game trace (far and mid water, different w) compares the pre-fog composite value with the final pixel. Fog resolved (audit #3, medium-high): the final water composite IS fogged. Final combiner 130C0300 gives out = FOG.a*R0 + (1-FOG.a)*A0A0A0, the same setup as the terrain draw; the cube and reflection passes have fog off (fin 0000000C). Runtime factor f = 1 - oFog.x per vertex (nv2a_pb_exec.c fog_factor, LINEAR mode), so the 2/-1 coefficients act on the vertex program's fog output, not on w. Fit: with the same pre-fog colour as the near pixel (82,79,78), f = 0.756 at the far pixel gives 0.756*(82,79,78) + 0.244*160 = (101,99,98) vs the traced (101,97,99). oFog.x itself was not read. Note: the near probe 200,350 is also fogged (factor 0.758, stageprobe3), so the far-vs-near brightening is not explained by fog alone; see fog-coefficients-linear-mapping.
facts.how_to_use: Editor water: fog the final composite toward the level fog colour (A0A0A0 on M05) with the same per-vertex linear factor as terrain; reflection/cube passes unfogged. This should give the far brightening and the neutral hue.

facts.title: M05 water composite fully decoded with real render-target values (stageprobe4): matches the game pixel within 1 level
facts.fact: stageprobe4 (B1AE4060, GPU readback of render targets; validated on M05 by audit #3). probe 200,350, water composite draw 5507460, prog 00421, fin 130C0300; pixel E8878793 -> (83,80,79); fog A0A0A0, factor 0.758. Inputs: V0 = (0.1145,0.0907,0.068, a 0.5); C0 = (0.392,0.478,0.396, a 0.247); C1 = (0.537,0.537,0.380, a 0.247); T1 (320x240 scene copy) = (0.2738,0.2702,0.2510, a 0.1651); T2 (ground map 80B0C000) = (0.1843,0.1843,0.2017, a 0.777); T0 at draw time = the pre-draw framebuffer = (0.529,0.529,0.576, a 0.91) (the probe's own T0 read is post-draw). Stages: s0 R0 = T1.a*C0 + (1-T1.a)*C1; s1 T1' = R0*T1.rgb, R1.a = 4*T1.a = 0.66; s2 R0 = V0*T2.a + T2.rgb = (0.273,0.255,0.254); s3 T0' = 2*T0pre*R0, T0.a = 0.91*0.66 = 0.60; s4 R0 = 0.6*T0' + 0.4*T1'; fog 0.758*R0 + 0.242*0.627. Hand decode (83.1,81.0,80.1) vs game (83,80,79). So the water light is V0*G.a + G.rgb with a real, non-zero ground map inside M05's window (G ~0.18-0.20, a 0.78). The water weight is fresnel (frame alpha, 0.91) x 4*scene-copy alpha (0.66), and the composite output is fogged. Ground-map alpha: the swizzled-fetch value a 0.777 is the one the GPU used; a linear readback gives a 1.0 and is off by 2-3 levels. The ground light T2 modulates only the reflection term (s3), not the refraction/tint term.
facts.how_to_use: Editor water reference: implement exactly these stages; validate against M05 probe 200,350 = (83,80,79). The thickness = 4*T1.a, where T1.a is the half-res scene copy's alpha (~0.165 here).

facts.title: UC terrain (n738): out = 4*lerp(T2,T1,T0.a)*T0.rgb*L, L = V1.rgb*V1.a*T3.a + T3.rgb; then micro dst' = 2*src*dst
facts.fact: ucg_frame_trace_raw.txt line 831 (program n738, also KF's near terrain): out = 4*lerp(T2, T1, T0.a)*T0.rgb*L with L = V1.rgb*V1.a*T3.a + T3.rgb (T0 = mask/colour map, T1/T2 = the two layers, T3 = the ground light map). The micro draw then does dst' = 2*src*dst with src ~(0.67,0.65,0.58): (18,17,12) -> (24,22,14). The trace logs d0 only, so V1 (the light-colour term) is unmeasured. The s2 constant C0 varies per level: 7F7F7F7F (0.498) at UC, 4C4C4C4C (0.298) at KF (see kf-bare-terrain-match). Source: the level's MATerrain TerrainDetailBlend (UC 0.5, KF 0.3), per editor pass 11. Probe 320,420 detail (audit #3): program 08421, 7 stages; t0 128x256 fmt 0F (DXT5 colour map, alpha = layer mask), t1/t2 256x256 fmt 0C (detail layers), t3 512x512 fmt 06 (ground light map). The x4 is T0 applied x2 times the final-stage x2, with C0.a = 0x7F (~x1, = TerrainDetailBlend) on the lerp. Fog FFDED0B4 at 2.727/-0.001818 (clear to ~400 m), so unfogged at the probe. The trace holds no texel values, colour-map alpha or V1, so it cannot identify which editor input is ~2x too dark; whether the colour-map alpha is inverted is untested. A runtime per-stage probe print (pass 13) is pending, then one UC + one BD launch. Generalised by the KF stageprobe4 decode: out = 2*L*(4*C0.a)*T0*lerp(T2,T1;T0.a), so the 'x4' on UC is 2*(4*0.498); C0.a = TerrainDetailBlend scales the gain per level (see kf-bare-terrain-match).
facts.how_to_use: Editor terrain: use 4*lerp(layer2, layer1, mask.a)*mask.rgb*(V1*V1.a*G.a + G.rgb), then the micro pass as 2*src*dst. V1 is still unknown; it may come from the MAEnvironment light colour.

facts.title: KF bare terrain = the UC n738 program with s2 C0 = 4C4C4C4C; audit18 matched the game, but audit23 (terrain sun x2) is ~1.55x too bright
facts.fact: kfmove_frame_trace_raw.txt, probe 200,330, game human at (1024,1581). Line 1235 is the same 7-stage terrain program as UC (n 738), but with C0 = 4C4C4C4C (0.298) in s2 instead of UC's 7F7F7F7F. Fog colour FF1C195B, coefficients 5.75/-0.005. Pixel history: (18,12,9) after the terrain draw, unchanged to the end of the frame. No micro draw (blend 306/300 on a 256x256 texture) touches it; the frame's only 306/300 draw is a 4-vertex one at line 4635. Game ground mean (22.6,15.1,11.7) vs editor audit18 (24.3,16.0,12.6) at a matched cam: a match. Regression (audit #3, 2026-10-22): audit23 (809B3D68, terrain sun x2) over-brightens KF bare terrain ~1.55x at the same matched pose (KFmovecopy 1024,1581): game (22.5,15.1,11.7) vs editor (35.9,25.0,19.1), where audit18 was (24.3,16.0,12.6) PASS. The UC aligned crop stays ~0.93x. So the terrain light scale is level-dependent. CORRECTED (stageprobe4, audit #3, 2026-10-22; KFmovecopy pos 1008,1581, probe 200,330, draw 1401083): out = 2 * L * (4*C0.a) * T0.rgb * lerp(T2, T1; T0.a), with L = V1.rgb*V1.a*T3.a + T3.rgb. Values: V0 = (0,0,0, a 0.5); V1 = (0.3176,0.2588,0.1843, a 0.5597) (the sun term); T0 colour map (0.142,0.133,0.126, a 1); T1 (0.692,0.656,0.606); T2 (0.682,0.688,0.682); T3 swizzled (0.189,0.141,0.154, a 1) (linear 0.20,0.149,0.165). The decode (21.9,15.2,11.9) reproduces the pixel (23,15,11). So C0.a (TerrainDetailBlend) IS a per-level gain on the detail x colour-map product: 4*C0.a = 1.19 on KF vs 1.99 on UC (7F). The total gain is 2.38 on KF vs ~4 on UC (consistent with UC's traced x4). KF V1 (sun) = (0.318,0.259,0.184) x 0.56 is also smaller than UC's (0.482,0.443,0.349) x 0.703. Fog 1C195B 5.75/-0.005 clamps off (no fog) at 14 m. The editor light ratio 1:0.93:0.87 came from the N=13 debug pixel, which shows 0.5*L at ~4/255 per channel, i.e. 8-bit quantisation noise. Computed from the file colours, the editor's KF L is warm: ambient 2*file_amb*lm.r (lm.r 0.675) = (0.34,0.25,0.28), plus sun 2*file_sun*0.56*lm.a = (0.32,0.26,0.19), total 1:0.77:0.70, the same as the game's 1:0.78:0.70. The editor's file sun colour (0.318,0.259,0.184) equals the game's V1 exactly (x1). The colour-map hue comparison was a ground patch mean (editor) vs one texel (game), so it is not comparable; a single-texel editor read at the game's T0 world point was requested from audit #3. The M13b probe hit a non-terrain material draw (no T3).
facts.how_to_use: Editor terrain: out = 2*L*(4*TerrainDetailBlend)*colourmap*lerp(T2,T1;mask), L = V1*V1.a*G.a + G.rgb. Do not apply a global sun x2: the per-level gain (TerrainDetailBlend) and V1 already differ (KF gain 2.38, UC ~4).

facts.title: UC terrain micro detail: src = 0.5 + (M-0.5)*(1+t), t = 0.706 - 1.73*fade, fade ~ (0.0497 + 0.0189*depth)^2; blend 2*src*dst
facts.fact: Game draw 4638536 (ucsp7 trace; UC texel at world (252.8,580.5)). T0 and T1 are the SAME texture 809CA000 at the same tc (59.255,171.977), sampled value M = (0.7112,0.6832,0.604). T2 (mode 4) supplies a per-vertex fade value: 0.33473 at the pixel (vertices 0.196/0.437/0.288). The combiner output (rc_eval) (0.7355,0.7043,0.6159) fits src = M + t*(M-0.5) = lerp(M0, M0+M1-0.5, t), with t ~0.112 (possibly fade^2), to 4 digits on all three channels. The blend is 2*src*dst; the observed src (0.67,0.64,0.60) from dst (44,40,25) -> (59,51,30) is ~9% below rc_eval, unexplained (fog 80808080 with factor 1.68 is the suspect). The editor uses lerp(m0, 2*m0*m1, 0.5) (taken from KF), i.e. a product instead of ADD_SIGNED and a constant 0.5 instead of the distance fade: at M = 0.71 the editor gives 0.86 vs the game's 0.7355. This micro pass is the source of the UC 1.78x over-brightness at this texel. Confidence: formula medium-high; the fade t -> distance mapping low (needs more micro-draw pixels). 12-pixel table (audit #3, stageprobe4m): the micro draw has T0 = T1 = the same 256x256 DXT1 texture, T2 mode 4 = an interpolated per-vertex fade attribute, and stage 1 and 2 C0 = 0.502. rc_eval = M + t*(M-0.5) holds on all 12 pixels, with the same t in R, G and B. Observed t ~ 0.70 - 1.70*T2: t goes from +0.63 near to -0.31 at T2 0.587 far, so the detail contrast inverts with distance. That is consistent with pass 15's single point (0.70 - 1.70*0.335 = 0.13 vs t 0.112) and rules out t = T2^2. T2 grows with view depth: pos.w 4.2 -> 0.0099, 9.5 -> 0.057, 15.5 -> 0.098, 20.8 -> 0.196, 32 -> 0.437, 44 -> 0.775. The micro draw is the last writer on all 12 terrain pixels. This is an observation; the final fit is pass 15's. Pass 15 fit (medium confidence): src = lerp(M0, M0+M1-0.5, t) = 0.5 + (M-0.5)*(1+t) (T0 = T1, the same texture). t = 0.706 - 1.73*T2 (rms ~0.015 over the 6 pixels with |M-0.5| > 0.15). T2 (the per-vertex tex2 fade) ~ (0.0497 + 0.0189*viewdepth)^2 (vertex values: depth 4.2 -> 0.0099, 9.5 -> 0.057, 20.8 -> 0.196, 32.1 -> 0.437, 43.9 -> 0.775). So the contrast gain 1+t ~ 1.706 - 1.73*T2 (~1.7*(1-T2)): near terrain gets ~1.6-1.8x detail contrast, and beyond ~37 m the gain is below 1. Open: game after/(2*before) is 0.72-0.98x of 2*rc_eval on the 3 bright pixels; suspected cause: the probe uses the nearest-texel M while the GPU mip-filters. Built into editor audit27 (F7105AE7.2BAE), awaiting audit #3 regression on UC/KF/M02. VERIFIED in editor audit27 (F7105AE7.2BAE) by audit #3 (patch means, top-down at game points; medium-high confidence at the probe point). (1) UC 125,260: editor final patch (63,51,27) vs game pixel (59,51,30) = 1.06/1.00/0.91, a match. The earlier '1.34/1.25/1.17 red cast' compared the editor against a 25x25 game screen-crop mean (47,41,23) and is withdrawn. (2) Micro stage: game M mean over 36 pixels (0.647,0.602,0.518); the editor's N13 = N14 (same texture) mean is 0.96-0.98x; game effective micro ~= M within 4%, so the t(fade) formula holds on average. (3) Pre-micro editor vs game 'before' (single pixels): 125,260 1.01/0.99/1.05; 100,280 1.16/1.11/1.13; 380,240 1.14/1.04/1.14; 580,260 1.30/1.22/1.26. Channels are equal (no hue cast); the magnitude scatter is single pixel vs patch (strong light-map shadows); at 610,280 the patch is much darker than the game's lit pixel. (4) Fog on/off: patch means identical (UC fog starts ~150-175 m). (5) KF texel unchanged (21,14,11) vs game (23,15,11). Remaining: far-pixel excess (580,260 and 380,240: 1.35-1.5x in R) sits in the pre-micro light term at those world points; unexplained, low priority. Regression (audit #3): audit27 is bit-identical to audit26 on KF (matched pose yaw 0/180, KF start, KF near ground), M02 start and NRC start (zero pixel diff). Only UC changes (top-down 252.8,580.5 at D28: mean (69.2,57.4,30.3) -> (67.4,56.0,29.3)), so the change is confined to the UC micro pass.
facts.how_to_use: Editor: fade = (0.0497 + 0.0189*viewdepth)^2 per vertex; t = 0.706 - 1.73*fade; src = 0.5 + (M-0.5)*(1+t) with M the mip-filtered micro texel; out = dst*2*src. In audit27, pending verification.

facts.title: Water thickness alpha (T1.a): BD composite 0.2439 (stageprobe5) with 5.67 m view depth surface->bed; hypothesis T1.a ~ vertical water depth / ~4 m. The earlier BD 0.098/0.089 reads are RETIRED
facts.fact: stageprobe4 samples for fitting the water thickness LUT (T1.a is the 320x240 scene copy's alpha; the composite uses 4*T1.a as the thickness weight). BD near px 320,300: frame 1 T1.a 0.0984 at fog coordinate (eye distance) 9.60 m, T2.a 0.882, out (25,28,21); frame 2 T1.a 0.0894 at 13.85 m, T2.a 0.955, out (16,17,11). M05 px 200,350: T1.a 0.1651, T2.a 0.777, oFog 0.242 (normalised; factor 0.758 with coefficients 2/-1), out (83,80,79). The traces hold no eye pose. The water-draw vertex constants c[114]/c[115] are identical across BD frames while the fog coordinate changes, so they are not the camera: BD c[114] = (0.0872,-0.0057,0.9962), c[115] = (154.09,-9.80,101.08); M05 c[114] = (-0.0697,-0.0079,0.9975), c[115] = (452.84,20.00,161.93). c[114] is a near-unit vector (probably a direction, e.g. a projection or wave axis) and c[115] a position/offset, possibly the water body's origin. Only 3 samples, so the depth -> alpha mapping is not yet fitted; T1.a falls slightly with eye distance at BD. Audit #3 (2026-10-22): the M05 sample is at eye distance ~50 m. It is not eye distance alone, since the BD slope is tiny while M05 at 50 m is higher; it probably depends on water depth below the surface (e.g. scene depth minus water depth) rather than view distance (inferred). RETIRED/SUPERSEDED (audit #3, stageprobe5, BDm2copy probe 320,300, both frames identical): the BD T1.a reads 0.098/0.089 were stale or wrong, and the 'T1.a falls with eye distance' conclusion is dead. Water is two draws. The SURFACE draw writes depth (zpre F32737 = the terrain bed -> zpost EDC76E; colour 3F192715). The COMPOSITE draw (T0 = scene copy, T1 = the 320x240 thickness texture, T2 = ground map) only depth-tests (EDC76E before and after). The depth buffer is z24 = a - b/w (a = 16795917, b = 16797870; near 1.0, far ~898). w(surface) = 13.850, equal to the fog coordinate; w(bed) = 19.518. So there are 5.67 m of view depth between the surface and the bed (high confidence). Composite T1.a = 0.2439 (swizzled and linear agree). Hypothesis (medium): T1.a ~ vertical water depth / ~4 m, consistent with the editor's depth/4 (0.224 for a ~0.9 m bed). The M05 0.165 (stageprobe4, decode reproduced within 1 level) stands. Pass 15 (confidence: the depth/w data high; the vertical-vs-slant conclusion medium, FOV assumed): game thickness alpha ~ vertical depth/4 with no view divisor. The editor's old slant (along-view-ray)/4 formula saturated; editor audit28 (82563E00.271EBE) now uses a = sat(vertical/4). Open: verify M05 (0.165 at ~50 m) and run the M02/IYF regressions on audit28. CAUTION (audit #3 re-decode): the BD pixel is reproduced only with an effective T1.a ~0.115, not the probed 0.2439, so the 0.2439 reading and the 'vertical depth/4' hypothesis it supports are in doubt. Editor audit28's sat(vertical/4) is built on 0.2439 and may need ~half that at BD. facts.title: The 512x512 ground light map is a camera-placed window, ~2 km at ~4 m/px
facts.fact: No Man's Land trace (light quads on surface 00C18000): only 8 of the level's 28 MAPointLights were splatted, the rest culled outside the window. Fitting the two R=200 quads to their lights gives px = X/4.07 + ~32, py = ~601 - Z/4.07 (Z flipped), so that frame's window was X -130.1954, Z 362.2446: about 2083 m square at about 4.07 m/px, placed by the camera frustum (camera near 350,1090 looking +Z), not centred. Quad size per light = 2*LightMapRadius / (m per px). That run used DrawDistance 100; the window size probably follows the far plane (pc_draw_distance.c ma2_pc_lightmap_parameters / ma2_pc_lightmap_extent), so the m/px scale depends on the setting (inferred from the code names). BD evidence (2026-10-22, stageprobe3): at the start pose, both the terrain and the water at screen 320,300 sample the window at uv ~(0.01,0.05), within 0.05 of the corner, and read 0. This suggests the near camera area lies at the window's edge (frustum-placed) with zero border texels (inferred; UNCONFIRMED, possibly a per-frame edge artifact; audit #3 is probing near/far pixels on two frames). Editor note (pass 15, 2026-10-22): the editor samples a full-map baked light map by world position (CLAMP), not the per-frame camera window, so window-edge effects in the game have no editor counterpart. UPDATE 2026-10-24: see ground-map-window-function.

facts.title: KF VTOL pad slab: V0 = 0, so all its light is the ground pre-pass FB; the '0.68x' is a spatial average, not a constant
facts.fact: KF VTOL pad slab (material_detail, level 0.5): V0 (d0) is (0,0,0) in the material draw, so all its light is the pre-pass FB = (NdotL*G.a*C0 + G.rgb)*V1. Probe: before the slab (22,15,11), after the pre-pass (97,75,68), after the material (104,85,75), which is the final pixel. This is the 3rd static whose light is FB only, with no vertex light. The editor's 0.68x gap is a spatial average (game slab p5.p75 = 34.103), not a constant factor. M13b's spire is COMPLEX with detail, and audit10's extra lerp had no visible effect on it. So for pre-passed material_detail statics, light = V0 + FB reduces to FB only (the pre-pass ground light), not just on the slab. The other depth-EQUAL textured draws (prog 00001: 1 on KF, 19 on M05 m05w, 5 on IYF iyfg) do carry V0 > 0, but they are a different single-stage program. The UC ucg trace has no such draws. Confidence medium (one KF frame; 08021 draws only in KF).
facts.how_to_use: Editor: for statics that take the pre-pass (material_detail, prog 08021), use V0 = 0 and light = the pre-pass FB (NdotL*G.a*C0 + G.rgb)*V1. Applies to walls too (all 6 KF 08021 draws), medium confidence.

facts.title: Near static models get an untextured ground-lightmap pre-pass; material pass adds it as light
facts.fact: Near static models (roads, buildings; not 'Mechs) draw an untextured pre-pass first (tex modes PASSTHRU / DOT_PRODUCT / DOT_ST, t3 = the 512x512 ground light map). It writes FB.rgb = (max(N.L,0) * G.a * DirectionalLightColor (C0 = 424E3F34 in Mission_02) + G.rgb) * V1 and FB.a = 2 * lookup.b * C0.a. The material pass then draws with depth EQUAL and t3 = that framebuffer copy, using light = V0 + FB.rgb, and specular uses FB.a. So static models receive the ground map's sun-shadow mask, ambient and lamp pools. Traces: Mission_02 lines 1746, 2681, 2460; GoCommando 3508, 3774 (per-level counts in R2-13). Which meshes get it: objects with ShadowReceiverType 1 (see ground-prepass-is-shadow-receiver, 2026-10-22). the pre-pass is a MaterialLight per-light pass (base class sub_00074B20, \Renderer\MaterialLight\ strings); five light-pass instance classes (ctors sub_00060480, 00060740, 00060960, 00060C80, 00060FC0; PS defs 0x4A3430-0x4A3CA0, texmodes [4/1, DOT_PRODUCT, DOT_ST, t3]). The traced one is most likely class 0x45F8E0 (prepare sub_00060A60 sets colour mask 01010101, draw sub_00060B20). Mesh dispatch: sub_000547F0 by material shading bits (mat flags bits 3-5;mat shading = none/flat/gouraud/translucent/material_only, parsed sub_0006B030) and global pass mode [0x50C720]; model attribute max_normal_mapped_lights (sub_000892B0, +0xA8) caps lights per model. No distance or class (building vs 'Mech) test found; best inference: material shading/render group + per-model light cap select it (low-medium confidence). Next: trace callers of sub_00060B20.
facts.how_to_use: Editor: light static models as V0 + (sun*N.L*lightmap.A + lightmap.L*ambient + pools) sampled at the model's ground position.

facts.title: Ground light-map pre-pass = objects with ShadowReceiverType 1 (roads, building bases, pads)
facts.fact: The untextured ground-light-map pre-pass (prog 0A624, t3 = 512x512 fmt 06 ground map; the material pass then uses z EQUAL with the 640x480 FB copy as t3 and prog bit 0x8000 set: 08C21/08021/08001) is drawn for objects whose ShadowReceiverType (key 7A647510) is 1. Evidence: (a) Retail placements: ShadowReceiverType 1 is on every MARoad (966/966) and MAWater (66/66), and on MACorporeal objects using ground-slab models only: Bb_34x34_Generic01/03/04, Bb_34x34_OfficeG, Bb_100x100_Airbase, BD_64x64_military02, Bd_64x64_military03, base60x30_gray, base60x60_gray, Env_ManHoleCover. The flag is consistent per model across all 22 missions; no model is a receiver in one placement and not in another. Buildings, Sets, Vehicles, Ramps, NULL and all other Environment models are 0. (b) Traces: pre-passes appear in Mission_01b (45), 02 (51), 03 (2), 04 (7), 16 (236), 17a (8) and 17b (37), which are exactly the missions with MACorporeal/MARoad receivers. Missions with only water receivers (05, 06a/b, 07, 11a, 14) show none. 12 and 13b have a few receivers but none on screen in the traced frames (the 13b spire and crystal are non-receivers, matching their missing pre-pass). Pre-passed textures per frame are few (1-8); the 256x128/256x512 08C21 pairs that recur in GC, M02, M16, 01b, M04 and RushHour are most likely building-base slabs. KF's only pre-passed mesh is the VTOL pad slab (material_detail 08021), a base pad. ShadowReceiverType 2 (MAMech 25, MAPerson 96, MASpider 3) gives no pre-pass ('Mech COMPLEX draws are V0 only); it is probably the projected blob/shadow receiver. Not code-traced: the read path from the entity field to the mesh lighting field (mesh+0x20 bits 3-5; sub_000547F0 branches on value 1 and the global pass mode [0x50C720] 0/2/4/5 -> sub_00055150/56480/54CF0/55AC0|55640) is unconfirmed. The .mat shading keyword sets bits 0-2: none 1, flat 2, gouraud 3, material_only 5, translucent 6 (sub_0006B030). The MP worlds were not checked (not in missions.json), but KF's pad fits.
facts.how_to_use: Editor: gate pass A (FB = (N.L*G.a*sun + G.rgb)*V1, with material light = V0 + FB) on the placed object's ShadowReceiverType == 1, for all of that object's meshes and facings. Everything else (buildings, walls, spires, crystals, props, vehicles, 'Mechs, glass) keeps vertex light only. This is narrower than audit29/30, which light all near opaque/cutout/blended parts. Implemented in editor audit31 (4C191C9F): pass A gated on the placement's ShadowReceiverType == 1, with MARoad always treated as a receiver. It awaits audit #3's matched-pair check. Audit #3 check: M02 Office19 wall + slab pair on audit31 is a qualitative PASS (no wall artefact).

facts.title: Stage probe builds: stageprobe2/3 (render-target reads stale), stageprobe4 B1AE4060 (GPU readback, validated), stageprobe4m (multi-pixel list)
facts.fact: Known caveats: ground-map edge-texel alpha reads are unreliable; the probe's own T0 read is post-draw (use the pre-draw pixel history). stageprobe5 (built from the stageprobe4m source; built and strings verified in the exe, but never run, so the output layout is unverified until the BD launch): with RECOMP_FRAME_TRACE=2 + RECOMP_FRAME_TRACE_PIXEL + RECOMP_FRAME_TRACE_DEPTH, each draw prints '[FTRACE] depth-pre x,y=raw va draw' before raster_batch (the existing '[FTRACE] depth x,y=' line is the after-draw value). It also prints the viewport scale/offset c58/c59 and the vertex-shader constants c0.c7 per draw. Depth is raw R16 or R24G8, from nv2a_gpu_debug_depth. Purpose: water depth below the surface for the thickness mapping. stageprobe5 RUN on BD (audit #3): output works. Correction: c58 = the unit camera forward vector and c59 = the eye position (not viewport scale/offset); e.g. BD eye (712.92,-20.00,1372.21), forward (0.4522,-0.0887,-0.8875). Built for R2-13 #7 (UC terrain shade, see uc-ground-map-is-retail-lightmap); untested until audit #3 runs it.

facts.title: UC ground map content = the retail A8L8 light map; the shade gap is a PC-port swizzle bug, not the sun term
facts.fact: Audit #3 (2026-10-22), UnderCover: the game's 512x512 ground-map texture (T3) is the retail baked A8L8 light map (128x256 texels covering 1024x2048 m), written at 1 texel per window pixel with wrap. It is tinted by C0 = LightAmbientColor (FF313326), plus 11 tiny additive blobs (lamp pools; their alpha is not written). The editor's light map equals the retail one (same stats), so the map is not the cause of the UC shade gap. The gap: game shaded ground 2-16 vs editor 30-50, while lit patches match at 0.95-1.25x. Leading explanation (inferred): the game's sun term V1.rgb*V1.a (vertex specular output, not captured in the trace) is ~0 in shade, while the editor uses per-pixel N.L*lm.a there. Open: the actual V1 value in shaded areas; it needs d1 (the specular vertex colour) added to the frame trace. SUPERSEDED (audit #3, stageprobe6): V1 at the dark UC pixel is (0.482,0.443,0.349,0.703), the same as at a lit texel, so the sun term is NOT ~0. The real cause is the runtime ground-map swizzle bug (see rt-swizzle-ground-map-bug): the game samples the 512x512 fmt-06 (swizzled) ground map from a render target that the PC runtime wrote LINEAR, so every fetch is Morton-scrambled. The combiner with the scrambled T3 reproduces the traced pixel (24,22,15) exactly; a correct linear readback would give ~50. The editor's smooth retail light map is the intended look.
facts.how_to_use: Editor: no change; keep the smooth retail light map. Do NOT chase the darker shaded ground seen in the PC port; it is the runtime bug.

facts.title: Model vertex light V0 = matDiffuse x (ambient + max(N.L,0) x sun), with per-vertex normals normalised in the shader (M15 facade and vents explained)
facts.fact: SOLVED v103. The lit model programs (hashes 037fde9c, 4bb785f4) compute, per vertex: Nw = normalize(n.x*c4 + n.y*c5 + n.z*c6) (n = vertex input v1; the world matrix rows are c4-c6; dp3 + rsq normalise in the shader); V0.rgb = c15.rgb * (c12.rgb + max(dot(Nw, -c13), 0) * c14.rgb); V0.a = c15.a. Constants are NV2A c[i] (D3D c(i-96)). c12 = LightAmbientColor (0.106,0.078,0.086); c13 = MAEnvironment DirectionalLightDirection (-0.317,-0.560,0.766), so the light vector is -dir; c14 = DirectionalLightColor (0.392,0.318,0.235). c12/c13/c14 are IDENTICAL in every draw of the frame. Only c15 changes: it is the per-material diffuse colour + alpha (e.g. 1,1,1; 0.647,0.608,0.529; 0.702 grey; facade 0.263,0.267,0.275). There is NO per-instance sun scalar, shadow, occlusion or vertex colour. FACADE: draw 4792724 has c15 = (0.263,0.267,0.275), so V0 = 0.26 x ambient where N.L <= 0. A lit vertex reproduces exactly: n (0,-0.149,0.988) -> Nw (0.608,-0.149,-0.778), N.L 0.706 -> d0 0.1006 (game 0.100618). VENTS (16 Env_WallVent instances, grill 140-vert and sideduct 60-vert parts, matched to draws by world position): c15 = white; per vertex, k = (V0.r - amb.r)/sun.r equals max(Nw.L,0) with max error 0.0000 on every vertex of all 32 draws. Per-instance mean k is 0.19-0.30 for both parts, with every instance lit somewhere. The k=0.74 vs k=0 contrast was a per-PIXEL/per-vertex sample of differently-facing smoothed normals, not a per-instance factor. NOTE: the stored mesh normals are NOT unit length (vent normals have length 0.121); the shader renormalises them. An editor that uses the raw normals, or face normals, will get the sun term wrong. Earlier hypotheses (light-map alpha, point lights, ShadowDiffuseFactor, occlusion ray) are all moot.
facts.how_to_use: Editor rule: per vertex, V0 = matDiffuse.rgb * (LightAmbientColor + max(dot(normalize(R * n_vertex), -DirectionalLightDirection), 0) * DirectionalLightColor), alpha = matDiffuse.a. R = the instance rotation (heading + the editor's existing z-flip convention, which matches the game's c4-c6). n_vertex = the mesh's own per-vertex normal, NORMALISED (raw lengths are ~0.12), interpolated across the triangle. matDiffuse = the material's diffuse colour (c15): facade 0.263,0.267,0.275; many materials are white. Check that the editor's .mat diffuse parse matches these c15 values. Tools: (program + constants), vshtab.py (per-draw c7/c12-c15 table), ventk.py (per-vertex k vs N.L check). Dump:

facts.title: PC-port bug: the 512x512 swizzled ground-map render target was written row-major and the scrambled map reached the screen; fixed in rtswz1/rtswz2
facts.fact: The bug is in nv2a_gpu_d3d11.c: target_for (creates a D3D11 target from guest RAM) and readback_target (writes it back) ignore the type bits and copy row-major. BUT the on-screen terrain/pre-pass/water draw samples T3 from the LIVE D3D11 target (texture_view RT alias -> rt->srv), which holds the image linearly and is sampled correctly; two UC runs logged no guest-memory sampling of that VA and no target discards. The stage probe reads T3 by nv2a_gpu_readback (nv2a_pb_exec.c:2366) then a swizzled fetch from guest RAM, so with the fix off its T3 values are scrambled BY CONSTRUCTION. So the earlier 'every fetch is Morton-scrambled' claim is proven only for the probe/guest-memory path; whether any visible shading is affected is OPEN. Fix exists behind RECOMP_RT_SWIZZLE_FIX=1 in test exe rtswz1 (2 rtswz1.exe, ecf4b54b.); RECOMP_RT_SWIZZLE_TRACE=1 logs [RT-SWZ] lines. Earlier (v94) evidence: audit #3 matched swizzle(3,506) -> linear (141,341) against the retail light map, and reproduced the traced dark pixel (24,22,15) with the scrambled fetch. Scope: this 512x512 fmt 06 target is the only swizzled RT used as a texture; fmt 12 frame copies and the 256x256 fmt 17 target are linear. UPDATE v101 (editor pass 18, medium confidence): rtswz2 (6FEAAEA6, fix ON by default) was swept over 10 levels plus the pause menu. No regressions were seen (HUD, menus, reflections/water, glass, indoor M04 unchanged). Light-mapped levels get visibly BRIGHTER ground: mean UC 44.8 vs 34.3, M16 63.9 vs 31.4, OF 72.2 vs 64.8; the exception is IYF, 32.4 vs 37.1 (darker). Not a pixel-exact A/B, because the scenes are dynamic. Treat the on-screen effect as likely, pending a matched-pose A/B. VERIFIED v102: rtswz1 FIX=0 vs FIX=1 at the s21 UC pose (within a few m). Ground lower-third mean went 21 -> 34 (1.6x). FIX=0 is a dark scrambled patchwork; FIX=1 is smooth and golden, like the editor. The probe's T3 alpha went from 0.37 (scrambled) to 0.9468 (linear, ~1.0). KF is 1.18x brighter, which closes its residual. IYF and M15 are unchanged in matched pairs (IYF means 36.9/35.7/41.6 vs 35.2/34.1/39.8), so the sweep's 'IYF darker' reading was pose noise. So the scrambled ground map DID reach the screen: VERIFIED IN GAME. The composite inputs are identical: V0 (0.0732,0.0613,0.0429,a .5), T0 (0.0745,0.0863,0.0667), T1 (0.0157,0.0268,0.0154,a 0.0898). Only the probe's own T2 (80C18000) read differs: a 0.314 rgb (0.150,0.177,0.141) with the fix (correct) vs a 1.000 (scrambled) without. So the on-screen effect is LEVEL-DEPENDENT. On UC/KF the target is seeded from guest memory (real effect, verified). On BD the target is fully GPU-redrawn, never seeded, so there is no on-screen effect. This corrects v95: 'screen samples the live RT, no on-screen effect' holds for BD, not for UC/KF. Pitfall: BDm2copy TeamDestruction spawns vary over an ~8 m grid, and the 320,300 pixel ranges 27.52 between launches, so compare only matched eyes.
facts.how_to_use: Editor: no change; its smooth ground light already matches FIX=1. Re-grade the earlier ground-map oddities measured with FIX=0, since they are likely this bug: 'ground-map edge alpha unreliable', 'alpha 0.777 swizzled', audit19-bd-water H3 and the BD pose-dependent ratio, the UC 9% micro gap, and the bright-pixel 0.72-0.98x gap. Pending: the BD water re-probe with stageprobe + fix. Probe T2/T3 numbers taken WITHOUT the fix are suspect until re-taken with stageprobe7 (298f7e0d.): M05 ground-map a 0.777, the BD T2 decodes, and the UC micro 9% via T3. The BD water editor gap is NOT this bug.
