facts.title: RadialFalloffLookup 64x64 = 255*(1-r^2)^2
facts.fact: sub_00052E60 (recomp_0008.c:27098) creates a single-level 64x64 texture registered as \Renderer\LightMapMgr\RadialFalloffLookup (fallback .32Bit), returns a 0x18-byte wrapper (vtable 0x45EC2C, D3D texture at +0x14). sub_00053DB0 (28731; formula 0x53EC8-0x53F43) fills texel=int(255*(1-r^2)^2+0.5), dx=2x/(W-1)-1, dy=2y/(H-1)-1, r^2=dx^2+dy^2, 255 at r^2<=0, 0 at r^2>=1: quartic falloff inside the inscribed disc, not smoothstep (0x493AF0=255.0, 0x493A5C=0.5, 0x493A60=1.0). Created via sub_00035E60 (vtable 0x45C8A0 slot 0) -> sub_000398C0, cached in [0x524AC0]; 0x52F50 and 0x540B0 clear it. That it is the texture 80679000 in traces is inferred. Likely use: ground light-map point-light splat (MAPointLight LightMap=1 adds a disc to the 512x512 map); sub_00037F60 (slot 61) reads [0x524AC0] and is the only caller of sub_00053C00 (LightMapCombined) (inferred). Spot cones use analytic sub_0006EA10. MaterialLight (sub_00074B20) and MaterialRadialBlur (sub_00062480) RadialFalloffLookup tables are different plateau curves. Supersedes t15 curve still to be measured. Open: which reader binds [wrapper+0x14] (0x37F80-0x37FB0, 0x38E60), swizzled store after 0x53F80.
facts.how_to_use: Editor: ground splat intensity = (1-r^2)^2 over the light radius.

facts.title: node_light mtb parser field offsets
facts.fact: Parser sub_0008B4E0 stores min_height->+0xD8, max_height->+0xDC, min_radius->+0xE0, max_radius->+0xE4, min_color->+0xE8, max_color->+0xEC (lea 0x8B512, 0x8B57C, 0x8B5DB, 0x8B63E, 0x8B68E, 0x8B6C6; strings 0x462A58 min_color, 0x462A4C max_color). Colour text parsed by sub_00263910 (%i, %i, %i); +0xE8/+0xEC are 4 bytes apart so each is a packed dword. Readers sub_0006D6E0 (compares, 0x6D7EF-0x6D802), sub_0006DC20 (early exit when max(0,B.(P-L)-param2)>=[+0xE4] or [+0xEC], 0x6DCD9-0x6DCE2), sub_0006E450 (pushes, 0x6E57B) read them as floats, conflicting with packed colour: possibly a different struct sharing offsets. No lightmap scale/bias use confirmed. Meaning unresolved.

facts.title: Spot axis sign is unresolved
facts.fact: Cone test sub_0006EA10 lights a point when D*[+0x90]+[+0x94] >= 0, D=dot(B,P-L)/param2 clamped to 1, B=light+0x28, L=light+0x14 (0x6EA91-0x6EA9C, 0x6EAF3-0x6EB11, 0x6EB2E-0x6EB36). If [+0x90]>0 the cone is centred on +B, contradicting spot-axis-sign (-dir); the sign of [+0x90] (written by sub_0006D920 and sub_0006E860) decides it. sub_0024F4A0 returns obj+4/obj+0x10 when flag 0x400 set, else rows 2/1 of the 4x4 at light+0x24+0x1C, rebuilt by sub_0024F570 from identity (0x2), Euler (0x200) or look-at (0x400); no inverse. sub_00038D50 is a vec3 equality predicate (tail-calls sub_00035B90), NOT a matrix builder (retracts the earlier caller-overwrites claim). SetAngles sub_0006E920 (vtable 0x461158) writes +0xD8/+0xDC=min/max(a,b), falloff factors +0x80/+0x84 and [+0x94]=cot(outer); cone test is under vtable 0x461180, shared struct unproven. Open: decode sub_0006E860/sub_0006D920 for the [+0x90] sign; in-game dump via sub_0006EDB0 (light+0x14, +0x60, +0x80, +0xC0). UPDATE 2026-10-24: sign resolved positive in spot-cone-scale-positive (cone on +B). UPDATE 2026-10-24: confirmed +Z by spot-axis-is-plus-z; sub_0008B4E0 is the lightmap child parser.
facts.how_to_use: Treat spot-light-axis and spot-axis-sign as unresolved until the in-game check.

facts.title: Culture per-texel seed
facts.fact: Per-texel placer 0x001801F6 re-seeds the MT19937 state at gen+0x1D4 for every texel with s=(texX<<16)^gen[+0x2C]^texZ (shl 0x180256, xor [esi+0x2C] 0x180259, xor [edi+4] 0x180265, call 0x1DA00 at 0x18026B); s==0 becomes 0x1105. Before seeding, L=0x0018045F(gen, texel world point); L==0 exits the texel. Writer of gen+0x2C still unknown (no store in ctor 0x17ED88, base ctor 0xC3545 or any MACultureGenerator-owned function; factory 0x17ED64 reached via descriptor 0x4B2D40); UID is a guess. UPDATE 2026-10-24: gen+0x2C is not a parsed property (culture-gen-2c-unparsed).

facts.title: Culture count and per-instance draw order
facts.fact: Per texel f=gen[+0xD0]*(gen[+0x7C]*L)*1e-6 (K 0x4541EC); D0=rand(0,1); count=floor(f)+(frac(f)>D0); capped at 1 if gen[+0x82] (SnapToGrid). Per instance: (a) if gen[+0x82]==0 x-jitter then z-jitter rand(0.001,0.999) (0x493AC4=0.001, 0x493AC8=0.999) else no draws and position=texel+0.001; (b) reject if 0x001804C3 or sub_00180518 true (no draws); (c) if gen[+0x81] yaw=rand(0,max); (d) scale=1.0+rand(-gen[+0x84],gen[+0x84]); (e) 0x001805FE places the instance (no direct RNG). Rejected instances skip (c) and (d), so the stream after a rejection depends on world state. Template pick drawing nothing is inferred. Confirms culture-seed-and-placement-order; jitter order x then z.

facts.title: Culture spacing test sub_00180518
facts.fact: sub_00180518 (only caller 0x1801F6, call 0x18037D) returns true if an active object lies within radius gen[+0x98] of the candidate position, and false at once when gen[+0x98]==0.0 (0x493A54). Walks a virtual spatial-query result, skipping objects whose +0x128 component fails 0xB3C50 or whose owner equals [0x4EAF44] or [0x4EB00C]. No direct RNG use (virtual target unresolved). +0x98 as min-spacing radius inferred. Open: gen+0x2C writer (runtime write watch), bodies of 0x18045F and 0x1804C3, yaw max constant.
facts.how_to_use: Editor: exact retail scatter needs gen+0x2C and world-state rejections; jitter range, scale formula and draw order are known.

facts.title: TypeOfCheck cases 1 and 2 are MoeEntityReference / MoeEntitySet gates
facts.fact: Class-id globals tested by update sub_001467B1: 0x4E4E84=MoeEntityReference, 0x4E4E88=MoeEntitySet (written by sub_0031F540/sub_0031F560 from descriptors 0x4A6660/0x4A6690). Case 1 (loc_00146986) reads [ebx+0xC] directly, requires its class to be MoeEntityReference, then resolves the referenced object via [obj+0x64] through hash-map find sub_000B4F70 (key ESI, container ECX, returns node+8 or 0). Case 2 (loc_00146862) uses RadiusSet (+0xDC) as map key and requires the result's class (+0x28) to be MoeEntitySet, then iterates members. So case 1 = a single referenced entity is in the radius; case 2 = members of an entity set are in the radius; case 3 = player (or any) entities in the area (names inferred).

facts.title: Template-name prefixes and faction codes are never parsed
facts.fact: No game function tests a template-name prefix (Env_/Veh_/Mech_/Bld_/Inf_) or faction code (_BK/_LD/_WW/_MD) against a literal. Mech_/Env_ strings that reach code are asset paths or keys: material parser 0x0004A830, HUD sprite format HUD_SS_Mech_Plyr%d.ggf (0x000C7AFB), particle loads Env_Mech_FootStep_01.mgparticle (0x000F716D) and Env_LeafScatter_Snowy.mgparticle (0x0010013B, 0x0010129B). _BK/_MD/Veh_/Bld_/Inf_ absent from ma2.xbe; _LD only in L2_LD_* cache-event names; _WW only in IOERR data. Negative search (inline compares checked as hex constants only). Prefixes and codes are naming conventions; team/behaviour come from properties. UPDATE 2026-10-24: _ST offset 0x4070CF not 0x4070E2; B3/B11 close (name-suffixes-not-parsed-b3-b11).

facts.title: Template-name suffixes _CP/_ST/_Vert/_QTR are never parsed
facts.fact: No game function tests suffixes _CP, _ST, _Vert or _QTR. ma2.xbe has no _QTR and no NUL-terminated _CP/_ST/_Vert; two _CP byte matches (0x3B1F74, 0x441838) are binary data; _ST of PS_TEXTUREMODES_DOT_ST (0x4070E2) is unreferenced. Five _vert hits are inside longer names: NULL_vertex_group (sub_0003FD40), D3DFMT_VERTEXDATA switch (sub_00043850/sub_00043998), [vertex info] parser (sub_00068DA0), gpc_vertex_node (sub_00258D20). Literal tests only; a char-by-char suffix check was not searched. Naming conventions only.

facts.title: MAActionMusic Execute fields
facts.fact: Slot 22 sub_0014D9CC (object size 0x7C). Music event (+0x68) is a 0-3 switch (0x14D9EE), not a bool: 0 play cue +0x64 (reaches 0x0BCD60, handle +0x74); 1 stop the track at UID +0x60 and clear current/fallback (0x14DB71, 0x14DBCC); 2 swap around that track and restore fallback as current (0x14DA2C, 0x14DAFE); 3 set current track intensity (0x14DABD). Intensity (+0x6C) is a mix level passed to 0x0BCA80 and copied to global 0x50C920. Set as fallback (+0x70, 0x14DD95) with a live handle makes this cue the fallback (globals 0x50C928/0x50C92C/0x50C930) and stops the old one. Is current track (+0x78) and Is fallback track (+0x79) are flags Execute writes. Globals: 0x50C91C current track id, 0x50C920 intensity, 0x50C924 cue, 0x50C92C fallback intensity, 0x50C930 fallback cue. Stop/play/swap labels inferred. Catalog: Music event bool at 72 -> enum 0-3 at +0x68; fallback-cue offset +0x7A would overflow the 0x7C object (it is global 0x50C930). Catalog code.offsets are runtime offsets here.

facts.title: MAActionSound Execute fields
facts.fact: Slot 22 sub_0014CB91 (object size 0x8C). Queue (+0x74, 0x14CBA4): 1 enqueue (0x14CE98; ordered by +0x88 via comparator 0x14CB21), 0 play now via 0x0BCDC0. Delay (+0x7C) used only on the queued path (copied to +0x84). Can be interrupted (+0x6C, 0x14CC8A): 1 gives the play handle slot &+0x64 and registers the sound (0x14CE32). Interrupts others (+0x6D, 0x14CC0F): 1 calls 0x14CCE3 (walks global list 0x50E5D4) before an immediate play. Source object (+0x70, 0x14CC33): if set, position from entity at UID +0x60 (class check vs [0x4EAF2C], position via 0x0DD8B9), else (0,0,0). Play when skipped (+0x6E): when 0 no play while game-singleton byte +0x42 is set (cinema flag, see game-singleton-0x42). Queue timeout (+0x78) is not read by Execute or the comparator. Callee meanings inferred. Open: names of 0x0BCDC0, 0x0BCD60, 0x0BCA80, 0x14CCE3; queue drain using Delay and Queue timeout. CORRECTION 2026-10-24: +0x84 is the delay countdown and +0x88 the enqueue time (maactionsound-queue-drain).

facts.title: PrecisionLookup is a linear 16-bit ramp
facts.fact: 1024x1 PrecisionLookup (0x50C734) is filled by sub_00056B60 (recomp_0008.c:37159), only caller creator sub_000541B0 (return 0x54528). texel[x]=low16(trunc(65535*x/(N-1))), N=1024 (create arg 0x400), trunc=_ftol (sub_0030A5C0), bytes high then low at a swizzled offset (lines 37327, 37348-37349); K 0x493CC0=65535.0. sub_00056960 fills only the Z2W pair (0x50C72C/0x50C730); sub_00055150 only reads 0x50C734 (0x553E9). Together with Z2WLookup0 it looks like a two-texture depth decode (inferred). Closes the PrecisionLookup open in water-z2w-lut.

facts.title: Spot cone scale [+0x90] is positive: cone is on +B
facts.fact: sub_0006E860 (store 0x6E8CA) and sub_0006D920 (0x6D98D) both write [+0x90]=1.0/max(arg1,arg2) (1.0 at 0x493A60), never [+0x94]; [+0xD0]=min(arg1,arg2) or 0.99*arg2 when equal (0x493CAC=0.99), [+0xD4]=max. They differ only in where the (min^2-max^2) reciprocal goes ([+0x74] in E860, [+0x80] in D920). So [+0x90]>0 for any normal spot, and the cone test (D*[+0x90]+[+0x94] >= 0) centres the cone on +B (light+0x28), not -B. Closes spot-axis-sign-reopened (sign), axis row still needs the in-game check.

facts.title: TypeOfCheck case 3 entity walks
facts.fact: Case 3 (cmp byte [ebx+0xF5] at 0x146837) calls sub_00146C8E when PlayerEntitesOnly==0, else sub_00146AED; both get the reference position and two counters. sub_00146C8E walks the global entity list from [0x533284] (next +0x2C, end [0x533288]); each entity passing the trigger gates (+0xE0, +0xE4, +0xF4, +0xF6, +0xF8, +0xFC and unit-type test sub_0019955F) has its distance (position via sub_000DD8B9, sub_0024EFE0) compared to radius float +0xD4: inside->1, outside->2; counts every tested entity (ebp-4) and those whose result equals trigger +0xF0. sub_00146AED walks the player-slot array (count=([0x50E284]-[0x50E280])>>2, element via sub_000C8E6A(i), skipped if sub_000C8DAE(i)==0), requires class MAPlayer ([+4]+0x28==[0x4EAED0]) and applies the same radius test. +0xF0 as inside/outside selector and sub_0024EFE0 as Euclidean length inferred.

facts.title: Mission_15 bump-like two-pass draw
facts.fact: In, lines 6061 and 6089 (same mesh n=2429, identical v0). Pass 1 (6061): t0 80E5D000 256x256 fmt 0C, t1 81901000 256x64 (stale, inherited from 6055), t2 80765000 64x64; blend off, 4 stages, LEQUAL with depth write, no fog. Pass 2 (6089): t0 80DC5000 256x256 fmt 0C, t1 80DD0000 256x256 fmt 0F, t2 80A27000 32x32 fmt 0F, t3 8035C000 640x480 fmt 12 (frame-buffer surface 0035C000); blend off, 8 stages, EQUAL no depth write, fog on. Final combiner and c[112.115] match. Full-screen quad at 6050 is not part of the pair. Interpretation (inferred): pass 1 = DOT_PRODUCT normal-map-like chain with SpecularPowerLookup on t2; pass 2 reads the frame buffer and adds lighting (EQUAL), a light-accumulation layer; its 32x32 t2 may be the cube map. Whether bump2.tif is pass 1 t0 is unresolved.

facts.title: Culture level read and slope reject
facts.fact: 0x0018045F returns the culture level ((texel&mask)>>shift)/(2^NBits-1) for the texel under world (x,z) (mapping 0x189E62, fetch 0x1899C6; info gen+4->+0x84, map gen+0xB4), or 0 if culture info is null or off-map. No height, slope or terrain-type test (y unused). 0x001804C3 is a slope reject: angle=[0x50F4F0]*acos(clamp(y,-1,1)) of (probably) the surface normal y; rejected if angle < [esi+0x8C] or > [esi+0x88]. [0x50F4F0] is 0 in the XBE image, set at run time (probably 180/pi: degrees guessed). Normal input inferred from the caller at 0x18036A.
facts.how_to_use: Editor: scatter rejected outside a per-type slope range (min +0x8C, max +0x88, probably degrees).

facts.title: EngageView serializer and owner conflict
facts.fact: Serializer 0x000E826B (slot 1 of vtable 0x467A64; slot 0 0x000E706E also cites the name) lists EngageView among 58 property names and passes &this+0x210 (lea 0xE9033, 0xE9069). re_index places 0x467A64 under MAProjectile via ctor chain 0x000E6A0E (writes +0x210 at 0xE6B1A); the catalog says MAMover. No reader found in MAProjectile (+0x210 used as a pointer at 0xD0913/0xD0EE0, probably a different class). Float readers adding EngageView sit in MAMech (0x1B42E5 at 0x1B56E5) and MATurret (0x1BAE7F at 0x1BB227). 39 of 127 +0x210 hits read. facts.title: sub_0004DB80 is the SPECULAR_MASK loader, not the draw path; no cubetexture reference
facts.fact: sub_0004DB80 is the SPECULAR_MASK material LOADER (vtable 0x45E710 slot 6, verified via lookup.py vt), not the draw path. The loader never references the cubetexture literal (readers: 0x4C350, 0x4CFE0, 0x4DFD0, 0x4E250 = other material classes), supporting the level-wide MAEnvironment EnvironmentMapName cube. facts.title: Spot cone axis = matrix +Z row, no negation
facts.fact: sub_0024F4A0 (light dir/pos refresh, 14 callers; recomp_0063.c:13592-13626): if flags (dword at struct+0) HI8 bit 4 (0x400) set it copies cached dir struct+4.+0xC and pos struct+0x10. else calls sub_0024F570 then copies struct+0x3C/+0x40/+0x44 = row 2 (Z row) of the row-major 4x4 at struct+0x1C into struct+4 with NO sign change. So the spot axis is the matrix +Z (node-matrix link inferred), supporting spot-cone-scale-positive and the t12 spot-light-axis (+Z). Writers: ctor sub_0006E450 writes flags 0x203 at light+0x24 and a float at +0x28; path 2 of sub_0024F4A0 stores flags=0x400 over the dword (clears 0x200); cone test sub_0006EA10 triggers the refresh with eax=ebx+0x24; SetMatrix sub_0006D5B0 (vtable 0x461158 slot 2) block-copies 28 or 92 bytes into this+0x14 (size by source flags bit 0); getter sub_0006D5F0 (this=light+0x10 inferred). CORRECTION: sub_0008B4E0 is the lightmap child parser (min/max_color/height/radius), caller sub_0008B290 = node_light element parser; writes +0xD4, +0xE0/+0xE4 - not the axis writer. Open: which matrix reaches SetMatrix for .mtb node lights; readers testing 0x200/0x400. RULING: the code facts describe the RENDER LIGHT's own orientation matrix (direction = row 2, cone centred on -dir) and stand as code. What is NOT proven is that this matrix is the .mtb node's world matrix: the SetMatrix (sub_0006D5B0) caller for node lights was never found. Model geometry plus a same-pose game frame show the beam follows the NODE's local -Y (node-light-spot-beam-direction-is-the-light-nodes-local-minus-y-not-plus-z-geometry-and-game-frame, runtime-observed HIGH). Both hold if the engine applies a basis change from node to light matrix. For editor authoring use node -Y. Editor caveat: it turns light directions by heading only (no pitch/roll; M01b searchlights are pitched 60).
facts.how_to_use: Editor: lamp pool/cone faces node +Z.

facts.title: MAAction Execute is vtable slot 22 = +0x58

The +0x60 clue came from MAModSubObjectShow (vtable 0x471C20, +0x60). recomp_0032.c 3700/3853 are in sub_0013F5D3 (no trigger fields); 7905/8022 in sub_00140D0A = MAModSubObjectCamShake (vtable 0x4720C0) slot 24. facts.title: EngageView +0x210 acts as a timestamp; vtable 0x467A64 is MAMover's
facts.fact: Vtable 0x467A64 is MAMover's (2-slot secondary vtable stored at obj+0x20 by MAMover init 0x0E6A0E, also 0x0E6C33); MAProjectile (own vtable 0x4680B8) inherits it via ctor calling that init (0x0EC0C1); the re_index in:MAProjectile label is a ctor-chain artifact. EngageView default +0x210 is set in the same init. Reader 0x1B5680-0x1B56F9 compares (+0x210 + 2.0) with clock T. Latch +0x209: if cl==0 and T > [+0xE0]+6.0 -> latch=1, +0xE0=T; if cl!=0 and T > [+0xE0]+3.0 -> latch=0, +0xE0=T; latch forced 0 while T < [+0x210]+2.0 (2 s hold-off). If latch set, vector [ebp+0x20.0x28] scaled by xmm3 (0x1B5700-0x1B572E): live code. So MAMech +0x210 is used as a TIMESTAMP (seconds), not a distance; the catalog label EngageView for +0x210 is suspect (writer unchecked). Open: writer of +0x210; cl/al sources; xmm3 and the ebp+0x20 vector.
facts.how_to_use: Do not use EngageView as an 80 m attack range.

facts.title: Fog is only ever D3DFOG_LINEAR; mode picks start/end source
facts.fact: sub_0003AEB0 reads fog mode from G+0x2438 (G=[0x524AD0], set by sub_000373D0 = fog vtable +0x124). Mode 0/other: state 0x5C=0 only. Modes 1-3: 0x5C=1, 0x8A=[G+0x243C], 0x5D=3, then 0x5E/0x5F = start/end (mode 1 from G+0x2440/+0x2444; modes 2/3 from stack args), each via sub_0003BA00. facts.title: MAActionSound queue drain and delay countdown
facts.fact: Queue drain = sub_0014C95A (MAActionSound vtable slot 7, Update), walking std:vector<handle> at 0x50E5D8/0x50E5DC: purges stale entries while skipping, destroys finished cues (slot 2 returns 0; 0x14CA0D-0x14CA39), drops expired entries (erase 0x14CA9B, never played), starts the head. CORRECTION to maactionsound-execute: +0x84 is the live delay COUNTDOWN (enqueue sub_0014CB91 copies DelayBeforePlay +0x7C into +0x84 at 0x14CBED) and +0x88 = game clock at enqueue (the name QueuedExpirationTime is misleading). Sort std:sort (0x14CE98) comparator 0x14CB21: started first, then higher PriorityLevel (+0x80), then earlier enqueue time. Units seconds: Update subtracts dt (double 0x4E2428) from +0x84 until 0; start needs +0x84==0; only Queue (+0x74) actions use Delay. Timeout (+0x78) helper 0x14CE0E = QueuedTime+timeout (timeout 0 -> clock+1.0, const 0x493A60); unstarted entry erased when now > QueuedTime+timeout+Delay; timeout 0 never expires. While game+0x42 is set Execute won't queue entries lacking Play-when-skipped (+0x6E) and the drain purges unstarted ones (0x14C9AA-0x14C9E4): +0x42 behaves as the cinematic-skip flag (inferred). Offsets: CueEvent 0x68, PlayWhenSkipped 0x6E, Source 0x70, Queue 0x74, Timeout 0x78, Delay 0x7C, Priority 0x80, countdown 0x84, enqueue time 0x88.

facts.title: MASpawner runtime offsets (use these)
facts.fact: Runtime offsets: +0x78 flags (bit 0x01 Enabled, 0x10 handshake), +0x7C MaxSpawners, +0x90 MaxActiveSpawners, +0x98 NumSpawned, +0x9C NumActive. maspawner-spawn-rules mixes serializer and runtime offsets; use these. Spawn tick sub_0013321F (slot 7): skips if Enabled clear (0x13322E) or 0x10 set (0x133244); if MaxSpawners != 0 and NumSpawned >= it (0x13324E-0x13325B); if MaxActiveSpawners != 0 and NumActive >= it (0x133261-0x133271). facts.title: DISPUTED: sub_0001BE20 may be allocator bookkeeping, not a spawner decrement
facts.fact: DISPUTED. Walker sub_0001BE20 (dec [esi+0x9C] at 0x1BEA1; bit 2 of ebx -> NumActive, bit 1 -> NumSpawned at 0x1BE96) is gated on global [0x50BA24], a mike tag at [obj], and obj inside [0x4D3950, 0x4E1150); with a parent it climbs +0xD4 and decrements the top's +0x98 AND +0x9C (both, not only +0x9C); parentless: only arg2 bits. Callers include sub_0001D250 (2229 callers, calls BE20 at entry) and sub_0001CF40 (1356 callers; free path, owner from [ptr-0x10]); the spawn creator reaches BE20 at spawn time via 0x1333CF -> 0xB4470 -> D250. Spawn creator sub_00133648 and its 27 direct + 31 second-level callees never write +0xD4 (6 indirect calls, slots 7/42/43, unresolved). the tag, fixed address-range check, [ptr-0x10] header and thousands of callers look like memory-allocator bookkeeping, so +0x98/+0x9C in BE20 may be allocator counters that merely share offsets with NumSpawned/NumActive; then spawner-numactive-decrement is WRONG and MaxActiveSpawners acts as a lifetime cap. In-game test: MaxActiveSpawners=1, kill the unit, watch respawn. Recount sub_00157CD0 zeroes/re-adds +0x98/+0x9C from children (class unknown).
facts.how_to_use: Do not rely on NumActive dropping when a spawned unit dies.

facts.title: Engine render-state ids are XDK D3DRS indices; fog is TABLE LINEAR
facts.fact: Flush sub_0003BC10 (only caller driver 0x3B2F0 at 0x3B313) pops the 0x870 dirty list (node=id+1; 12-byte records +0 requested, +4 last flushed, +8 pending) and dispatches by id: id < 0x5C -> descriptor table 0x45B0E0 into thunk 0x40CF80; 0x5C.0x87 -> OR mask from 0x45AEC0 into dirty word 0x41BC70 and cache value at 0x41BC78+id*4; id >= 0x88 -> stdcall handler from table 0x4181A0. 0x40xxxx-0x41xxxx is the statically linked XDK D3D library; the layout is the XDK render-state layout (simple states first, deferred states starting at D3DRS_FOGENABLE cached in D3D__RenderState with dirty bits, complex states with handlers), so ids are Xbox XDK D3DRS indices: 0x5C FOGENABLE, 0x5D FOGTABLEMODE (=3 LINEAR), 0x5E FOGSTART, 0x5F FOGEND, 0x8A FOGCOLOR: TABLE fog, LINEAR (strong inference). Consumer 0x410150 reads the four fog values (dirty bit 0x2000 shared by 0x5C-0x5F): enable 0 exits; mode 0 -> start=end=1.0 and 0x2601; mode 3 -> linear path (reciprocal of end-start); also ids 0x60/0x61. 0x8A handler 0x40C600 writes NV2A push-buffer method 0x2A8 (count 1) with the colour's bytes 0/2 swapped (ARGB->ABGR), raw value to 0x41BEA0. Closes the id->D3DRS map open in fog-only-linear. UPDATE 2026-10-24: keys 0x5C-0x5F are not D3D8 RS numbers (fog-helpers-emit-nv2a).

facts.title: MAMover-family +0x210 is a runtime timestamp; catalog EngageView entry contradicted
facts.fact: MAMover init 0x0E6A0E stores 0.0 at 0x0E6B1A (not 80.0); MAMover copy (vtable 0x467A70 slot 16, 0x0E938F) copies it at 0x0E93F3; MAMech 0x1B3D93 stores 0.0 (0x1B400F) or the clock when predicate 0x186566 returns nonzero (0x1B4044-0x1B404A); MAMech 0x1B42E5 stores the clock at 0x1B4D70 (gated by [ebx+0x12C]==1) and pairs it with +0xE4 = clock, then clock+7.0 (const 0x493D64). Reader 0x1B56E5 = 2 s hold-off (see engageview-owner-and-label). Other classes use the slot differently: MAFlyer stores ints 0/1/3 (0x1BF134, 0x1C00D9); MAProjectile serializer 0x0E826B writes three bytes at lea [ebx+0x210] (0x0E9069-0x0E9075). CATALOG FIX: key 3C00F3DB EngageView (owner MAMover, offset 528=0x210, write 0x0E7415, read 0x0E85BC): 0x0E7415 is the EngageView string push inside MAProjectile(+sub)#0 0x0E706E, not a store; no store of a parsed 80.0 to +0x210 exists. EngageView's real storage is unknown; mark the offset/label contradicted.

facts.title: gen+0x2C is not a parsed property
facts.fact: gen+0x2C (MACultureGenerator) is NOT a parsed property (16-property slice has nothing at slice 0x0C). Only per-cell read: xor edx,[esi+0x2C] at 0x180259 in fn 0x1801F6 (the wiki credits the reseed to sub_0001DA00: doubtful). Candidate writer 0x183B9D (stores 0/1/2 at +0x2C via helpers) is also called from 0x186566 (the MAMech predicate) and many 0x1Bxxxx MAMech sites, so it is probably not culture-specific (unproven). If gen+0x2C is never written it stays at its ctor value and the per-cell seed depends only on cell coordinates (inferred). Store at 0x18068C (fn 0x18063B Generated Entity) writes the NEW INSTANCE's +0x2C, not the generator. sub_00180518 neighbour-conflict test: returns 1 on the first object within radius [this+0x98] (spatial query vtbl+0x14) whose vtbl+0x34 flag is set, predicate 0x0B3C50 holds on obj+0x128, and obj+0x28 is neither [0x4EAF44] nor [0x4EB00C]; 0 if radius equals const 0x493A54 or [scene+0x1C] null.

facts.title: MissionVariable table semantics
facts.fact: 0x4EB9E0 = flat array of 30 one-byte flags (ids 0.29), bounds-checked against 0x1E everywhere; -1 = unset. Writers: MAActionMissionVariableSet Execute sub_001A94A1 (vtable 0x47CEE8 slot 22): flags[this+0x64] = byte this+0x68 (VariableState), accepts 0.29; save-restore sub_000F235C (MARoot anon vtable 0x46878C slot 1) restores as (value != 0); sub_0016990A (sole caller sub_00016880) unknown role; save side sub_000F175D reads only (ob%dvar%d strings). Readers: shared trigger gate sub_001452D4: for 1 <= MissionVariable(+0x90) <= 29 the trigger is blocked unless flags[idx] == byte +0x94 (index -1 and 0 skip the test, so var 0 is writable but never gates). 22 callers: slot 7 of 16 MATrigger types, MAFreeCameraController #46/#48, 4 unowned. sub_00169A49 ANDs flags over an int32 list (objectives; list 0x4EB240 unidentified). Wiki fixes: sub_00169A49 is a reader, not a writer; sub_00145D77 does not read the table; the radius gate is in sub_001467B1. Conflicting wiki notes to reconcile: t04 MissionVariable -1 everywhere in retail vs catalog 12,728 of 13,300 slots are -1. UPDATE 2026-10-24: MARoot mf0.mf29 are this table (maroot-flags-are-mission-variables); save reads MEM8(0x4EB9E0+i).

facts.title: sub_0001BE20 is heap-statistics bookkeeping
facts.fact: sub_0001BE20 (heap, size, flags) is gated on byte [0x50BA24]; it checks the heap ptr is in the static descriptor array [0x4D3950,0x4E1150) and its tag is mike (0x656B696D), climbs the +0xD4 parent-heap link, then decrements +0x98 (flag bit 1) and +0x9C (bit 2), subtracts the size from +0x94 and adds it to +0xB8 (0x1BE48-0x1BEA1). A one-shot underflow warning uses flags 0x4BAACD/0x4BAACC. Heap descriptor layout: +0x00 mike, +0x94 live bytes, +0x98/+0x9C counts, +0xB8 cumulative bytes, +0xD4 parent heap. sub_0001D250 = sized free (<=0x80 pool table 0x4E1178, 0x81-0x100 table 0x4E1150 via 0x1E3F0, else 0x1C670); sub_0001CF40 = free(ptr), header [ptr-0x10] heap, [ptr-0xC] size, [ptr-2] align; fallback 0x2BBBFE/0x2BBBE7 when [0x50BA44] clear. The MASpawner offset match is a coincidence. MASpawner slot 7 (0x13321F) compares +0x98 (0x133255) and +0x9C (0x13326B) then increments both (0x133305/0x13330B) before spawning via 0x133648; no spawner-side decrement found (xscan, 18 hits); only resets are and [esi+0x9c],0 at 0x133F03 and a store at 0x13246D. So MaxActiveSpawners likely acts as a LIFETIME cap (inferred; needs a runtime trace of +0x9C across unit deaths). Open: callers of 0x133F03 (from 0x133EDB) and 0x13246D (from 0x132449): re-activation or death callback; which of +0x98/+0x9C is NumActive and which total. UPDATE 2026-10-24: counters settled as lifetime cap in spawner-counters-lifetime-cap; 0x133F03 is the MACollectionArea ctor and 0x13246D the MASpawner ctor.

facts.title: Water thickness pass is an NV2A register-combiner program
facts.fact: First per-plane water pass (lines 6700-6709): NV2A register-combiner, not an SM pixel shader: 4 stages, ctl 0x00011104, prog 0x005E1, final 0x0000000C/0x00001C80, colour mask 0x01000000 (alpha only), z func 203 (LESS) mask on, blend off. T0 = 640x480 fmt 0x12 surface 0x80488000 (dependent-AR source into T1); T1 = 256x64 LUT 0x81271000 fmt 0x1A; T2 = 1024x1 LUT 0x81279000 fmt 0x1A. Stage 2 const C0 = 0x08FFFFFF. Decoded (rcdec): alpha = 8*(T1.b-T2.b) + V0.a^2 + (T1.a-T2.a)*C0.a, agreeing with the t15 thickness formula (resolves the thickness conflict in favour of t15; confirms water-z2w-meaning). Diffuse V0.a = 5.27 in the trace (unclamped as logged). Stage 3 shows non-zero ICW/OCW (D4D420DC/0C00): probably a pass-through. PC translation kit/source/game/src/kernel/nv2a_gpu_d3d11.c pixel_program (~391-428) specialises shaders keyed on use_rc, rc control, stage program, final combiners and per-stage ICW/OCW; RECOMP_PIXEL_SPECIALIZE=0 falls back to the generic PS (code-confirmed). Open: which code writes the combiners (SetPixelShader token vs raw NV097) and its caller; whether WATER material routine 0x4EC40 issues it; which LUT is Z2W and which PrecisionLookup.
facts.how_to_use: Editor: use the t15 form 8*(T1.b-T2.b)+V0.a^2+(T1.a-T2.a)*C0.a.

facts.title: MARoot objective array save/load keys
facts.fact: Save = sub_000F175D, Load = sub_000F235C (slots 0/1 of fn table 0x46878C; direction inferred). Objectives are stored under per-index keys: ObjectiveType%d, NumObjectiveVars%d, ob%dvar%d, NumObjectiveObjects%d, ob%dobj%d, dwVoiceCueID%d, ObjectiveImage%d, ObjectiveItemDesc%d, ObjectiveItemText%d, ObjectiveEnabledBool%d, ObjectiveEditorName%d. NumObjectiveItems (C25E8457) is written as constant 30 (0xF1E42): 30 slots 0-29. Mission flags in the same serializer: NumMissionFlags + mf%d / mfname%d. No fixed per-element stride or runtime offset recovered; no reader branching on MARoot ObjectiveType found; MAObjectiveType's own ObjectiveType is at +0x5C beside ObjectiveNumber +0x58 (serializers sub_0012E29A/sub_0012E32D). Open: loop base/stride inside sub_000F175D; meaning of ObjectiveType values; sub_0016990A (Objective %d/Variable %d) clue.

facts.title: MARoot loader scalars
facts.fact: Loader sub_000F235C reads named getters and stores: MissionType (838106BC) -> this+0xB4 (store 0xF2617, then passed to sub_00166339 in ecx); MusicType (F3DA2E47) -> this+0xB8 (0xF266A); BuildingCollapseInterval (1F28C318) -> float this+0x104 (0xF27B1, via sub_00033C70); UseVehicleFromPreviousMission (4FE620E0) -> byte this+0x108, normalised with setne (0xF2745-0xF275B). Consumers not traced; no enum compares in the loader. Catalog fixes: these store offsets match the catalog evidence offsets (180/184/260/264), not code.offset; conv_kind bool is wrong for MissionType and MusicType (full int). Save flag (0AAB6A1F, read 0xF2DEA) and UseStandardMechResources (F5512E1B, read 0xF2446) are also read here; stores not traced.

facts.title: MARoot mission flags mf0.mf29 = the MissionVariable byte table
facts.fact: Mission flag (N) mf0.mf29 = the MissionVariable byte table at absolute 0x4EB9E0 (30 bytes), not a MARoot field. Save sub_000F175D reads MEM8(0x4EB9E0+i); load sub_000F235C writes it (recomp_0024.c:21772-21776, 23326). Same table as trigger gate / MATriggerTimer / objective check / MAActionMissionVariableSet (mission-variable-table-confirmed). CORRECTS the t12 wording that save reads only ob%dvar strings. mf%d, mfname%d, dwVoiceCueID%d, ob%dvar%d are referenced only by the save/load pair; voice-cue slots (30 u32, all 0 in the 1,320 retail slots) have no traced reader; objective VO plays through MAActionPlayVoice's own CueID (+0x78, sub_0019B89F) (inferred, negative). Leads: save starts with edi=0x4EB240 (int32 list ANDed by sub_00169A49, probably objective-to-variable links); load fill loop at recomp_0024.c:23016 writes across MARoot+0xBC (possible voice storage); byte 0x4EB9DE unknown. CORRECTION 2026-10-24: 0x4EB240 is the 0x41-byte-record Variable block holding dwVoiceCueID, not an objective-variable list (maroot-voice-block).

facts.title: MACorporeal topple method detail
facts.fact: sub_000DD8B9 is a POSITION getter, not the topple path: returns [this+0x90] if set, else vtable slot 0 of the sub-object at [this+0x8C]+0x40, else the zero vec3 at 0x5283D8. Topple method is sub_000E0C3F (MACorporeal base slot 85, +0x154), which calls DD8B9 for positions (0xE0D22/0xE0D32). After the mass-ratio test (settings-object-and-statics), byte arg [ebp+0x10] must be nonzero (0xE0D16). If this+0x1C bit 0x20000 is set: scale s = slot +0x18 float of the +0x8C+0x40 sub-object; helper 0x2AD120 gives vector V, and |s*V|^2 is compared with static 0x4B2E18 (0xE0DDC); mirror block at 0xE0E18-0xE0E46. Identities unknown. Neighbour getter sub_000DD905 reads float [this+0x90]+0x28, else slot +0x20 on the +0x8C sub-object, else const 0x493A54. +0xDC = mass is still inferred (best candidate CorporalMass 02C7B6FC, code null); on MABuilding sub_000D81DA writes a LIGHTS child pointer at +0xDC, so +0xDC is not universally a float. UPDATE 2026-10-24: CorporalMass layouts tangled, see corporal-mass-layouts.

facts.title: MAEnvironment fog loader and applier
facts.fact: Only 6 of 70 MAEnvironment catalog entries have a read site, all fog, all in the named-property loader sub_00130290 (Get(name) into MAEnvState): start 0x130353, end 0x130398, band top 0x1303DD, band bottom 0x130422, colour 0x130461. Fog applier sub_001309CD: each field has a target and rate: start target +0xE8/rate +0xEC; end +0xF0/+0xF4; band top +0xF8/+0xFC; band bottom +0x100/+0x104. sub_00130E06 steps the live value toward the target by rate*dt, clamped, returns 1 when equal; results go to sub_001267EE, which writes the live fog block ebx+0xF8.0x118 (getter sub_0012683B). Defaults: start 200 m, end 450 m, band top 25 m, bottom -10 m. Fog colour: catalog says ARGB uint (default 0xFF000000) but the applier reads three float targets +0xCC/+0xD0/+0xD4 with rates +0xDC/+0xE0/+0xE4 (per-channel fade) (inferred; unpacking via sub_0011D75C unconfirmed). FogOn shares slot +0xC4 and is the default pushed for Get(FogMode) (0x1304BB). Open: argument-to-field map of sub_001267EE, who reads the live block; the other 58 inferred entries have no read site (probably editor-only or unused). UPDATE 2026-10-24: live fog block and colour unpacking in live-fog-block.

facts.title: MACameraPan Smooth path basis is Catmull-Rom
facts.fact: MAFreeCamera (vtable 0x46D110) is the camera body (position +0x90, rotation +0x9C, lens near/far/FOV copied +0x84 to +0x8C by slot +0x40 0x11DB9D). Pan interpolation lives in MACameraPan (vtable 0x46D738); shot timing is MAFreeCameraController Shot length (default 8 s). MACameraPan keys an untimed vector of Vec3 points at +0x1A8 (begin/end/cap, 12-byte items). Slot +0x2C (0x121D53) copies +0x7C to +0x124, appends via 0x122CDA and clears Smooth path (+0x160) when the count is exactly 2. Setup writes a 4x4 basis at +0x1B4.0x1F0 = 2x the Catmull-Rom matrix (rows -1,3,-3,1 / 2,-5,4,-1 / -1,0,1,0 / 0,2,0,0) (recomp_0028.c:18791-18810): Smooth path = Catmull-Rom, 2 points = linear. Fields: Heading +0x110, Pitch +0x114, Pan speed +0x118, Lock on target +0x13C, Look at vec3 +0x140, Smooth path +0x160 (writer 0x121ED1, reader 0x1220AC). No duration property; t source unknown (Pan speed*dt?). Evaluator not found. Open: per-frame Update of both classes (MACameraPan +0xB8/+0xBC 0x12224E/0x1225AA, base 0x11C993). UPDATE 2026-10-24: per-frame driver and hold-at-end in campan-driver.

facts.title: Cinema per-frame tick and candidate forced-end paths
facts.fact: sub_0015D4C7 (vtable slot +0x18 of anonymous vtables 0x45396C / 0x475F1C; no direct callers) keeps no persistent list. Each frame it fills a local vector via the recursive tree walk sub_0015D3BF (push_back 0x16B8F7), keeping nodes whose [+0x1C] has bit 11 set and bit 13 clear. sub_0015D417 then calls each node's vtable +0x1C(flag) and +0x24; a nonzero +0x24 leads to sub_0016B147(ctx,node). For MACinema +0x1C = sub_001559A0, so that handler is a callee of this tick, not a skip-button caller. Active latch byte [this+0x138]: cleared when element 0 of the global array [0x50E280]'s float (sub_000C8BDC) is <= 0 (0x15D553), and when [sub_00018F10+0x69] or byte 0x50C94D is set (0x15D5D4; skips the callback and the checkpoint). sub_0015D45F gates the checkpoint sub_0015EFF2. These two clears are candidate forced-end paths. Element type MACinema inferred. Open: bodies of 0x0B61C0/0x16B147 and tail calls 0x15D2E9, 0x161B4B, 0xCC2ED, 0x81260, 0xEA529, 0xCA4DE, 0x15F29B, 0xDBAC0, 0x15D499; who fills 0x50E280; meaning of 0x50C94D. CORRECTION 2026-10-24: 0x15D4C7 is likely the world tick; 0x50C94D is a lobby/load flag; the 0x50E280 clear is player 0 health (cinema-world-tick-correction).

facts.title: MAMech named-property loader fn 0xFAA65 and label suspects
facts.fact: fn 0xFAA65 is the MAMech named-property LOADER (push <Name>; call [eax+0xC] getter, then a store), same pattern as MARoot/MAEnvironment loaders, not a schema registration (corrects the first sweep). Store slot = catalog offset - 0x20 (loader base = object+0x20). Catalog write_site VAs are name pushes in fn 0xF8F8F (save side), not stores. So catalog read_site != consumer for MAMech. Slots (loader-relative): Current heat +0x85C (read 0x100A52, ratio 0x105522; runtime heat vs loaded value); Jump Jet Pause +0x4F8 (also written by setters 0x105741/0x10577A: possibly runtime state); Footprint Alt Cue ID +0x460; Claw Release Cue ID +0x7B4 (type should be cue_id); Fall Rotate Speed Back +0xAA8 / Left +0xAA0; Footprint Decal +0x440 (read 0x10129B, 0xF8793 bone_foot_print_r/l); Footprint Model +0x44C (MAMech#22 0xFD9D9); Jump Jet Over +0x500; Claw crack decal +0x7A0 (code name MechClawDecal, crack unsupported; /tmpDev/claw/claw.mat is a known missing retail file). Roles inferred. Footstep shake: MAMech#8 sub_000FD43E computes [+0x46C]/[+0x470]*[x]*[+0x484] (Mech Footstep Shake Amount, default 0.5) and passes it to a shake call (code-confirmed). Label suspects (inferred): Fall Rotate Accel Back/Left (180/90 deg/s) are copied raw into fall state [+0xD0] (00105EF2): rotation RATES not accelerations; Post Fall Destruction Delay is code-bool with no MAMech consumer (probably a toggle); Left Leg current HP (+0x50, default 335) collides with a MACorporeal float store at 0xE10F0 (likely starting HP, offset/type wrong); Max Fire Speed use at 0x1B4515 unverified. 0x105EF2 (MAMech#16) reads 4 of these; consumers mix two base conventions (setters use ecx+0x4D8). Lower confidence: Small Hit Anim Blend Strength 0.75 (0xFDD5D); Skip walk animation (0xFE422, shared walk 0xDC796); Cooling rate 10/s (x87 in 0x1052FF); Jumpjet Max Forward Back Speed (0x18A459). UPDATE 2026-10-24: limb HP is a table at [MAMech+0x240]; Left Leg current HP suspect resolved (mech-loader-positional-binding).

facts.title: MARoot objectives live in a global 30-record table, stride 0x64
facts.fact: Objectives live in a GLOBAL table of 30 records, stride 0x64, base 0x50E860 (save base; load pointer starts at 0x50E86C). Record +0x10 (0x50E870+i*0x64) holds ObjectiveType%d (load stores MEM32(esi+4), esi=0x50E86C+i*0x64); readers use eax*0x64+0x50E86C / 0x50E860 with bound cmp eax,0x1E (recomp_0037.c:15370-15380). Record layout: +0x00 enabled byte (set to 1 at recomp_0036.c:14647/14838, tested in recomp_0052-0057; inferred ObjectiveEnabled), +0x0C text, +0x10 type, +0x18 (used when >0 by HUD), +0x20.+0x47 ten int32 MissionVariable slots, +0x48 done byte, +0x4C/+0x50 list. Only compare seen on the type: cmp eax,9 (recomp_0029.c:3985, dup 4263). The catalog ObjectiveType enum (0 to 3) belongs to MAObjectiveType, a different class. Load stride inferred.

facts.title: Objective completion, current index 0x4EB23C and reset
facts.fact: Completion = sub_00169A49 (5 call sites in recomp_0000.c): walks the 30 records (esi starts 0x50E8B4 = record+0x48, stride 0x64): skip if done byte (R+0x48) or enabled byte (R+0) is 0; AND MEM8(0x4EB9E0+v) over the 10 int32 variable slots R+0x20.R+0x47 (slot valid if 0<=v<0x1E); if at least one valid slot and all set: done=1, then call sub_001699ED only when the record index == MEM32(0x4EB23C). So objectives complete when ALL their linked MissionVariables are set. 0x4EB23C = CURRENT OBJECTIVE INDEX; sub_001699ED (leaf) advances it: start at min(cur+1,29), step past records enabled AND done, stop at the first not-done or disabled record; if all pass the index becomes 30 (the only all-done value). Reset to 0 by sub_00163A16 (0x163A24, from 0x163ABC), sub_00163AE8 (0x163B2F) and sub_0016990A (0x1699E4). CORRECTION: sub_0016990A is the mission-objective RESET (zeroes the index and the 30 MissionVariable bytes 0x4EB9E0, and refreshes the Variable %d / Objective %d records); only caller sub_00016880 (rseed string): not a debug dump. HUD: sub_001FC461 (HUD_Text.ggf) shows record[cur]+0x0C text when enabled, not done and nonzero; Objectives Display sub_0021D6F7 (vtable 0x48A4F0 slot 14) draws the entry where i==cur. Mission-end on cur==30 NOT found (inferred negative; candidates sub_001F7D9D, sub_002047D4, sub_0021C34E, walker callers 0x15AF0/0x15B8C/0x15CBC/0x15DE9/0x15F11); at 30 the HUD reads one record past the table (0x50F424/0x50F46C).
facts.how_to_use: Editor: an objective needs all of its linked MissionVariables set; MissionVariable ids 0.29.

facts.title: MABuilding tests objective type 9/10 and sets a flag
facts.fact: In MABuilding: sub_00127ED7 (vtable 0x46E3E8 slot 11, +0x2C) and sub_00128000 share a block at 0x128173. With its objective index >= 0 (likely ObjectiveNumber, read 0x128159) it reads MEM32(0x50E860+idx*0x64+0x10); if the type is 9 or 10 it sets MEM8(this+0x1E4)=1 (recomp_0029.c:3986-3998). Flag meaning unknown (objective target building?). Values 9/10 are outside the catalog's documented MARoot 0-5 range: check ObjectiveType%d on a live mission. HUD Objectives Display (vtable 0x48A4F0 slot 13 sub_0021DAC0) passes the type (or record +0x18 when >0) via sub_0021CC23/sub_0021CE35 to sub_0021DDF8 -> 0x000F60AA (icon/text by type?) without comparing it.

facts.title: dwVoiceCueID storage and 0x4EB240 block
facts.fact: It is 30 records of 0x41 bytes (end 0x4EB9DE), filled by sub_0016990A under key Variable %d (MissionVariable names?), and the MARoot load stores dwVoiceCueID%d at +0x1C of that block (load base ebp+0x70 = 0x4EB240, recomp_0024.c:23277; store 0xF2BC7). No reader of those values found. MARoot+0xBC is 18 dwords set once to a default (23011-23016), unrelated. Per-record advance inferred.

facts.title: NumActive never decreases: MaxActiveSpawners is a lifetime cap
facts.fact: Counters: NumSpawned +0x98 vs MaxSpawners +0x7C (total limit, 0x133255); NumActive +0x9C vs MaxActiveSpawners +0x90 (active cap, 0x13326B); both increment on spawn (0x133305/0x13330B). The resets are constructors only: 0x133F03 (and [esi+0x9c],0 at 0x133F53) is the MACollectionArea ctor (create 0x133EDF; 0x133EDB is an unrelated slot-46 getter); 0x13246D is the MASpawner ctor (create 0x132449), zeroing +0x98 at 0x1324C0 and +0x9C at 0x1324C6. Other writers: slot 7 (increments), slot 16 0x133DB2 (MaxActiveSpawners setter, mov [ecx+0x90] at 0x133E15), serializer 0x13270D (anon vtable 0x4704BC slot 0). So NumActive never decreases and MaxActiveSpawners acts as a LIFETIME cap (inferred; confirm with an in-game +0x9C log across a kill). Misattribution fixed: the wiki open 0x157CD0 touches +0x9C is MACultureSystem's own +0x90/+0x98/+0x9C (from slot 8 0x157C40 when [this+0x82] is set). Slice type of NumActive bool is wrong (uint counter). Open: caller of serializer 0x13270D, caller of slot 16; 0x1452D4 increments [ebx+0x98] twice. UPDATE 2026-10-24: 0x1452D4 is MATrigger FIRE; serializer order in maspawner-serializer-order.
facts.how_to_use: Settles the spawner dispute: treat MaxActiveSpawners as a total cap per spawner.

facts.title: CorporalMass save and load use different layouts (TANGLED)
facts.fact: MACorporeal ctor (0xD702D) zeroes +0xDC (store 0xD70FE). No literal float store to [reg+0xDC] exists in MACorporeal's 127 vtable slots. MABuilding sub_000D81DA (caller 0xD75C7) stores the LIGHTS child pointer (vtable +0x50 on [esi+0x94]) at +0xDC when [esi+0x28]==classid 0x4EAFFC, else clears it (0xD81E4): one offset, two types. CorporalMass is referenced by 0xD8561 (SAVE; 0xD85C7 mid-body entry) which reads float [[edi+0x6C]+0xDC] with edi=object+0x20: +0xDC of the SUB-OBJECT at object+0x8C (the physics body; DD8B9 also uses +0x8C), MaxSpeed = [[edi+0x6C]+0xBC], passed to vtable +0x14 (Set) on the archive; and by 0xD9C64 (LOAD; 0xDA04E push name, Get via vt+0xC, 0x33C70 float) which stores to [[ebx+0x70]+0x0C], MaxSpeed at [[ebx+0x70]+0x10]: a DIFFERENT block (object+0x70, or +0x90 if ebx=object+0x20). RESOLVED 2026-10-24: one pipeline, see corporalmass-pipeline.

facts.title: MissionType becomes a one-hot bit mask
facts.fact: MissionType -> sub_00166339 (switch cmp ecx,0x12; 19-entry jump table 0x1663A3; recomp_0037.c:3755) converts it to a one-hot mission-type BIT MASK: clears [eax+4], then ORs 1<<N for N=0.17; 18 gives 0 (bare ret); >18 gives 0x1. Loader passes eax=edi+0xAC, so the mask word is MARoot+0xB0 (inferred). The mask is tested by wrapper 0x1663EF (callers 0x122FB5, and 0x166437 from 0xD7584): builds a temp object (vtable 0x476954) and tests against [param+4] with 0x1A000 = bits 13|15|16 (mission types 13, 15, 16 share some behaviour; inferred). facts.title: MACameraPan per-frame driver and hold behaviour
facts.fact: Driver sub_0012224E (slot +0xB8). With Smooth path (+0x160) set it calls sub_00122787 each frame; otherwise sub_0012266F (undecoded). Start/reset = slot +0xBC sub_001225AA (cursor +0x1A4 = 1). Advance: acc +0x16C += (1.0/sub_0001DC30)*Pan speed (+0x118); if sub_0001DC30 returns the frame rate (likely) this is speed*dt, otherwise frame-rate dependent (inferred). When acc > threshold +0x168 the segment counter +0x1A0 increments and the cursor moves; u stored at +0x164. Curve eval sub_00122956 (cubic t, t^2, t^3 chain, called at 0x12289E); the resulting Vec3 is copied to this+0x7C. It does not read the +0x1B4 basis directly (may come via 0x250370, undecoded). At the last key u=1.0 is evaluated once, then later frames exit at 0x1227A9: the camera HOLDS the last position (no loop). +0x15C==0 skips the step. Open: sub_0001DC30, sub_0012266F, arrival test sub_00122DC0 (0x12236C) and the end-of-pan effect, gate 0x50C85C. UPDATE 2026-10-24: non-smooth mode and sub_0001DC30 resolved in campan-chase-mode.

facts.title: MAMech loader binds names to offsets positionally; limb HP is a table
facts.fact: Loader 0xFAA65 binds names to offsets positionally: registrar->vt[+0xC](name, desc) returns a handle (type +0, value +0x40; getters 0x33C70 float type 7, 0x33AF0 int type 3), and the following store's displacement is the field. Examples: SmallHitAnimSpeed fstp [ebx+0x940] (0xFB986); SmallHitAnimBlendStrength [ebx+0x944] (0xFB9CE); RotateDuringFall = bit 0x8 of [ebx+0x24C] (0xFBA1D). Whether ebx = object or object+0x20 is per the sweep-2 convention (unreconciled). LIMB HP: LeftLegCurHP is NOT a direct MAMech field: the loader calls helper 0x16C416 (ecx=limb idx 0.5, edx=[ebx+0x240], eax=value): a limb table of 20-byte records at edx+4+20*idx with +0 max, +4 cur, percent = cur*100/max (0x16C416-0x16C42D). Left leg = idx 2 -> max +0x2C, cur +0x30 of [MAMech+0x240]; save slot 0 (0xF8F8F) agrees (LeftLegMaxHP push [eax+0x2C] 0xF9B2A, CurHP [eax+0x30] 0xF9B70). Catalog +0x50 is wrong; the 0xE10F0 collision is a frame temp ([ebp+0x50]), not an object field (resolves the Left Leg current HP suspect in mamech-loader-slots). Open: class of the object at MAMech+0x240 (6-limb damage table); 0x1105BA (vt+0x14, also MACorporeal slot 2). REVISED 2026-10-24: the limb table is the 6-zone block at entity +0x260 (mech-damage-zone-table).

facts.title: Live fog block written by sub_001267EE
facts.fact: Live fog setter sub_001267EE (eax=block, ecx=mode dword, xmm0=start, 7 stack args, callee pops 0x1C; lookup's cdecl label wrong): +0xF8 mode; +0xFC/+0x100/+0x104/+0x108 RGBA floats; +0x10C start; +0x110 end; +0x114 band top; +0x118 band bottom. Applier passes ecx=MAEnvState+0xC4 (FogOn/FogMode) and the stepped targets; block is ebx=[MAEnvState+0x4] (0x1309D7), owner class unnamed (likely the world/renderer env object). Render-side reader 0x126A30-0x126ACD (not in index): maps mode +0xF8 (1->0, 2->2, else 0); calls vtable+0x134(start,end) (the draw-distance fog call, ret 0x126AAA), vtable+0x13C(band top, bottom), and passes the RGBA at +0xFC via 0x54150 before vtable+0x12C. sub_0011D75C unpacks ARGB (eax) into four floats R/255,G/255,B/255,A/255 at ecx (+0.+0xC; const 0x493AB0 = 1/255): resolves the fog colour unpacking in menv-fog-applier; applier fades R/G/B and distance/band values, alpha passes unstepped. Open: writer of MAEnvState+0x4; caller of 0x126A30; D3D ids for vtable +0x12C/+0x134/+0x13C; sub_0012F8F3 fld's block+0xF8 as a float (conflicts with a mode dword).

facts.title: sub_0015D4C7 is probably the per-frame WORLD tick; 0x50C94D is a lobby/load flag
facts.fact: Callees of sub_0015D4C7 are general world-update work, not cinema teardown (inferred): 0x0B61C0 is a return-0 stub; 0x16B147 a this+0x38 thunk to push_back 0x16B8F7; 0x15D2E9 a second recursive node walker (+0x1C,+0x24,0x16B147,+0x28); 0x161B4B the game-object singleton [0x50C958] (0xB0 bytes); 0x0CC2ED a release helper over sized free 0x1D250 (heap); 0x0EA529 loops vector [0x50E304] calling vt+0x248; 0x0CA4DE a per-player pass over [0x50E280] (so 0x50E280 = the PLAYER vector); 0x0DBAC0 loops [0x50E2C8] calling UID resolver 0xB4F70 then vt+0x3C; 0x15D499 tests [0x4EB19C] and writes [0x4A6625]/[0x50C7E0]. Byte 0x50C94D has 7 writers (0x14A70 =1, 0x15270 3DLobby / \Missions\%s.wdf, 0x16919C =1 missions\3DLobby.wdf, 0x1691FB campaign transition, 0x1F54DD/0x1F5A00/0x1F5A55 =0): a lobby/mission-load flag, not a cinema byte; the latch clear at 0x15D5D4 = level transition (inferred). facts.title: MAMech damage zones: one 6-zone block at entity +0x260
facts.fact: MAMech damage zones are in a TABLE pointed to by MAMech+0x260 (the loader/writer see it as [reg+0x240], the +0x20-biased base). Block 0x7C bytes, allocated in MAMech ctor 0xF7E69 (push 0x7C; call 0x1B8D0 at 0xF8563), built by zone ctor 0x16C019, NO vtable: block+0 = owner MAMech*; block+4 = 6 records x 0x14 {+0 max int, +4 current int, +8 percent = cur*100/max, +0xC ctor constant 0,0,1,2,3,4 (meaning unknown)}; element ctor 0x1A9E44 via array helper 0x1B870; dtor 0x16C054 (single caller 0xF8757). Index 0.5 enforced by SetMax 0x16C3F7 and SetCur 0x16C416 (recompute %). Zones (names from catalog labels, inferred): 0 Front Torso +0x04/+0x08, 1 Back Torso +0x18/+0x1C, 2 Left Leg +0x2C/+0x30, 3 Right Leg +0x40/+0x44, 4 Left Arm +0x54/+0x58, 5 Right Arm +0x68/+0x6C; percent at +0x0C/+0x20/+0x34/+0x48/+0x5C/+0x70. Accessors: GetMax 0x16C43F, GetCurrent 0x16C472 (block on stack, idx in ecx; -1 if idx>5). SetCur callers: 0xF8793, 0xF8D30, 0xFAA65, 0x105EF2, 0x131EB0, 0x163C57, 0x166C0C. 0x163C57 (gated on MAMech classid 0x4EAF78) sets every zone current = max (repair/refill, inferred). 0x105EF2 (MAMech vt#16) is a MAMech->MAMech copy of the zones. VERDICTS: the 4-limb table at +0x240 REVISED to +0x260 with 6 zones; mech-sweep-3 direct slots 0x68/0x6C REFUTED (they are offsets inside the zone table); 0xE111A zeroed on arm loss REFUTED (base [ebp+0x60] in 0xE0F23, slot #87 shared by MACorporeal/MAMover/MAProjectile/MAEffect/MAMech/MATank, a motion/physics struct). Loader 0xFAA65 reads the zone block as [ebx+0x240] (FrontTorsoMaxHP -> SetMax zone 0 at 0xFB4E2-0xFB4EC); [ebx+0x260] there is the int BuckingDamage (0xFB073-0xFB084) = entity +0x280. Catalog: HP properties' code.offset = offset inside [MAMech+0x260]; Front Torso offset 608 (0x260) is the table pointer itself. Death test (torso current <= 0) not found; clue: callers of GetCurrent 0x16C472. Open: class of the zone table; struct at [ebp+0x60] in 0xE0F23. UPDATE 2026-10-24: +0xC codes are written by builder 0x16C019 (mech-zone-code-builder).

facts.title: CorporalMass is one pipeline: PhysicsInfo (+0x90) copied into body+0xDC
facts.fact: RESOLVES the CorporalMass tangle. 0xD8561 (save) / 0xD9C64 (load) ARE a pair for the same class (same string set Corporal3DObj.CorporalMass.IsFlammable; called together by subclass serializers 0xE4D80 / 0xE4EEE; MACorporeal base inferred; both this=object+0x20). MACorporeal+0x90 = Moe\PhysicsInfo block: 0x34 bytes, zero-filled, NO vtable, allocated in ctor sub_000D702D (0xD7290 push 0x34 -> sub_000D6DCB alloc, sub_000D6DB4 memset, stored 0xD72AD). Fields: +0x00 position vec3 (position getter DD8B9), +0x0C mass, +0x10 max speed, +0x14.+0x24 more. LOAD writes PhysicsInfo +0x0C/+0x10 (0xDA063); copy into the physics body (+0x8C): sub_000D7940 (only caller MACorporeal slot 11 sub_000D7B3D, 0xD7B6C) loads block+0x0C and calls body mass setter sub_002AC8D0 (movss [body+0xDC]; also body+0xE0, probably inverse mass) at 0xD79DA; block+0x10 -> body+0xBC/+0xC0 (max speed); block+0x14 -> body+0xC4. sub_000DE8EF (vt +0x40) repeats the mass/max-speed copy (0xDEE99-0xDEEC2). SAVE reads body+0xDC (0xD8771); MASS = physics body (object+0x8C) +0xDC. Topple compare is in sub_000E0C3F (slot 85), not sub_000DD8B9: body_other+0xDC * [0x4B2E1C] >= body_this+0xDC means no topple; also skipped if body_other+0x164 != 0. So no original-game asymmetry (inferred; only a save before the slot-11 copy would see stale values). Open: callers of slot 11 (+0x2C) and gates 0xC364B/0xE064A; other callers of 0x2AC8D0.
facts.how_to_use: Mass is physics-body +0xDC, not entity +0xDC.

facts.title: Correction: 0x1A000 is a function; the 13/15/16 claim is retracted
facts.fact: CORRECTION to mission-type-bitmask: 0x1A000 is NOT a mask constant but a FUNCTION (call 0x1a000) returning any mask word nonzero ([ecx+4.]). Wrapper 0x1663EF builds a temp {vtbl 0x476954, mask} via 0x166339 and tests it. Jump table 0x1663A3 maps MissionType N -> one-hot bit N (13/15/16 = 0x2000/0x8000/0x10000; type 18 sets no bit; 0 and >18 set bit 0). The claim that mission types 13/15/16 share a behaviour is unsupported: RETRACTED. 0x122FB5 = mission-type group test: mask at this+0x7C (not MARoot+0xB0; unverified there); true if mask==0 or type 18, else bit N. Only caller sub_0015DAF4 (0x15DB26) walks the child list of sub_B4280(ebx) (first +0xC, next +8); for children whose classid [+0x28]==0x4EAFE0 a false result passes the node to sub_B5350 (effect untraced: probably disables/removes objects not meant for this mission type; inferred). 0xD7584 path: sub_166437(0,P) returns (P->mask==1) with P=[esi+4]+0xCC; gates sub_D7508 (string _low) when global 0x50C8C9==0 and arg1==0; callers ignore the return. Open: sub_B5350 effect; classid 0x4EAFE0; sub_B4280; global 0x50C8C9; sub_D7508 _low (low-detail variant?). UPDATE 2026-10-24: sub_B5350 detaches the subtree (mission-type-group-detach). UPDATE 2026-10-24: readers identified (mask-test-helpers-and-readers). UPDATE 2026-10-24: see mission-type-mask-location-resolved.

facts.title: sub_0015D4C7 is not a cinema-skip walker; sub_000171E0 is a level-transition teardown
facts.fact: sub_0015D4C7 is slot 6 of two anonymous vtables (0x45396C, 0x475F1C) and reads the active PLAYER vector (begin 0x50E280 / end 0x50E284, same as bot_ensure_active). It only uses the first element: calls sub_000C8BDC, compares the float with 0.0, and the <=0 branch clears [this+0x138] (behaviour inferred, partial scan). It also uses pointer lists 0x50E304/0x50E308 and 0x50E2C8/0x50E2CC (see water/pointer-list correction): looks like a per-level/per-frame world manager tick (inferred). sub_000171E0's Stop(cinema,0,0) (via sub_00155B53) is a LEVEL-TRANSITION TEARDOWN gated only by byte 0x4EB19C; no pad/input read in 0x171E0-0x17700; called from five sites in one 0x14xxx routine (0x14A70/0x14B02/0x14E7B/0x14E86/0x14ED7; 0x14A70 also writes lobby/mission-load flag 0x50C94D=1); [arg1+0xF5] nonzero = instant teardown (inferred). Cinema start/stop/advance (0x155A99/0x155B53/0x1559A0) read no input. The SKIP BUTTON path is still unknown: runtime trace needed (log the return address at Stop 0x155B53 when pressing skip). facts.title: MABuilding +0x1E4 objective flag routes to an object-event branch
facts.fact: +0x1E4 is zeroed in ctor 0x127D46 (init block +0x1E0.+0x1E4), set to 1 at 0x128188 (vt slot 11 path); no MABuilding method reads it. Reader 0x129606: cmp byte [edi+0x1E4],0 -> return 0 if clear; else runs predicates, calls 0x131D6C (latches bit 0x02 in [obj+0x1A8] once), returns 1. Called from 0x13224A (only when [obj+0x28]==0x4EAFFC = MABuilding classid; a true return skips its generic path) and 0x131957. So the flag routes an objective building into a special object-event branch (probably objective destroy/complete notification; inferred). No HUD/radar/damage reader. game_network 0x3608BE reads +0x1E0.+0x1E5 into an XOR checksum (idiv 0xFE) at 0x360A09 -> record +0x8F0 (likely net state hash; inferred). 0xF60AA is a plain 2D table accessor, no type branch: arg+0x218+0x24*(6*row+col) for row<0x12 (18), col<6, else NULL (whether row = objective type unknown). +0x1E4 is also a field in MASnatchItDataCore (0x1351A9), MAFlagCTF (0x151625), anon_00479428 (0x18FD16). Open: 0x131D6C operand [ebp+8] / 0x131EB0 (see object-destroyed-event); caller 0x131957 and vtable 0x470200 identity; F60AA caller and rows. The attacker is the damage record +0x0C link on the TakeDamage path; there is no last-attacker field on the victim. See damage-attacker-is-rec-plus-0c-link-no-last-attacker-on-victim-13200f-not-kill-credit and powerup-collect-rule-game-side-armour-only-when-damaged-weapon-only-when-useful.

facts.title: MACameraPan non-smooth mode is a chase, not node interpolation
facts.fact: Non-smooth mode (this+0x160 == 0) = sub_0012266F: cam (this+0x7C) += unit(Vt - cam) * PanSpeed (this+0x118) * c0, c0 = runtime double 0x4E2428 (written by sub_0001DD00/DD80/DDB4/DE70; probably frame dt, inferred). Vt = T->vtbl[+0x60] with P = this+0x15C, T = P+0x8C. On overshoot (dot(Vt - newcam, D) < 0) snaps to Vt and calls sub_0012F014(P) (recomp_0028.c:20055-20056). Arrival test sub_00122DC0 = per-axis box test |cam - this+0x130| <= 0.0002 on x, y, z (const 0x45AF34 = 2e-4); arrival jumps to loc_00122476 (not decoded). sub_0001DC30 returns a RATE (fps): 30.0 fallback (0x493B98) when dword 0x50BA80 <= 4, otherwise computed from 0x50BA7C/0x50BA78 (inferred fps). Smooth path uses (1/fps)*speed, chase uses c0*speed: same PanSpeed field. Resolves the open in campan-driver for sub_0001DC30 and sub_0012266F. UPDATE 2026-10-24: c0 is the scaled frame delta, so the chase is frame-rate independent (frame-delta-and-fps-ring).

facts.title: Live fog setter caller and renderer-side reader
facts.fact: Live fog SETTER entry = sub_001267EE (0x1267EE-0x12683A, ret 0x1C; 0x1267FD is a mid-body store to +0x10C). Only direct caller: recomp_0030.c:11304 (return 0x130B18, in the fog applier). Writes block +0xF8 mode, +0xFC.+0x108 RGBA, +0x10C.+0x118 range/band. 0x126A30 (fog READER/applier to renderer) has NO direct callers (indirect entry; inferred). It calls renderer object [ebx+8] slots +0x12C (ptr to packed 0xAARRGGBB from block+0xFC via 0x54150 -> fog colour, inferred), +0x134 and +0x13C with float pairs (start/end, band; inferred). No D3DRS immediates at the call sites. Renderer object, not MAEnvState (MAEnvState vtable 0x46FFD0 has only 46 slots). Mode block+0xF8 -> 0x81350 = 3-way switch (0/1/2 -> 0x8137A/0x8136C/0x8135E), result unused on the decoded path. Writer of MAEnvState+0x4 NOT found (candidates 0x130FEA/0x131003 unverified).

facts.fact: WATER body 0x4EC40 (WATER vt slot 6) has no direct D3D/SetPixelShader call; binds reflectiontexture via 0x2612E0 (name -> slot lookup 0x261CE0, cached at [this+0x44]; inferred). facts.title: 0x131D6C one-shot object-destroyed event; 0x131EB0 heals the killer
facts.fact: 0x131D6C (name inferred) = one-shot object-destroyed event: obj=[ebp+8], source in EAX (0 -> exit). If bit 0x02 of [obj+0x1A8] is clear: set it, call obj vt+0x124 ([obj+0x1AC],0,0,0) (MACorporeal slot 73 = 0x0DF911, which notifies through [0x4EB210]+0x120) and vt+0xF4 (0) (slot 61 = 0x0DCD08); then 0x131EB0(obj); 0x0DF216(SRC) if bit 0x01 set; gates on singleton 0x18F10 byte +0x69 and 0x12AE8E; then 0x13200F(obj) (raises 3 weapon classes like a power-up). Six callers (0x10063D, 0x109217, 0x115E74, 0x115EF3, 0x129606, 0x1E0200), so not objective-only; no direct MARoot objective-table reference (recomp_0030.c:14612-14711). 0x131EB0 heals the KILLER: if [obj+0x1B0] != 0 and SRC is a MAMech (classid 0x4EAF78) it walks SRC's damage-zone block [SRC+0x260] with GetMax 0x16C43F / GetCurrent 0x16C472 / SetCur 0x16C416, adding float([obj+0x1B0]) x scale (0x493A60 = 1.0, or 0x16B0C4 result when [SRC+4] is MAPlayer) clamped to max. So destroying an object with +0x1B0 (a salvage/repair amount) repairs the destroyer's mech (meaning inferred). Conflict: wiki t01a/t01b treat actor +0x1A8/+0x1AC as a rider table; here +0x1A8 is a flag dword on the destroyed object (class differs? MABuilding slice offset 0x188). The attacker is the damage record +0x0C link on the TakeDamage path; there is no last-attacker field on the victim. See damage-attacker-is-rec-plus-0c-link-no-last-attacker-on-victim-13200f-not-kill-credit and powerup-collect-rule-game-side-armour-only-when-damaged-weapon-only-when-useful.

facts.title: Frame delta 0x4E2428 and the fps ring
facts.fact: 0x4E2428 (double) = SCALED FRAME DELTA in seconds: dt = timescale 0x4A14F0 (set 1.0 by sub_0001DD00 init) * e (elapsed given to the producer); game clock 0x4E2440 += dt; 0x4E2418 = e (recomp_0001.c:11360-11364). In producer sub_0001DD80 only, float 0x50BA70 overrides e when > 0 (fixed-step override?). fps ring: 0x50BA78 = ring head h (0.63) of 64 double timestamps at 0x4E2200 (stamp 0x4E2408 from indirect clock [0x4A1500]); 0x50BA7C (M) and 0x50BA80 (N) = producer-call counters zeroed by DD00. sub_0001DC30 fps = k/(T[j1]-T[j0]), j1=h-1, k=min(M-1,W), W=clamp(entry eax,4,63); returns 30.0 if N <= 4; no zero-span guard. Other globals: 0x4E2438 unscaled sum of e; 0x4E2424 = int(dt*1000); 0x4E2430 = int(clock*1000) cumulative ms (WIKI.md:604 step stamp is WRONG); 0x4E2420 frame count. So the camera-pan chase (c0 = 0x4E2428) is frame-rate independent. Open: which producer runs live (DD80/DDB4/DE70); the wiki's 0.2 s dt cap (WIKI.md:4556) is not in DD80/DDB4 (check DE70); writers of 0x50BA70/0x4A14F0 after init.

facts.title: MAMissionTypeGroup children are detached at level load by mission type
facts.fact: Level load: sub_0015DAF4 finds the MATerrain node (classid 0x4EAF5C) under ebx via sub_B4280 (find-first-child-by-classid; root eax, classid edi, flag 0 = recursive), walks its children, and for each MAMissionTypeGroup child (classid 0x4EAFE0; MAGroup subclass, obj 0x80) runs the mission test 0x122FB5(child, [ebx+0xD4] = current mission type). Groups that FAIL go to sub_B5350 = DETACH the subtree, not delete: sub_B4EF0 on every descendant then the node (calls [node+0x60] obj vt+8, node vt+0x34, clears bit 0x04 of flags +0x1C, then sub_B6700 re-parents children to owner and sub_B66A0 unlinks node from owner). No free seen; next sibling is loaded before the call. Meaning: each GameType/MissionType's objects live in a MAMissionTypeGroup under MATerrain; groups whose mask excludes the current type are detached at load (fits t04_scenario.json:4382). Resolves the sub_B5350 open in mission-type-bitmask-correction. Open: +0x1C bit 0x04 meaning; sub_B6700 tail; class of ebx and its +0xD4. UPDATE 2026-10-24: invoker and class layout in mission-type-mask-location-resolved.
facts.how_to_use: Editor: per-game-type objects go in MAMissionTypeGroup children of MATerrain.

facts.title: Damage absorb keys verified by CRC; per-type arrays on the absorber
facts.fact: Flame/Ballistic absorb labels are NOT swapped: keys (crc32(name+DamageAbsorbed)^0xFFFFFFFF) Standard 34F74FCC, Energy 28641E98, Ballistic 90ECAE7B, Explosive 4F229D5F, Flame 85020171 match the catalog; retracts the sweep-4 swap suspicion. Damage type index 0 Standard, 1 Energy, 2 Ballistic, 3 Explosive (splash), 4 Flame (name table XBE 0x459970 stride 0x100; documented). Per-type absorb code = sub_001872A0 on the ABSORBER object [this+0x220] (only when its vt+0xC returns 6 = reactive armour). Absorb vt+0x1CC = sub_000E9A10(dmg,type,splash) -> sub_000E6999. Per-type arrays on the absorber: float +0x48+4t (gate: skip if <= 0; absorb fraction), +0x5C+4t, +0x70+4t, byte +0x84+t (fits Absorbed/Factor/RecoveryDelay/PassedOn x5); names inferred. Open: which store in serializer sub_00186EA5 fills +0x48+4t; the first multiply uses [ebp+0xC] (splash arg?) not the +0x48 array (needs trace: RECOMP_DEFENSE_PROBE hooks at sub_E9A10); reactive armour 75% ballistic vs MAMech Ballistic default 0.0.

facts.title: Archive put/get pattern distinguishes save from load; MARoot direction fixed
facts.fact: DIRECTION FIX: MARoot sub_000F175D is SAVE and sub_000F235C is LOAD. Load: archive vt+0xC(raw name BriefingText) -> variant -> getter 0x33C10 (returns [v+0x40] when tag==6) -> MEM32(esi+0x9C)=eax (0xF285F; recomp_0024.c:23204-23216, inside sub_000F235C starting:22598). Save: holder ctor 0x33890(field), name object (ctor 0x1A060), archive vt+0x14(name, holder), dtor 0x33A90. Variant holder: [+0x00] type tag, [+0x18]/[+0x20] owned blocks, [+0x1C] string buffer {begin,end,cap}, [+0x40] payload. Ctors: 0x33830 (tag 3), 0x33850 bool, 0x33870 word, 0x33890 (tag 6 dword/text id), 0x338B0 double, 0x338D0 byte; 0x33A90 destructor (frees, copies nothing; frees [+0x40] only for tag 0x11). Generalization (inferred): every class serializer pair is put = archive vt+0x14(name obj, holder) and get = archive vt+0xC(name) -> getter -> mov; so MAMech 0xFAA65 with mov [ebx+disp],eax after getters is a LOAD.
facts.how_to_use: Use this pattern to tell save from load in any serializer.

facts.title: Ground lightmap window not sized from any DrawDistance data field
facts.fact: Stock: sub_00052F90 computes authored extent = sqrt(A^2+B^2), A = F*tan(0.5*K*v), B = F/sub_0030C650(.), from camera queries (camera via ebp->[+0x6C]->[+4]->[+8]); 0x493A5C = 0.5; K involves runtime global 0x50E0DC = 0x50E0D8 * const 0x493D90 (set in data_init sub_0031F230). The catalog has no DrawDistance property. PC: ma2_pc_lightmap_parameters scales the far plane by the PC-only PC_DRAW_DISTANCE (default 50; 2^((DD-50)/50), clamp 0.100) and widens horizontal FOV to the rendered one; ma2_pc_lightmap_extent = max(authored, frustum diameter) (kit/source/game/src/pc_draw_distance.c). So even DD50 differs from stock (diameter term). Consistent with ground-map-window-drawdistance. Open: class at this+0x6C; clamp bounds esp+0x128/0x12C; runtime K. Closes B5.

facts.title: MATrigger +0x88 fired byte and +0x98 activation count
facts.fact: +0x88 = TriggerFired byte (catalog D91E85D1, internal; mapping inferred, slice 0x68). Fire routine 0x1452D4 tests it before firing (fire-once) (0x145360, set 1 at 0x1453A8/0x1453E1; 0x14524D tests +0x89 first). Read by all 18 MATrigger subclass slot-7 evaluators (Radius 0x1467B1, Point 0x145A14, NationRadius 0x14726F, Cuboid 0x1480E3, Timer 0x148BB7, Destroyed 0x1491EF, MenuActivate 0x14A415, Height 0x14F018, Checkpoint 0x14F3D4, FlagStatus 0x14F6B4, Logic 0x14F9BC, Counter 0x14FC90, PlayerVehicleType 0x14FE79, Attach 0x19EDFD, GameTime 0x19F40A, StatCompare 0x19FAAA, Uber 0x19FD75, Spider 0x1A0094). +0x98 = NumberOfTimesActivated (catalog 6F75E9B0, u32; mapping inferred): incremented only by fire; read only by MATriggerCounter 0x14FC90 (on its referenced trigger). No MaxFireCount limit exists. Base helper sub_0014524D (checks TriggerEnabled +0x89, then sets +0x88=al) is called by 14 evaluators; whether any passes 0 (re-arm) is unchecked. Already-fired path of 0x1452D4 calls sub_000B4F70 / sub_000C6FBF (re-fire vs exit, unidentified). No MASpawner reader of +0x88/+0x98 found (scan limited to the trigger family). CORRECTION 2026-10-24: 0x14524D only clears +0x88 (re-arm); B4F70/C6FBF are not on the fired path (trigger-rearm-0x14524d).

facts.title: MAMech death = torso zone current <= 0
facts.fact: Zone-dead predicate 0x16C3E2(block, zone in ecx) = GetCurrent <= 0 (setle). 0x16C3B9 = FrontTorso(0) dead OR BackTorso(1) dead. MAMech DEATH: sub_00100BE8: if a torso zone is dead -> call mech vt+0x78(0) (slot 30, unnamed; presumably destroy/explode) and skip the leg tests (recomp_0025.c:26058-26074). Legs only set flag bits in a 64-bit word at mech+0x268/+0x26C (LLeg = bit 0x10000000 of the high/low dword; RLeg packed there, bit untraced). No arm zero test found. Slot 116 (vt+0x1D0 sub_00100A52) calls sub_00102102(this,1,0,0) (664 B, 21 callers: kill/eject?) when word bit 19, or bit 17 with [+0x1C] bit 17 clear, and a threshold from sub_000EB475 ([+0x7DC]/[+0x7E0]) passes. Slot +0x78 meaning inferred. Open: MAMech vt slot 30 name; sub_00102102 identity; writers of +0x268 bits 17/19 (masks 0x20000/0x80000); RLeg bit; arm-zone zero tests. Resolves the death-test clue in mech-damage-zone-table. CORRECTION 2026-10-24: vt slot 30 (+0x78) is a setter of +0x184, not destroy/explode (mech-slot30-setter-0x184). UPDATE 2026-10-24: slot 30 sets health to 0 (corporeal-health-184).

facts.title: Water shader issuer still unknown statically
facts.fact: Not; mostly negative. WATER callees: 0x1D250 = sized free (ptr, size, heap ctx; pools 0x4E1178/0x4E1150 when byte 0x50BA44), not a bind. 0x2612E0 = named-texture bind wrapper (0x261290 / name resolver 0x261CE0). 0x69D70 = material texture-stage setter (mipmap_bias/mipmapping/filter/tiling/filename; 27 call sites; shared with 0x4C080/0x4C350/0x4CFE0; inferred), indirect calls at 0x69E2E/0x69E3B/0x69E48 are the only device-level clue. 0x50BA30 (and 0x50BA2C) = heap/allocator context passed to the sized free (inferred), not the D3D device. PS_FINALCOMBINERSETTING strings only in game_render printers 0x3F32C4/0x4018DF. Water combiner issuer parked for a runtime trace (log combiner/PS binds during the water draw).

facts.title: MACorporeal slot 11 effectively always runs the PhysicsInfo copy
facts.fact: Not Slot 11 (sub_000D7B3D) = base-then-override register-and-physics-init: calls MAEntity base slot 11 sub_000C364B first (all visible paths return 1; its only false path needs sub_000B3BA0 = 0, which always sets al=1), so the PhysicsInfo -> body copy sub_000D7940 effectively ALWAYS runs. Also registers the object when +0xA0 != 0 (node at +0xA4 in list headed by global 0x4EB014; helpers 0xB58D0/0xB59D0). Gate sub_000E064A (true when +0x84 bit0, or classid [0x4EB06C]/[0x4EB178], or classid [0x4EB04C] with +0x1A8 bit4) -> sub_000E0681 clears a 16-bit entry keyed by +0x2C in table 0x50E2D4; does not block the copy. WHEN slot 11 runs is unresolved (300 indirect [reg+0x2C] call sites): needs an in-game call-stack capture at 0xD7B3D entry. Confirms corporalmass-pipeline.

facts.title: Renderer vtable 0x45C8A0 fog slots
facts.fact: Fog applier 0x126A30 renderer O = [[[0x50C958]+0x18]+8] (0x50C958 = game object; game+0x18 zeroed in ctor 0x161510, writer not found). O vtable = 0x45C8A0 (renderer built by sub_35C20; identity inferred): +0x124 = 0x373D0 SetFogMode(0/1/2), +0x12C = 0x37400 (fog colour ptr), +0x134 = 0x37450 (float pair; return 0x126AAA patched by ma2_pc_fog_distance), +0x13C = 0x374B0 (float pair), +0x144 = 0x37500 SetSkyFogBand. Mode: block+0xF8 1->1, 2->2, other->0 via sub_81350 (callers 0x1236D0, 0x16165A, 0x20EC20, 0x126A2A) -> 0x373D0 stores it at [[0x524AD0]+0x2438] and calls 0x3AEB0, branching ==1 path A / ==2 0x3AFB4 / else. Path A pushes state ids 0x5C (val 1), 0x8A, 0x5D (val 3), 0x5E via helpers 0x3BB80 (id in ecx) / 0x3BA00. The ids are Xbox render-state ids (see xdk-render-state-fog: ids are XDK D3DRS indices, TABLE LINEAR). Open: what 0x3BB80/0x3BA00 emit; paths B/C of 0x3AEB0; 0x524AD0 identity. UPDATE 2026-10-24: helpers emit nothing; modes 1 and 2 both LINEAR (fog-helpers-emit-nv2a).

facts.title: Repair-on-kill amount and difficulty scale table 0x4EBA00
facts.fact: Repair-on-kill amount obj+0x1B0 is read as an INT (cvtsi2ss at 0x131FB0); 0 skips; repair = trunc(int x scale) per zone, clamped. Only caller of 0x131EB0 is 0x131DBA in the destroyed-event 0x131D6C (destroyed obj = arg, killer = eax). Catalog candidates at code offset 432 (+0x1B0) are class-specific: MAEffect Blast damage (9A5E5C92, uint hp) best fit; MABuildingDestroyed.DamageDuration, MASnatchItDataCore.PickupSndID, MACorporealDestroyed.DamageAmount (float; unlikely). Runtime class unknown (trace); mapping inferred. Scale: default 1.0; human-killer scale used only if [sub_18F10+0x69]==0 and killer owner classid ([killer+4]+0x28)==0x4EAED0 (MAPlayer). sub_0016B0C4 = table lookup: float table 0x4EBA00 [row 0.7][level 0.3] (16 B per row); eax==4 -> level = singleton [0x524A6C]+0x24+0x0C (>=4 -> 1). Kill path uses row 4: level 0 = 2.0, 1 = 1.0, 2 = 0.75, 3 = 0.5 (filled at runtime by sub_0016A580; level likely = difficulty, inferred). Note MAProjectile.RiderAttachAngle slice record lists code offset 432 not 400 (breaks slice+0x20 rule): check. The attacker is the damage record +0x0C link on the TakeDamage path; there is no last-attacker field on the victim. See damage-attacker-is-rec-plus-0c-link-no-last-attacker-on-victim-13200f-not-kill-credit and powerup-collect-rule-game-side-armour-only-when-damaged-weapon-only-when-useful.

facts.title: MAEnvironment +0x20 rule holds; apply 0x1C0 is not CoolingWaterway
facts.fact: RESOLVES menv-unread-props-sweep's conflict: reader sub_00124CC1 runs on the +0x20 sub-object (vtable 0x46DA30 slot 1; ctor 0x123173 stores vptrs 0x46DA38 @+0, 0x46DA30 @+0x20, 0x46DA28 @+0x24; 0x46DA28 slot 3 also = reader, +0x24 use unresolved). Ctor default blocks at entity+0x78/+0x88 = reader+0x58 LightAmbientColor / +0x68 DirectionalLightColor (0x20 shift). So the +0x20 rule HOLDS: CoolingWaterway reader+0x1C0 = entity+0x1E0; DamageLava reader 0x1F0 = entity+0x210; SpeedShallow 0x23C = entity+0x25C. Writer/saver sub_00123746 = 0x46DA30 slot 0. Apply sub_001234D6 is in primary vtable 0x46DA38 slot 11 (this = entity): the wiki's apply reads 0x1C0 is entity+0x1C0 = reader+0x1A0, NOT CoolingWaterway, so the AI-feed fact (menv-airange-is-colour-channel context) may mislabel the field (flag). Global [0x524A70] (accessor sub_00018E90) is NOT the environment: it points to static object 0x52A8C0 (vptr 0x476F1C) built by sub_0016A580 (the same function that fills table 0x4EBA00) -> likely a game-rules/difficulty settings object (inferred). MAMech updates sub_001B3D93/sub_001B42E5 use it. Water-zone consumer still not located; clue: sub_001B42E5 fld [ebx+0x210] at 0x1B4D70/0x1B56E5 after ebx rebinding at 0x1B4D1E (would be DamageLava). 0x360-byte entity factory sub_00122FF5 (no direct callers). facts.title: +0x1A8 is a class collision: MAMover rider vector vs MAPowerUp flag dword
facts.fact: MAMover family (MAMech/MATank/MATurret/MAVehicle/MAFlyer/MAProjectile): +0x1A8/+0x1AC = begin/end of a 12-byte rider-entry vector (sub_EB12B: count=(end-begin)/0xC, uid at entry+8). MAPowerUp (vtable 0x470200, factory 0x13100A, classid global [0x4EB04C], descriptor 0x4B03C0): +0x1A8 = flag dword; bit 0x02 = collected/consumed latch (tested then set once in sub_131D6C, arg esi = the pickup, eax = collector), bit 0x01 tested next; +0x1AC passed to virtual vt+0x124. The gate fact sub_E064A (classid [0x4EB04C] with +0x1A8 bit4) is MAPowerUp bit 0x10. MAMech slot 119 (0x10063D) reads the contacted pickup's +0x1A8 bit 0x02 before calling 0x131D6C(pickup, mech); expected MAPowerUp slice offset 0x188. Annotate t01a/t01b rider-table facts 'MAMover-family only'. Open: classid [0x4EAF44] (descriptor 0x4AECF0, factory 0xEC09D) tested at 0x100681; MAPowerUp bit 0x01 meaning; vt+0x124 use of +0x1AC. UPDATE 2026-10-24: classid [0x4EAF44] = MAProjectile (classid-4eaf44-maprojectile). CORRECTION 2026-10-24: 131D6C is a free function (powerup-notify-0x131d6c).

facts.title: 0x50E304 is movers-with-riders; 0x50E2C8 holds hash keys
facts.fact: CORRECTION of water-body-and-pointer-lists: 0x50E304 is NOT a water list. It is the list of MAMover instances that HAVE RIDERS: helper 0xE9AFD pushes this only if a 12-byte rider entry in +0x1A8.+0x1AC has nonzero uid at +8; only caller 0xE9A5F = MAMover vtable 0x467A70 slot 7 (+0x1C), an init/activation virtual (ctor 0xD702D). 0x50E2C8 elements are HASH KEYS: walker 0xDBAC0 (only caller world tick 0x15D4C7) looks each up via 0xB4F70 (pointer-keyed chained hash, container [0x161B4B+0xA4], buckets +0x34/+0x38, returns [node+8]); result obj [obj+0x94]+0x100 float4 -> virtual slot 15 (+0x3C); then 0xA1FA0 clears the list. No direct appender to 0x50E2C8 (all refs inside 0xDBAC0): append is indirect or never happens in this build, conflicting with the 'runtime-filled' note (inferred). Needs runtime write watch.

facts.title: Zone record +0xC codes written by builder 0x16C019

facts.title: Fog helpers are leaf list updaters; fog modes 1 AND 2 are both LINEAR
facts.fact: Helpers 0x3BB80/0x3BA00 emit NOTHING: leaf list updaters on the fog-state table at G+0x18. Flush 0x3BC10 (caller 0x3B2F0) dispatches keys; key 0x8A (fog colour) -> table 0x4181A0 -> 0x40C600 writes RAW NV2A words (header 0x000402A8 + colour with bytes 0/2 swapped; cursor 0x41BC68). Keys 0x5C-0x5F are NOT D3D8 RS numbers: they OR 0x2000 into dirty word 0x41BC70 and cache the value (drain not found). Keys < 0x5C index table 0x45B0E0. Fog-mode table 0x3AEB0: mode 1 -> 0x5C=1, 0x8A=[G+0x243C] colour, 0x5D=3 (TABLE LINEAR), 0x5E=[G+0x2440] start, 0x5F=[G+0x2444] end; modes 2 and 3 -> same but 0x5E=0.0, 0x5F=1.0 (0x493A60) fixed; other modes -> 0x5C=0 (fog off). So modes 1 and 2 are both LINEAR (not EXP/EXP2): mode 1 over FogStart/FogEnd, mode 2/3 over fixed 0.1 (meaning inferred). CORRECTION: 0x3AEB0 never calls 0x3B0A0; its callers are 0x37450, 0x37473, 0x374B0, 0x44700, 0x44762; entry routes 0x373D0 (vt 0x45C8A0 +0x124), 0x37400, 0x37450, 0x37473. UPDATE 2026-10-24: 0x2000 flag not tested by immediate; cull-face emitters not fog (fog-0x2000-flag-negative).

facts.title: 0x14524D is the trigger RE-ARM (only clears +0x88)
facts.fact: Sub 0x14524D only CLEARS fired byte +0x88 (AL always 0; earlier 'sets +0x88=al' wording is wrong). Clears only if TriggerEnabled +0x89 != 0 and one of: (+0x9D != 0 and float +0xA8 < 0.0; sign inferred), (+0xAC != 0 and +0xAD == 0), or (+0x9C != 0). ecx = trigger; incoming eax ignored; ret 4 (one stack arg, not decoded). Called from all 14 evaluators (recomp_0032.c:19369, recomp_0033.c:3999/4703/21773, recomp_0034.c:330/954/1631/2189/2648, recomp_0043.c:5432/6726/7615/8220/8979). Both calls sit in an earlier gate (esi != 0 and eax == [0x4EAF38]); B4F70 = UID hash lookup; C6FBF returns 0 on both exits so the gate always falls through (early exit 0x145499 unreachable as recompiled; check raw bytes). facts.title: RadialFalloffLookup is generated at runtime: texel = (1-r2)^2
facts.fact: The 64x64 RadialFalloffLookup texture is GENERATED at runtime: sub_52E60 creates '\Renderer\LightMapMgr\RadialFalloffLookup' (create 0x52EB0 via sub_435B0(64,64,1,6,0); '.RadialFalloffLookup32Bit' fallback at 0x52F08 only if the first create fails), sub_53DB0 fills it (y-loop 0x53F9A around x-loop 0x53FBB, swizzle mask 0x53FA8). Cached in [0x524AC0]. Formula: dx = 2x/(w-1)-1, dy = 2y/(h-1)-1, r2 = dx^2+dy^2, v = (1-r2)^2 if r2 < 1 else 0, texel = (int)(255*v + 0.5) (constants 255.0 0x493AF0, 0.5 0x493A5C, 1.0 0x493A60). NOT smoothstep: editor falloff should use (1-r2)^2 (corrects t12:1954). Link to id 80679000 inferred. MaterialLight / MaterialRadialBlur have their own lookups (MaterialLight = plateau).
