facts.title: Terrain lit pass uses all 4 NV2A stages (T0 colour map, T1/T2 detail, T3 ground light map); micro pass separate; a third ground texture on PC needs a new pixel path
facts.fact: Verified-in-game traces (UC/KF, program n738, 7 stages): T0 colour map (alpha = layer mix), T1 TerrainDetailMap, T2 TerrainDetailMap 1, T3 = 512x512 camera-window ground light map built each frame from the static A8L8 MAEnvironment LightMapName lightmap; V1 = sun, c0 = DetailBlend; out = 4*lerp(T2,T1,T0.a)*T0.rgb*L, L = V1.rgb*V1.a*T3.a + T3.rgb. Maps without a lightmap (New River City) run the same program without T3. The static decode of 0x4A4760 shows V0 as light; the traced program is what runs. Micro pass: separate draw, T0/T1 micro maps (+T2), dst' = 2*src*dst, only blocks within ~128 m. Draws per block: one base pass per 128 m render block (16 cells x 8 m, (CellSize+1)^2 vertices, CellSize 16 in all 60 worlds) plus one micro draw for near blocks (medium confidence). PC side: pixel_program(const Nv2aGpuState*) in kernel/nv2a_gpu_d3d11.c:422 builds a GpuPixelKey (words[0] use_rc, [4] alpha_test, [10] shader_depth), chooses pixel_main/pixel_clamped, called at:1733, gated by RECOMP_PIXEL_SPECIALIZE (researcher read kit/source/game/src/kernel; PC Release lineage 5508c574 unchecked); a PC-only extension (more than 2 ground textures) needs a key bit in pixel_program and extra SRVs beyond the 4 stages; editor-side hook targets Renderer:set_terrain (render.cpp:1026) and terrain_ps_ (render.cpp:519).
facts.how_to_use: Open: colour map resolution/format (wiki only: terrain colour/detail maps are DXT1 x125 / DXT5 x30 / DXT3 x15 in the archives; base UV spans the whole map) and its loader; whether the game issues exactly one base + one micro draw per block; per-texture Nv2aGpuState stage count on the PC side.

facts.title: The game's glow is a bloom post-process: mask = framebuffer ALPHA written only by draws whose colour-mask includes alpha; chain 640x480 -> 320x240 -> 160x120 -> 4 blur passes -> max-blend into 320x240 -> added to the frame
facts.fact: Decoded from trace bdp4far_f1_trace_raw.txt lines 6178-7741 (rcdec.py). (1) Mask: material_color_shift writes colorshift0_bloom x base.a (rgb = 2x(V0xT + C0.rgb x T.a); bloom values 0.1.1.0 in retail, e.g. 0.25/0.5/0.73/1.0); COMPLEX writes colorshift0_bloom x multi.g + colorshift1_bloom x multi.b + specular_bloom x multi.r x cube.a; specular_mask writes specular_bloom x mask(base.a) x cube.a (specular_bloom 0.0.2 in Mission_02 materials). All other draws (colour-mask 00010101) leave alpha alone. (2) Chain: 640x480 frame -> 320x240 (4 taps = 4x4 box; rgb x alpha via blend SRC_ALPHA/ZERO) -> 160x120 (4x4 box) -> 4 blur passes V,H,V,H (taps at +-1.5 and +-0.5 texels, weights 0x3F, 0x3F?, 0x7F, 0x7F constants = 0.247/0.498; ~1.49 gain per pass, 8-bit clamp each pass) -> upsampled and max-blended (blend eq 0x8008 MAX) into the 320x240 target -> added to the 640x480 frame (blend CONSTANT_COLOR/CONSTANT_COLOR, eq ADD; blend colour not in the trace, assumed 1). Surfaces 0x2000 (320x240), 0x4D000 and 0x5FC00 (160x120). The editor implements it as View > Bloom (commit cdaf11c on retail11-render). Confidence: high for the chain, medium for the gains. Side findings: the dropship mtb (Vmil_Dropship_Talon_Ale_WS) has no MAModSubObjectDiffuse (class 0A72F444 appears only on mech light_entry nodes, with colour 005F6400 etc.); no node_facing nodes in Mission_02/04/16 models.
facts.how_to_use: Open: blend colour of the final composite (assumed 1); tap order inside the blur passes; what writes alpha for CONSTANT_ALPHA-blended (8003/8004) draws 'C0.a x T0.a' (13 draws per frame, likely glow cards/sprites).

facts.title: Game bloom chain, independently traced (Mission_02 and Mission_04): bloom source = scene.rgb x FRAMEBUFFER ALPHA (not a luminance threshold); the final composite blend colour is 00FFFFFF, i.e. additive x1.0
facts.fact: Chain: (1) scene 640x480 A8R8G8B8 -> 320x240 RT with a 3-stage 4-tap box combiner, blend SRC_ALPHA/ZERO; (2) 320x240 -> 160x120; (3) two blur ping-pongs at 160x120 (3-stage, s1 constant 0x7F00003F, each pass gains ~x1.4); (4) merge into the 320x240 RT with ONE/ONE and blend equation 8008 = MAX; (5) composite onto the 640x480 scene: quad tex 320x240 bilinear, blend 8001/8001 CONSTANT_COLOR with blend colour 00FFFFFF, eq ADD. Scene alpha > 0 on 9% of pixels (M02) / 1.5% (M04), max 193 / 116; final bloom RT mean (1.1, 1.6, 1.3) in M02 and ~0 in M04. Confirms the retail11 decode of the same chain and RESOLVES its open item 'blend colour of the final composite (assumed 1)': it is 00FFFFFF. Note: retail11 counted 4 blur passes (V,H,V,H); this trace counts two ping-pongs (consistent: 2 ping-pongs = 4 passes).
facts.how_to_use: Open: which materials/effects write framebuffer alpha (colour-mask in their draws); the 13 CONSTANT_ALPHA draws per frame.

facts.title: Bloom mask (framebuffer alpha) formulas per material, from rcdec of the m02bloom2 draws: material_color_shift alpha = C0.a x T0.a x V0.a with V0.a = 0.5 and no x2 (high confidence)
facts.fact: Stages: s0 'T0.a = T0.a x V0.a', s1 'R0.a = C0.a x T0.a', C0.a = colorshift0_bloom (0x7F for 0.5). Checks: M02 roof glow strips alpha max 63/255; M04 blue bars 116/255. Editor fixed in commit 5159104. specular_mask draws (medium confidence): alpha = T2.a (cube alpha) x C0.a x T0.a, C0.a = specular_bloom exactly (M02 C0.a values 0.098 x20, 0.2 x48, 0.149 x2, 0.5 x16, 0 x43). COMPLEX (mech paint) draws: alpha = R0.a x C0.a + R1.a x C1.a (C0.a = C1.a = 0x7F) + cube.a x T3.a x C0.a, no V0.a. Resolves the open item 'which materials write framebuffer alpha' for these three material types; the 13 CONSTANT_ALPHA 'C0.a x T0.a' draws are consistent with the color_shift formula.

facts.title: MAModSubObjectBlend (vtable 0x471610, ctor 0x13C315, update 0x13CBB6): per-tick alpha ramp cur += dt x AlphaLevelDelta x sign, clamped to [MinAlphaLevel, MaxAlphaLevel], PingPong flips the sign at a clamp (triangle wave); property keys are CRC32(name)^0xFFFFFFFF
facts.fact: Key->field (hash-matched): 7CBB9EB0 MaxAlphaLevel +9C, 3CF4E6C6 MinAlphaLevel +A0, 37A15C72 AlphaLevelDelta +A4, 6BEC1C07 CurAlphaLevel +A8, D1858164 CurSign +AC, A0018DB3 RandomModifier +B0, 2A7466CD OrigAlpha +B4, 68172E7C PingPong +B9; also Loop +BA, UseRandomModifier +BB, GetOrigAlpha +B8, StartDelay +44. Runtime: +BC=Max clamp, +C0=Min clamp, +C4=delta, +C8=current, +CC=sign, +D0=random modifier, +D4=orig/restart value. Stepper sub_001408F7: cur += dt(global 0x4E2428) x delta x sign, clamp, returns true when clamped. On clamp: PingPong sign *= -1 (0x493AF4 = -1.0); else Loop resets cur to +D4. With UseRandomModifier, value += rand[0,1) x RandomModifier. Value clamped to [0,1] (sub_0003C400) and stored as float at +4 of the 12-byte struct at target+0x100 (target = owner vtable +0x78); struct dword 0 bits 3-5 = blend mode, set to 2 (alpha blend) when GetOrigAlpha is false, left at 3 (additive) when true. Example Mission_13b Env_SkyHesperus_02 light_rayNN: Min 0, Max 1, Delta 0.25/s, PingPong, saved Cur 0.612 => triangle 0.1.0, period 8 s, ray is near 0 only briefly. The ray keys 43E08AE7/EE4B7833 (100) and E0B25EA0 (1) are not in the Blend save list (base-class keys, meaning unknown). Mode numbering 2=alpha / 3=additive follows the sky alpha-mode note (medium confidence).

facts.title: MAModSubObjectUVAnimate: property keys DB7ACEF3 = Uspeed (+C0), 5DEEBC5D = Vspeed (+C4); sub_00108384 multiplies them by a factor from the owner entity's velocity along its forward axis (sign flips when moving backwards), so it behaves as a speed-driven tread scroller
facts.fact: Hash-matched keys. sub_00108384 reads the owner's velocity, dots it with a transformed (0,0,1), flips the sign when negative, and passes Uspeed x factor and Vspeed x factor on to the UV target. A static owner (sky) would therefore give factor ~0; the plain time-based scroll path was not found. Defaults Uspeed = Vspeed = 1.0 in the ctor (0x10808E).

facts.title: Used-by link keys (editor used_by, checked on Mission_05): which property links which object to which
facts.fact: MAAction* holds ActionEntity / MarkerUID / cinemaID (the unit, marker or cinema it acts on). MoeEntityReference holds ReferenceUID (a condition input of MATriggerLogic, or a unit watched by MATriggerDestroyed); its owner is its parent trigger. MAEvent (AI order) holds TriggerID (the trigger that starts it) and belongs to the unit through parent MAAIGroup -> unit. MADefend DefendUID (marker), MAFollow FollowUID, MAAttack AttackUID reach units/markers; the order owner is the behaviour's parent MAEvent. In Mission_05 a tank is reached only through MAEvent chains (4 follow orders, started by triggers TD - Hand Base, TL - ComeOnIn!, TT - Redirect Defenders, TT - Guard Orders).

facts.title: (1) The ground map T3 is a camera window about 1245 m wide (2.43 m per texel at M16), fitted by FFT correlatio
facts.fact: (1) The ground map T3 is a camera window about 1245 m wide (2.43 m per texel at M16), fitted by FFT correlation of the stored 128x128 lightmap alpha onto the game 512x512 T3; x window 810.2055, rows 0-45 empty beyond the north edge. (2) At the road (1740.6,1387.4) game T3.a is 0.16-0.24 against stored lm.a 0.137: no discrepancy. (3) Slab pre-pass prog 0A624: R0 = (2T0-1).(2V0-1) x T3.a x C0.rgb + T3.rgb, times V1.rgb; alpha = T2.b (64x64 LUT) x C0.a x 2 = 0.173 at the traced pixel; output 20,17,15 equals the editor light divided by 2. (4) Overlay prog 08C21 with EQUAL z: out = fog(2 x (FB.rgb x T0.rgb + mask.g x colorshift0 + mask.b x colorshift1) + multi.r x shin_strength (0.698) x FB.a); no cube lookup. The editor spec used multi.r x cube.a (about 0), giving 0.47x; with A = 0.173 constant it gives 0.86x. OPEN: FB.a may depend on view angle; a g4 framebuffer dump was requested. (5) The final 12,11,11 is a dark asphalt texel (multi.r about 0). the raw M16 T3 file has whole-map alpha mean 0.788, i.e. the 0.79 in the earlier entry is a whole-map mean, not the road texel.

facts.title: Culture seed: the 'per-cell' and 'per-texel' facts describe the same thing; the seed is per culture-map texel
facts.fact: RULING: sub_001801F6 runs once per grid cell and the cell IS the culture-map texel: 0x180256-0x18026B builds s=(texX<<16)^gen[+0x2C]^texZ and calls sub_0001DA00 (reseed). culture-seed-and-placement-order says '(cx<<16)^gen[+0x2C]^cz' for the same call; cx,cz = texX,texZ. The disassembly-addressed culture-texel-seed is the precise one. gen[+0x2C] has no store anywhere (culture-gen-2c-unparsed); its value is unknown. In culture-generator the literal text 'cy' means texZ.

facts.title: Map > Environment and Time of day/weather: what each control writes to MAEnvironment/MASky2 and how the game uses it (sun, shadows, fog, sky picker, Look/Night, lit windows = IsNightTime, weather = PrecipEffectID/EnableRain, lightning = LightFlash, flash timing)
facts.fact: Source: editor kit/source/game/src/app/app_tabs.cpp, app_weather.cpp, core/weather.h (research 2026-10-23 citing recomp sub_00124CC1 reader, sub_00126060 update, sub_0012693E precip start, sub_001263F8 lightning). the source only; no run. Writes are HIGH (read from code); game-side effects MEDIUM-HIGH (cited in weather.h, match wiki menv-lightning-night / isnighttime-buildings-only). Fields are MAEnvironment unless noted. [Sun direction / Sun height] write DirectionalLightDirection = (sin yaw*cos elev, -sin elev, cos yaw*cos elev); marks the lightmap stale. [Update shadows / Update shadows for the new sun] re-bakes the scenario lightmap from the sun (editor bake; the game uses the stored lightmap as its ground light map). [Fog distance] FogStart, FogEnd (m). [Height fog band] FogBottom, FogTop (m); the game uses the band only when FogMode = 2 (editor warns when ground sits inside it). [Fog colour] FogColor (u32 ARGB, alpha byte kept). [Sky picker] copies Corporal3DObj (sky model), CorporalMTB, SkyTerrainSkyScale, SkyTerrainSkyOffset, position and heading from a retail world that uses that sky into MASky2; SkyFogTop/Bottom left alone (wiki skies-masky2). [Night checkbox + Look list] apply a whole LOOK copied from a retail world: sun, ambient, fog and shadow colours, fog distances, reflection map (EnvironmentMapName) and the MASky2 sky. The look also sets IsNightTime to the retail world's own value (look.lit): lit for Go Commando, Ill Wind, Bogged Down; not lit for New River City, Witch Cauldron, Cold dusk. The Night box itself does not write IsNightTime; the picked look does. [Lit building windows] IsNightTime (0/1). Game: only MABuilding reads it. It darkens nothing: Mission 06a is flagged 1 with a warm sun, Mission 12 is dark and flagged 0. [Weather: None/Rain/Snow/Dust] write PrecipEffectID and EnableRain (the game starts the precipitation object each frame when EnableRain is set; PrecipEffectID 0 = nothing). The disc has only two MAPrecipitation templates: 31780 Env_Snow_Blowing (Missions 10, 11a, 11b) and 31516 Env_DustStorm_Wst. RAIN is not a game template: saved as the snow template 31780, plus the scenario archive carries a rain streak particle (.mgparticle XML, about 70 KB) in place of the snow effect's particle. On load, a snow world whose archive carries that particle reads as rain again. On Missions 10/11 as the base level the game's own snow files may win, so rain can show as snow. Editor's in-memory rain id is 990001. Snow/Dust add the effect files to the scenario if the base level lacks them. [Lightning flashes] write LightFlash, SkyFlash and EnableLightning together. Game: LightFlash drives the flashes (bursts up to MaxFlashes, next burst FlashTimeMin.FlashTimeMax ms later) and ThunderCueID (0 in every retail world, so no thunder); EnableLightning is stored only (a trigger action sets it; nothing reads it). The flash is a light on mechs, vehicles and people, not a ground/sky change. [Flash timing 'every N to M s'] FlashTimeMin, FlashTimeMax stored in ms (UI seconds, 1.60). The game picks the next burst with a remainder by (max - min), so equal values crash it; the editor forces min < max (min 1-59, max min+1.60) and fixes it again on save (weather:to_game). Tags for the wiki section: Map > Environment; Map > Time of day and weather. NOTE: the game reads only LightFlash; SkyFlash and EnableLightning are never 1 in retail and are not tested (see lightning-gate-is-lightflash-only-.).
facts.how_to_use: Part of 'How the editor maps to the game' (see page t16_editor_to_game). Editor writes read from code (HIGH unless marked); game-side effects carry the cited facts' confidence. Open items are listed inside.

facts.title: Terrain > Paint: textures 1/2 = TerrainDetailMap pair mixed by colour-map alpha (255 = T1, 0 = T2); pattern size = TerrainDetailMult; close-up = micro detail; 3+ textures = PC ground layers; tint = colour-map RGB; boundaries = terrain type map
facts.fact: Source: editor kit/source/game/src/app/app_paint.cpp (header comment + enable/disable_ground_layers, fill_ground, tint_ui, boundaries_ui). the source only; no run. What each control writes: HIGH (read from code). Game-side effect: MEDIUM-HIGH, cites existing wiki facts. [Ground textures: Texture 1 / Texture 2] MATerrain TerrainDetailMap and 'TerrainDetailMap 1' (paths stored as \Terrain\<name>.tif). The brush writes the COLOUR MAP ALPHA (TerrainBaseMap tif): alpha 255 = Texture 1, alpha 0 = Texture 2, in between mixes (fill_ground: layer 0 -> 255, layer 1 -> 0). Matches the game: lerp(T2,T1,T0.a). Works in every game version. [Pattern size] TerrainDetailMult, TerrainDetailMult1: how many times each texture repeats across the whole map (wiki terrain-detail-uv-repeats). [Close-up detail / Close-up size] TerrainMicroDetailMap0/1 + TerrainMicroDetailTiling0/1. Not painted: two fine textures averaged over everything within about 128 m; the game draws them only when BOTH maps are set (wiki terrain-microdetail-pass). [Add a texture (3rd and more, up to 8)] switches the scenario to the P4 GROUND LAYERS (PC build only; core/ground_layers.h): per-texture weights stored in the scenario, starting as the colour map alpha mix so nothing changes visibly; each layer has its own repeats (layers 0/1 take TerrainDetailMult/Mult1). The original Xbox game and older PC builds show only Texture 1 and 2 there. The p4 exe logs '[TERRAIN-LAYERS] N layers . t3 512x512'. [Remove texture / Back to 2 textures] bakes the pair's share of the weights back into the colour map alpha, so the map is a plain retail pair again. [Colour tint] the colour map RGB, which multiplies the textures. [Tint the whole map with this colour] sets every colour-map RGB, alpha kept. [Repaint ground colours from height] regenerates the colour-map RGB from height/slope (procedural colour map, theme colours), keeps the alpha (the texture mix). [Show it in its own colours] (texture brush option): also moves the colour map under the brush to neutral, because ground = texture x colour map. CAUTION: the editor comment on tint_ui says '4 x detail x colour'; the traced law is 8 x TerrainDetailBlend, so any 'neutral = 1/(4 x DetailBlend)' value in code is 2x the traced neutral unless the editor lighting carries the other factor. [Boundaries: Playable / Border / Out of bounds / Water] writes the GROUND-TYPE LAYER (the map's terrain-type grid, 'typemap'; storage record not checked, MEDIUM). Meaning from the editor help: spawn points, vehicle pads, flags and objectives must stand on Playable (or Water) ground; bots never walk onto Out of bounds ground; Border is a band round the arena; Special is water/waterway inside the arena. Overlay colours: clear playable, orange border, red out of bounds, blue water. [Make the whole map playable] sets every cell Playable. Tags for the wiki section: Terrain > Paint > Texture; Terrain > Paint > Colour tint; Terrain > Paint > Boundaries. WITHDRAWN: the '2x too bright on the lit path' caution is wrong. The editor's albedo carries 4 x DetailBlend and its ambient/sun are already x2, so editor total = the game's 8 x C0.a; neutral 1/(4 x DetailBlend) gives the texture's own colour in both. The law stays 8 x TerrainDetailBlend total gain including the light doubling.

facts.title: Map tab basics: Name/Author/Description, Kind, Built on (base retail level), Size, What the player starts , Game types, Check scenario (graphics memory ~58 MB crash limit), Sky and fog colour
facts.fact: Source: editor kit/source/game/src/app/app_tabs.cpp (tab_map, sky_picker). the source only; no run. Writes HIGH where the code names the field; storage places not checked are marked. [Name / Author / Description] scenario info the game shows in its map or mission list (stored with the scenario; exact record not checked, MEDIUM). [Kind] multiplayer map (played against bots) or mission (enemies use the campaign AI); decided when the map is created, shown read-only on the tab. [Built on] the retail level (archive) the map copies: its ground textures, lighting and buildings come from there; the scenario file refers to that base. Graphics memory counts the base theme's textures and models plus anything placed from other levels. [Size] read-only from the terrain (size_x x size_z in m; cell scale from TerrainWorldScale, 8 m per cell in retail). [What the player starts in] MARoot's player configuration container: on foot, Battle Armor (Mission 2), or already inside a 'Mech or tank (Missions 5 and 13). Saving adds the model files that body needs. [Game types] (multiplayer only) the types list the map supports; each type needs its own objects: spawn points for every type, flags for Capture the Flag, bases for Snatch It; the editor re-syncs the spawn groups when a type is ticked or unticked. [Check scenario] runs the validator (the game would not load or would break); Test runs it first. It also reports graphics memory: real levels use about 25 MB of the 64 MB; past about 58 MB the game crashes while loading. [Sky] writes MASky2 (model, mtb, scale, offset, position, heading) from a retail world that uses the sky. Picking a sky by hand makes the look read 'Custom'. [Use this sky's fog colour] copies FogColor from the level the sky comes ; off = the base level's own FogColor. [Fog colour swatch / Advanced: fog colour numbers] both write FogColor (u32 ARGB, alpha kept); the numbers (R,G,B 0-255) sit under Advanced. Tags: Map > Scenario; Map > Game types; Map > Sky; Map > Check.

facts.title: Lightning flash colour writes LightningColorRed/Green/Blue
facts.fact: (1) E1 RAIN DRAWS MAGENTA IN THE PC GAME. The editor's rain was the game's snow particle file rewritten (weather.cpp rain_particle: orient_to_velocity true, rate 600, gravity 10, life 1.1 s) using the same snow textures. In the game the streaks fall but the screen goes magenta and gets worse over time. Two editor-side tweaks failed: no orient_to_velocity at rate 600 (big magenta triangles + flakes), orient on at rate 120 (big magenta quads). CONFIDENCE: observation HIGH; CAUSE UNKNOWN (LOW). Hypotheses: the PC renderer's path for velocity-oriented particles binds no texture and draws the magenta fallback, or a scenario-shipped .mgparticle looks up its texture/material differently from retail packs. The source comment says rain was OK in game on 2026-10-23, so a game-exe regression since then is possible (LOW). (2) DECISION for tonight: Rain now exports as plain SNOW; the magenta particle renderer bug is a known issue for the report, to get at most one 2 h timebox after the Environment tab build. So 'Weather: Rain' no longer writes the rewritten rain particle: it writes the snow template (31780) and the game shows snow. (3) [Lightning flashes > Flash colour]: a colour swatch + picker under 'Lightning flashes' that writes LightningColorRed/Green/Blue (0-255, default white 255,255,255). Game: the flash light's colour (MAEnvironment LightningColor B/G/R at 0x18E/0x18F/0x190, wiki menv-weather-layout). Editor-side write: HIGH; in-game look of a non-white flash: not tested. Tags: Map > Time of day and weather > Weather; Map > Time of day and weather > Lightning flashes. FIXED: the magenta came from the editor renaming the particle effect ('MA2SE Rain'); keeping the snow effect's name fixes it (master 2b008eb), and Rain exports as rain again. See particle-effect-found-by-name-renamed-rain-effect-drew-magenta-fixed-2b008eb-retail-has-no-rain-effect.

facts.title: Cutscenes tab: Preview writes nothing (5 s fallback); 'Played by' creates MATriggerTimer/box + MAActionActivateCinema cinemaID; shot fields write MAFreeCameraController triggerInit/triggerExit, CameraDuration, bSkipTo; Add/Delete shot behaviour
facts.fact: Format: control -> writes -> game use -> status. 1. facts.title: Paint: 'Show it in its own colours' neutral 1/(4 x DetailBlend) is RIGHT (editor albedo 4 x C0.a with light x2 = the game's 8 x C0.a, which includes the light doubling); Plants paints the MATerrainInfo culture map one level step per hit (scatter live, undo works); colour-tint eyedropper is UI only
facts.fact: The editor's terrain albedo is 4 x C0.a x detail x colour and its ambient and sun terms are already x2 (render.cpp tps: 'albedo already carries 4 x DetailBlend and amb / sun are x2'), so editor total = 2 x L x 4 x C0.a = the game's 8 x C0.a. The game's 8x INCLUDES the light doubling; the colour map's own factor is 4 x DetailBlend, so colour 1/(4 x DetailBlend) gives the texture's own colour in both. The wiki law stays: total gain on detail x colour with the light x2 = 8 x TerrainDetailBlend. can close as no change. (2) NEW [Terrain > Paint the ground > Plants]: paints the culture map in MATerrainInfo (key 89FB5118; u16 level fields cultureBF<i>Shift/NBits), one level step per hit, written back at the end of the stroke; the scatter regenerates live; undo works (levels checked before/after/undo). Game side: the culture type's GenerationTemplate is scattered by level/top x Density per km2 within StopFade of the eye (Env Grass: 75 m, 800 per km2), consistent with wiki culture-level-sampling-and-count-formula (level = ((T & mask) >> shift)/(2^NBits - 1), count = floor(f) + (rand < frac f)). Editor draws plants only within the type's StopFade of the camera, as the game does. CONFIDENCE: editor write HIGH; game match by the same rule MEDIUM-HIGH. (3) [Colour tint > Pick a colour from the map] (2beb920): eyedropper (next click on the ground takes its colour, then switches off; Alt+click while tinting). UI only, no new field. Tags: Terrain > Paint > Colour tint; Terrain > Paint > Plants.

facts.title: Traps: Add Capture the Flag copies the base level's whole 187-object CTF set at its own positions (spawns 6/6 -> 18/18); a vehicle pad is a 5-6 object spawner group ('Units in total 0' still spawned); ticking a game type after Create adds no spawns; Check does not warn about no pads with on-foot starts; Save moves the file to Documents\MechAssault 2\Scenarios
facts.fact: (1) [Game proof] A multiplayer map built only through the editor UI plays in the PC game: 6 Red + 6 Blue spawns at opposite ends, Team Destruction ran to 'Blue Team Wins!' with bots (kill feed, timer), vehicle pads work (player starts on foot beside a pad with an Atlas on it). Check scenario passed (238 objects, 2.8 MB, graphics 23 of 64 MB). (2) [Players > Add Capture the Flag] copies a whole set of 187 objects FROM THE BASE LEVEL (Bogged Down) at that level's own positions, not at the map's team ends: flags/bases land in the base level's places, spawn counts jump 6/6 -> 18/18 (the base level's CTF spawn rings come along) and dozens of helper markers appear. Retail CTF towers (tall red/blue beacons) then stand all over the map in Team Destruction too; whether they sit in a CTF-only mission-type group (so the game hides them in TD) is OPEN. Fix item for the helper: add only the flag, base and logic pieces at each team's ring. (3) [Players > Place vehicle pad (Atlas)] one pad is a group of 5-6 objects (4 clicks = 22 objects); its properties are a spawner: 'When it arrives: At the start', 'Units in total', 'At once', 'Seconds between' (11 s). 'Units in total 0' on a pad was read as 'nothing will appear', yet the Atlas appeared in game (meaning of 0 = unlimited is a guess, MEDIUM). Check does NOT warn when a map has no pads while players start on foot (the default Players start as: On foot). (4) [Map > Game types] ticking a type AFTER Create does not add that type's spawns ('Free-for-all 0' stayed); Create adds spawns for the types ticked then (6 per team in TD). Spawns had to be placed by hand (Players > Free-for-all > Place spawn point). (5) [Pickups] a power-up's weapon class properties PowerupWeaponFireClass0-2 now read 'Upgrades energy / ballistic / missile weapons' (labels from the catalog family names). (6) [Terrain > Water > Place water] digs a basin under the water and places it in one step (Ctrl+Z undoes both); [Paint > Texture] painting Texture 2 along the road and round the pond shows in the view and on the minimap; [Save] the game lists scenarios only in the scenario folder (Documents\MechAssault 2\Scenarios), so Save offers to move the file there. Tags: Players > Spawns; Players > Capture the Flag; Players > Vehicle pads; Map > Game types; Pickups; Terrain > Water; Save. facts.fact: Retail lightning data: LightFlash = 1 in only 4 of 60 worlds (Mission_08, Bogged Down, Ill Wind, Mountain High; MaxFlashes 4, FlashTime 3000-15000 ms, ThunderCueID 0). SkyFlash and EnableLightning are 1 in NONE. The editor's control writes all three together, so it writes two flags retail never sets. Game gate: only LightFlash (env+0x18D) is tested in the environment update (sub_00126060 at 0x1260AA -> sub_001263F8: ms clock [0x4E2430] vs burst timers +0x164/+0x168, in-burst +0x16C; sub_001262A2 starts a burst, sub_0012612E steps the flash light at env+0x358, colour from +0x18E). The flash light is created for every world in the env init (sub_001234D6). Not gated by precipitation, EnableRain or MaxFlashes (0 takes the other branch). The class constructor also defaults SkyFlash and LightFlash to 1 (sub_00123173 area), so retail data turns them OFF per world. Needs the player camera with a unit in frame, ideally with Ill Wind as a positive control. The wiki formula (L = V1.rgb x V1.a x T3.a + T3.rgb; T3.rgb = ambient x stored luminance, T3.a = sun/shadow mask) agrees with the editor's on paper, so an input differs; open, LOW. Tag: Environment > Weather > Lightning flashes; Environment > Sun. UPDATE: sub_00126060 runs the flash routine every frame while LightFlash != 0. Ctor defaults MaxFlashes 4, FlashTimeMin/Max 3000/15000, in-burst gaps 350/300 ms (+0x184/+0x188). A flash = light env+0x358 on for 40-80 ms (last of a burst 200-250 ms), so ~4% of 1 Hz screenshots catch one. The editor export now matches retail (LightFlash 1, SkyFlash 0, EnableLightning 0, MaxFlashes 4, white). The 'shade 2x darker' item is WITHDRAWN (snow veil; see editor-terrain-shading-matches-game-.). NOT SEEN: an editor map with the retail-matching values, 1196 frames at 80 ms (~9 bursts) in PC Release, showed no flash on the pilot. Do NOT record 'lightning works in game'. Decider: same method on Ill Wind / Bogged Down; if retail flashes, diff MAEnvironment; if not, the env+0x358 light does not reach the shader (runtime issue). RUNTIME GAP: retail Bogged Down does not flash in PC Release either; the editor export is not at fault. See lightning-is-a-pc-runtime-gap-retail-bogged-down-does-not-flash-in-pc-release.

facts.title: Editor terrain shading reproduces the game on an editor-made map once weather is removed: game lit/shaded/cast luma 32.7/14.7/11.0 vs editor 42.0/19.3/12.3; lit/shade contrast 2.2 vs 2.2, lit/cast 3.0 vs 3.4 (bake L = 0.35 + 0.65 N.L with cast-shadow mask A; shader L = amb x lm.r + sun x N.L x lm.a). The earlier '2x darker shade' came from a snow veil lifting dark pixels +15-20. Pitfall: never compare lighting with weather on
facts.fact: Without snow: game lit slope 32.7 / shaded slope 14.7 / cast shadow 11.0 luma (shadow RGB 10,16,7) vs editor 42.0 / 19.3 / 12.3 (11,18,8); lit/shade contrast 2.2 vs 2.2, lit/cast 3.0 vs 3.4. So the editor bake (L = 0.35 + 0.65 N.L, A = cast-shadow mask) plus the shader (L = amb x lm.r + sun x N.L x lm.a) reproduces the game's terrain shading on an editor-made map, as the wiki formula predicts. CONFIDENCE MEDIUM-HIGH (one pose pair, tracetools + RECOMP_CAM_SET). Pitfall for the wiki: no weather on lighting comparison pairs. (2) LIGHTNING timing (Environment > Weather > Lightning flashes; code HIGH): sub_00126060 calls the flash routine every frame whenever LightFlash (env+0x18D) != 0, no other gate. Class constructor defaults: MaxFlashes 4, FlashTimeMin 3000, FlashTimeMax 15000, gap between flashes in a burst 350 / 300 ms (+0x184 / +0x188), LightFlash 1, SkyFlash 1, colour white, ThunderCueID 0. A flash = the light at env+0x358 ON for 40-80 ms (the last flash of a burst 200-250 ms); the next burst comes FlashTimeMin.Max later. SkyFlash is only copied, never read; EnableLightning never read. The light is a directional light that lights dynamic objects only (wiki weather-lightflash-dynamic-only). Proof plan (needs g2): PC Release, Night look, flashes 1-2 s apart, player camera with own mech in frame, shots every 40 ms for 20 s, measure luma on the mech; Ill Wind as positive control. RETAIL BOGGED DOWN (LightFlash 1, FlashTimeMin 3000 / FlashTimeMax 15000, MaxFlashes 4) in the PC Release exe shows NO lightning flash: Team Destruction 4v4, 818 consecutive frames (about 87 s of game time by the HUD clock, about 107 ms per capture) with the pilot, an Atlas and a VTOL in frame; 0 spikes in full-frame mean, centre-box mean and centre-box median (threshold 12% + 2 over a 31-frame running median; centre median flat 11.0-11.5); 6-29 bursts were expected. The editor map (b2light) showed none either. CONCLUSION: lightning flashes are not visible in the recomp runtime, for retail and editor maps alike, so the editor export is NOT at fault. Cause OPEN, two leads from the code: (a) the ms clock [0x4E2430] vs the burst timers env+0x164/+0x168 in sub_001263F8 (a time-base mismatch would stop bursts from ever starting); (b) the flash light at env+0x358 (a directional light that should light dynamic objects) is created and toggled but never reaches the shader. CONFIDENCE: observation HIGH (positive control), cause unknown. Record as: 'Lightning is a PC runtime gap: retail Bogged Down does not flash in PC Release'. Hand to the runtime owner; the editor keeps writing LightFlash 1 (correct for the original game). Tags: Environment > Weather > Lightning flashes. TRACE: clue (a) RULED OUT: [0x4E2430] is ms, env update ~110/s, bursts run (flash-on sub_001262A2 / off sub_0012612E fire; 1 flash at 0.2 s, 5 by 14.4 s; count 3/4 -> 0/4; next burst 13.2 s). Light object env+0x358 exists (vtable 0x00463600, same class as the sun at env+0x354), colour env+0x18E. So bursts run and the light toggles, but the render path never uses it (clue b). Next: RECOMP_LIGHTNING_HOLD + light field dump. GATHER: the per-object light gather fills the unit vertex shader's ONE directional slot (c13 dir = sun light +0x48, c14 colour) with the sun only (c12 ambient, c15-c23 up to 3 point lights). With the flash light held ON, c13/c14 are byte-identical and no white directional appears: the registered, enabled flash light is never chosen. Remaining cause = the gather's selection rule (first/brightest directional, list order) or a PC-side change; writer of c13/c14 not found. NOT FIXED: env DirectionalLightColor (env+0x88) equals the unit shader c14 at load, but raising it, its 3 RAM copies or the sun light while the flash is on does NOT change unit lighting (RGB 38 off vs 31 held); writing the flash into NV2A constant slot 110 in nv2a_pb_exec.c also changes nothing. So the unit c14 is a CACHED value that reaches the GPU by another path. Next: log the caller of sub_0040BF20/BF70 for registers 0x6D/0x6E during a mech draw (15 SetVertexShaderConstant(13/14) sites). FIXED: see lightning-flash-fixed-in-pc-shim-unit-sun-colour-constants-get-the-flash-added-per-draw (unit sun-colour constants were uploaded once; the shim now adds the flash per draw while it is on).
facts.how_to_use: Observation HIGH (retail positive control); cause OPEN, owner = runtime (not the editor). The editor keeps writing LightFlash 1 (correct for the original game).

facts.title: Destroy objective completes whoever kills the target: completion check ignores killer/weapon (code) and an on-foot pilot's demolition charges finish it and Win (F1 PASS, g3)
facts.fact: M2-2/F1): (1) HIGH: the objective completion check sub_00169A49 (generated recomp_0037.c (made at install time, not in the repository)) never looks at the killer or weapon; it marks a record done only when every mission variable id it lists (up to 10 dwords at record +0x2C) has a nonzero byte in the var table at 0x4EB9E0. (2) LOW: the link 'target unit destroyed -> variable set' goes through the destroyed event 0x131D6C (killer in EAX) and the Destroyed/variable actions (sub_001A94A1 = MAActionMissionVariableSet, recomp_0045.c:37); no killer/weapon test found, but that path was not fully read. So the code gives NO sign that a pilot cannot complete a Destroy objective; F1 stays UNPROVEN, and the real limit is likely whether a pilot weapon can kill a mech at all (no wiki fact on pilot damage vs armour; sub_19955F kind bit 0x01 = PILOT is a targeting filter, not a damage rule). Quickest settle: one g3 run, Destroy objective on one mech, shoot it with the pilot pistol. Not written to the wiki (LOW). F1 PASS: an on-foot pilot destroys an AI-off Loki with demolition charges (4 charges) and the Destroy objective completes and the mission Wins. So the claim 'on foot cannot finish a Destroy objective' is FALSE, and Destroy -> complete -> Win is proven in game (the recomp advance works in practice despite the empty sub_001699ED body). SUPERSEDED by tree3-on-foot-pilot-can-complete-destroy-objective-and-win-proven-in-game (verified in game); mission-variable readers in tree3-mission-variable-table-readers-objective-check-trigger-gate-timer-save.

facts.fact: Set members are stored as uid properties (MoeEntitySetMember0.n) on the set, NOT as MoeEntityReference child nodes, so the old cleanup (which only dropped references to removed units) left dead member uids: a fresh Flat-ground mission listed 'Invulnerabilty at Start' (4 members), 'Red Stuff' (15) and 'Blue Stuff' (14) all pointing at units that no longer exist. facts.title: Velocity-oriented particles: quad builder sub_00298BE0, emitter ctor sub_00297800 flags at emitter+0xD8 (orient bit2, stretch bit3, sorting 5-7, facing 11-13), stretch unbounded; PC shim has no magenta fallback (missing textures read white); guest VS constants written by sub_0040BF20/BF70 with register bias 0x60 (c13 = 0x6D, c14 = 0x6E)
facts.fact: Orient = atan2 of velocity on the camera basis (CRT atan2 + x87 fcompi: stale-g_fp_cmp class, angle only); stretch multiplies size by the screen velocity length, UNBOUNDED. Colour per particle = sub_00297670 on the gradient at emitter+0xB8. Same vertex format/shader as billboards. HIGH (code-confirmed). The PC shim has no magenta fallback shader: the only 0xFFFF00FF is the RECOMP_RASTER_TEST debug triangle (kernel/nv2a_pb_exec.c:1071); missing textures read white (nv2a_pb_exec.c:1805). So the editor-rain magenta is texture/colour DATA or huge stretched geometry. Suspected (LOW, inferred): ENV_snow.tif RGB under near-transparent texels is magenta (alpha mean 0.6/255). Retail DOES ship rain: EnableRain with PrecipEffectID 31780 in Mission_10, 11a, 11b and Cinema_3_1a (so the editor tooltip 'the game has no rain' is probably wrong). MEDIUM (dictionary data). [Environment > Weather > Lightning; unit light gather] all guest vertex-shader constants are written by sub_0040BF20 (ecx = register, edx = ptr to 4 floats) and sub_0040BF70 (+ stack float count); constant register bias 0x60 so c13 = 0x6D, c14 = 0x6E, c15 = 0x6F; no immediate 0x6C-0x6E exists in the XBE, so the light gather computes the index. The PC shim only copies what the guest wrote (nv2a_pb_exec.c case 0x1EA4 ~3844, 0x0B80 range ~3907), so which light goes in c13/c14 is decided in guest code. The slot-2 writers at 0x6B960/0x6BB20/0x6BE80 are transform constants, not lights. Gather not yet located; nearest named light code: D3DLightMgr (sub_000528B0), SceneLightRegion (sub_00083C50), node_light (sub_00080AE0, sub_0008B110). HIGH for the negatives, gather location OPEN (a 1-run caller-address log of register 0x6D/0x6E writes would find it). Tags: Environment > Weather; Lightning flashes. CORRECTED: 31780 is the SNOW template (Env_Snow_Blowing), not a retail rain effect (the editor tooltip 'the game has no rain' was right); the ENV_snow.tif / streak-builder magenta suspicion is REFUTED (cause = renamed effect, see particle-effect-found-by-name-renamed-rain-effect-drew-magenta-fixed-2b008eb-retail-has-no-rain-effect).

facts.title: text.mgf interface/Text/<Lang>/{Credits,Mission,Persistent}.mgText = MGIc container with a TEXT chunk: count, lowest/highest id, header size 16, then count x (id, offset) and zero-terminated UTF-16LE strings
facts.fact: Verified by code + fmt_test. File: text.mgf, interface/Text/<Lang>/Credits.mgText, Mission.mgText, Persistent.mgText. Container 'MGIc'; the 'TEXT' chunk (tag, 0, size, 7) holds a 'ver ' sub-chunk (12 bytes) then 'data' (tag, size). The data block = u32 count, u32 lowest id, u32 highest id, u32 header size (16), then count x (u32 id, u32 offset from the start of data); strings are zero-terminated UTF-16LE. English: Mission has 592 ids 524288-525060 (524370 = 'Press A to open the gate.', 524787 = 'To the Rescue'); Credits has 333 ids from 262144; Persistent has 1694 ids 1-131181. Ids are the numbers that map files and triggers use to name briefing, objective and message text, so the editor looks strings up by id (GameData:game_text).
facts.how_to_use: Look up a message/briefing/objective id: pick the language folder, read Mission.mgText (ids 524288+) for mission strings, Persistent.mgText (ids 1-131181) for the shared UI/weapon/unit names, Credits.mgText for credits. Editor controls that show 'the game's text for id N' use this table.

facts.title: CORRECTS bots-vehicle-value (t01a): vehicle_pref is Mech 1.0, tank 0.80, VTOL 0.55+0.05*skill, BattleArmor 0.30+0.05*skill
facts.fact: CORRECTION (supersedes the numbers in t01a 'bots-vehicle-value'). The old fact's other terms (minus for distance, damage, enemy armour within 40 m -0.5, a closer on-foot ally -0.6; 20 s blacklist after three failed entries) were not contradicted by this audit. Consequences measured in the review: every 'Mech is worth the same (1.0) so a bot takes the nearest free one even if a stronger one is near (c3 row t3B-01: the game's m_nBattleScore is unused), and the skill bonus makes Veteran/Elite bots prefer VTOLs and BattleArmor (Elites spend 32 % of their time in a 'Mech, 16 % in VTOLs; Recruits 53 % in a 'Mech). facts.title: CORRECTS bots-ai-tuning-props / skill-tune-mover: AccuracyRadius is not on the fire path and Elite is NOT ~2x as damaging as Green (124 runs measured)
facts.fact: CORRECTIONS to t01a 'bots-ai-tuning-props' and t01b 'skill-tune-mover'. (1) 'AccuracyRadius = random miss offset' is UNSUPPORTED: the fire function sub_18482E (recomp_0040.c:15478-15540) does not read +0x1F8 AccuracyRadius, +0x1F0 or +0x1F4. It rolls a float in [0,100) (sub_1DBE0 at:15494); if the roll is < 25.0 (const 0x459448) it scales a factor by roll*0.01, else 1.0, and the factor goes to sub_17B222 / sub_17AF1C (not traced). +0x1EC/+0x1F4 are read in sub_151E48 and +0x1F8/+0x1F0 in sub_151F2C (recomp_0034.c:7899-8345), off the fire path (reads code-confirmed HIGH, meaning inferred MEDIUM). (2) FireDelay +0x218 is read by the fire gate sub_1858EF (recomp_0040.c:18335-18415) against an int ms timestamp: a time gate (read HIGH, meaning inferred). FireTime +0x214 has no reads in sub_18482E or sub_1858EF (HIGH). (3) The AI target choice sub_1837B3 (recomp_0040.c:12443-12760) does not read +0x1E8 bit 0x80 (AttackPilot) or +0x20C (EngageRadiusPilot) (HIGH for that range; it reads only +0x20/+0x2C). (4) MEASURED (HIGH): every MP vehicle the bots board is authored AccuracyRadius 5.00 / FireDelay 1.50 ([BOT-SKILL] lines). Per-skill 'Mech bot damage over 124 runs since 10-21 ([BOT-SUM]): dmg/min Green 1209, Regular 789, Veteran 882, Elite 1230; dmg/shot flat 28.6 / 26.9 / 30.9 / 31.0; shots per engaged second 2.27 / 2.41 / 1.51 / 2.60. So 'Elite is about twice as damaging as Green' is false for the bots. Open unknowns: who calls sub_151E48/sub_151F2C; which callee reads the roll factor; whether the aim has any velocity (clue) term.

facts.title: CORRECTS bots-eject-rule (t01a): bots no longer eject at 12 percent HP; the only exits are swap, trapped/bail and not-allowed kinds
facts.fact: CORRECTION. The old rule 'eject below 12 % HP with an enemy within 80 m' (t01a 'bots-eject-rule') is no longer in the code (ma2_bot_brain.c:1240-1270 pick_swap, 1660-1672 the only EJECT sources). The only ways out of a vehicle are: swap (HP <= 35 % AND a usable vehicle <= 70 m with no enemy within 50 m), trapped/bail, and not-allowed kinds. Evidence: 216 of 277 vehicle->pilot transitions happen at hp < 0.15 (mech 115, VTOL 51, BA 28, tank 22) and the 'pilot' then reappears at its base with hp 1.0 (E2E_1022 bot 10: MECH hp 0.00 at 724,1306 for 3 s -> PILOT at 955,827 = a respawn, i.e. the pilot died with the 'Mech). So bots ride every vehicle to its death. Confidence HIGH (code + run logs). DEDUPE: superseded by bots3-bots-never-eject-vehicle-death-kills-pilot-supersedes-bots-eject-rule (same finding, verified in 31 runs).

facts.title: Bot senses (audit): sight up to 690 m with no fog/far-plane cap, radar 300 m through walls, hearing flat 180 m, cloak ignored, facing from body yaw only
facts.fact: (2) RADAR: the bot 'radar' sends the position of every enemy within 300 m, all directions, through walls, with an error of 15 % of the distance; core hardcodes RECOMP_BOT_RADAR = 300 (core.c:2763; the RadarDist read is an open TODO); the retail HUD radar uses RadarDist at +0x18C (constructor default 30.0, maybe overridden) and a blip needs 3-D distance < RadarDist. (3) HEARING: flat 180 m for any weapon, all directions, as soon as the enemy fires; within 25 m everything is known; a heard enemy outside the field of view never gets a sight check (no 'turn to look') (brain.c:455, 486, 506-507). (4) CLOAK: bots ignore an enemy's cloak: perceive (brain.c:486-515) marks a cloaked enemy seen with the plain AI ray at any range and the radar keeps updating it every 0.5 s; only the shot is blocked, and only for strict cloak, via weapon value (defense.c:433 dk.cloak_strict). The game's own AI drops a cloaked target beyond 50 m (65 m in one mode) and a strictly cloaked one at any range (sub_17B81E), so camo is useless against bots while the bots' own camo (brain.c:1407) works against the player. (5) FACING: bot field of view and the human's 'attacking' test come from body yaw only (core.c:1508-1519 actor_yaw = root node forward +0xE0/+0xE8, within +-12 deg), not torso twist; the retail radar heading uses body yaw + torso twist (sub-object P+0x40). So bots misjudge a player aiming over the shoulder and ignore his Alpha Strike charge unless within 90 m.

facts.title: Bot knowledge (audit): map-wide hunt uses live positions of unseen enemies; damage credit is split by guesswork
facts.fact: (1) HUNT CHEAT: when a bot knows nobody, pick_roam (brain.c:1044-1072) goes for a LIVE enemy anywhere on the map 60-90 % of the time, weighted toward the scoreboard leader (Elites weight him x3), heading to 25-70 m from his real current spot, re-aimed every 8-20 s; [BOT-HUNT]: 42 hunts in 160 s, every bot hunting a live enemy at t=0.0. This breaks the design's own rule that bots never use live positions of unseen enemies (sec 2, sec 10). (2) DAMAGE CREDIT: every health drop of a victim is split among all bots targeting it that fired in the last 1.5 s, including damage the human or another enemy did (core.c:3126-3136); that feeds out_v (our damage rate -> time-to-kill -> the 'finish' commitment) and the [BOT-SUM] dmg metric, so bots over-commit to finishing kill-steals and the skill metrics are inflated.

facts.title: Bot skill effect (audit): reaction time does not delay the first shot; Elites are not stronger (kills 1.0/1.0/1.2/1.3x, Elite damage lowest in 4 of 6 matches)
facts.fact: (1) Kills per bot for Recruit/Regular/Veteran/Elite are about 1.0/1.0/1.2/1.3x; Elite damage is the lowest of the four skills in 4 of 6 matches (qe_td, 560 s: Recruit 15.8k vs Elite 5.8k per bot; shots 564 vs 279). Elites spend 32 % of their time in a 'Mech (Recruit 53 %, Regular 54 %), 16 % in VTOLs (others <= 2 %): vehicle_pref adds +0.05 per skill level to VTOL and BattleArmor, and Elite cover_use 1.0 / retreat at 32 % health make them fight less. (2) The brain's reaction time (0.90 s . 0.12 s) only delays committing to Attack and switching targets; on travel, hunt, power-up and vehicle orders out->fire uses mem_engageable (seen right now, brain.c:2660-2664) and the controller fires as soon as its own 4 Hz ray is clear (ctrl.c:455-494), so a Recruit opens fire as soon as an Elite; only the sight re-check period (0.25-0.70 s) differs. Together with bots-skill-tuning-correction-. skill changes little. Proposed fixes: t4-B5, t4-B6, t4-A2.

facts.title: Bot combat (audit): target flapping, heat ignored, coarse friendly-fire hold, no target lead, fixed threat numbers, no pilot denial, crude weapon choice
facts.fact: (1) TARGET FLAPPING: bots swap between two enemies and back within fractions of a second: mem_pot_dps scales by 1.0 when the enemy is 'attacking me', else 0.3, and the flag toggles each time the enemy's last shot ages past 1 s (combat_state_update); the x3.3 swing beats the keep margin (x1.25 smart, x1.05 others) and the reaction 'wait' gate restarts on every change (brain.c:564-568, 720-727; core.c:3086-3088); qe_td (570 s TD): 771 enemy-to-enemy swaps, 354 within 2 s of the previous, 318 A->B->A within 5 s. (2) HEAT: ctrl_fire never reads me->heat (ctrl.c:488-524), while the game vetoes fire on heat-limited weapons at >= 100 %, heat above 40 % degrades camouflage and absorbed damage becomes heat; no heat field in [BOT]/[BOT-SUM], unmeasured. (3) FRIENDLY-FIRE HOLD: ally_in_line is 2-D (no height), 8 m either side of the line, to 9 m past the target (ctrl.c:417-428, 496); ffhold frames per engaged second Green 5.9, Regular 8.1, Veteran 10.3, Elite 12.0 at ~60 fps (Elite ~20 % of engaged frames held). (4) NO TARGET LEAD: aimPt is the target's current point (vt 0x134); no velocity term found in sub_18482E (recomp_0040.c:15419-15640, partial check, MEDIUM) although the design promised leading. (5) THREAT MODEL: fixed per-kind numbers (k_kind dps 'Mech 45, tank 35 . range_acc 1.0 / 0.6 / 0.25 at 150 / 300 m) (brain.c:105-116, 559-568), not the real arsenal, though wpn_props already reads damage / fire_ms per barrel. (6) PILOTS: an on-foot enemy pilot scores ~3 against ~20+ for a fighting 'Mech (ttk floor 3 s), so a pilot sprinting to a free vehicle is ignored (brain.c:657-741); the AttackPilot bit 0x80 the bots set (core.c:715 ai_flag_bits) is not read by the AI target choice sub_1837B3. (7) WEAPON USE: secondaries fire on a fixed every-other-half-second cadence whatever the barrel's fire_ms/burst; no group is picked by target type (homing vs VTOL, splash vs infantry/BA) and charge weapons are never held (ctrl.c:514-521). Proposed fixes: rows t4-A1, A4-A9.
facts.how_to_use: Use for questions about why bots strafe-miss, stand still next to allies, or ignore pilots.

facts.title: Power-up collect rule (game, sub_131C9A): armour only when damaged, weapon power-up only when a weapon needs ammo or a class can level up
facts.fact: From BOTS-REVIEW rows t4-D1/D4 (recomp_0030.c:14136-14328, sub_131C9A, code-read). The game only lets a unit collect a pickup it can use: an ARMOUR pack only when the unit is damaged (a 'Mech: any of its 6 damage zones below 100; other units: health below 100 %); a WEAPON power-up only when a weapon needs its ammo refilled (+0x1A8 bit 0x01 / sub_12AD65) or some weapon class can still level up (the +0x1B4 x6 dword loop; sub_12B749 / sub_12AED4 per class; meaning of +0x1B4 inferred = which classes the pickup raises). Otherwise the pickup stays where it is and is not consumed (the +0x1A8 bit 0x02 latch is set only on a real collect: wiki mapowerup-plus-1a8-flag-bits). Alpha Strike is ready only when weapon classes 0-2 are all at their arsenal's top level and a hit drops a class one level (ma2_bot_defense.c:443-447; wiki alpha-topup), so weapon upgrades are the road to Alpha Strike. Confidence: collect branches HIGH (code read), +0x1B4 meaning MEDIUM (inferred). DETAIL: sub_131C9A, ecx = pickup, eax = collector; returns false if pickup+0x1A8 bit 0x10 or bit 0x08. ARMOUR (pickup+0x1B0 != 0): a MAMech (classid [0x4EAF78]) can take it only if one of its 6 damage zones ([actor+0x260] block, sub_16C459(zone)) != 100; any other class only if vt+0x7C (health %) != 100. WEAPON branch: if pickup+0x1A8 bit 0x01 (refill) and sub_12AD65(arsenal = [actor+0xA4]) == 0 (not all full) -> true; else for c in 0.5 with pickup+0x1B4[c] != 0: sub_12B749(arsenal, class c) / sub_12AED4 says the class can still rise -> true; otherwise false and the pickup stays. Armour repair given to the collector: sub_131EB0 (recomp_0030.c:14595-14840): 'Mech zones get +0x1B0 x scale, other kinds via vt 0x6C/0x74/0x78. Bot pickup view: armor = MEM32(e + 0x190 + RECOMP_BOT_PU_OFF default 0x20) = +0x1B0, confirmed by the recomp (ma2_bots_core.c:2449-2489); view cap MA2_BOT_MAX_PICKUPS 32 (ma2_bot_api.h:29). Code-read HIGH.
facts.how_to_use: Use to explain why a full-health player drives over an armour pack without taking it, and how pickups interact with Alpha Strike; editor power-up placement notes (pickup raw fields) can point here.

facts.title: Bot power-up use (audit): nearest pickup of any type, shared 25 s taken list, VTOL ferry never delivered, hurt bots stall short of the pack, no denial, 32-pickup view cap
facts.fact: c4 BOTS-REVIEW rows t4-D1.D7 (the game source tree source + 4C 6v6 UnderCover copy log, 7.4 min; HIGH for code, MEDIUM-HIGH for run counts). (1) D1: ground bots go for the NEAREST power-up of any type (nearest_powerup, brain.c:1594-1620, distance only); armour vs weapon are told apart only when hp < 0.4 and the pack is within 45 m (scores:1830-1841); the kill-drop rule (score 1.0 for any pickup within 70 m of a kill, 15 s) and the 'quiet, under 35 m' rule (0.9) fire at full health too; 17 of 52 power-up decisions came at hp >= 0.97; me->wpn_room is computed (core.c:2073-2079) but only the VTOL reads it (brain.c:2191). Tank bot7 at hp 1.00 chased a 1071 armour pack t=162-197; hurt bots (hp 0.09-0.29) went for weapon upgrades instead of armour. (2) D2: order_powerup marks a pickup 'taken' as soon as a bot is within 4 m, collected or not (brain.c:424, 2202-2208); g_pu_taken is ONE list for ALL bots of BOTH teams, 16 slots, keyed by position (3 m match,1601), lasting 25 s, so a full-health bot driving over an armour pack hides it from hurt teammates for 25 s. (3) D3: the VTOL power-up ferry never delivered once in the 6v6: VTOL bot3 held 'fetch' about 72 s, from t=363 sat on the ground 3 m from a pickup that is 7 m below where the VTOL can sink, calling 'hook' each second ~30 s ([BOT-CARGO]); the 25 s give-up blacklists one pickup and fetch_since restarts on the next. (4) D4: no bot weighs Alpha Strike (see powerup-collect-rule-.). (5) D5: the 'grab the armour' push (score 1.70) usually fails: in 5 of 8 cases the goal lasted <= 1.1 s because nearest_powerup drops a pickup whenever a remembered enemy is nearer to it (de < 0.8 d) (brain.c:1605-1607, 1841, 2211-2212); bot0 ('Mech hp 0.37 -> 0.21) circled ~15 m from a 786 armour pack for ~25 s. (6) D6: bots never take a pickup to deny it to an enemy; a closer teammate gets the pickup even at full health (brain.c:1604-1617). (7) D7: the bots' view holds at most 32 pickups (MA2_BOT_MAX_PICKUPS, ma2_bot_api.h:29, core.c:2454) INCLUDING flags, data cores, checkpoints and collection areas; 59 distinct live pickups (29 armour) were seen in 7 minutes on UnderCover; entities beyond 32 in scan order are silently dropped (live count at once not measured; whether kill drops expire unknown). Proposed fixes: t4-D1.D7.
facts.how_to_use: Read before changing bot power-up behaviour or explaining a bot dying next to an armour pack.

facts.title: Bots on editor-made (custom) maps: navigation always works; the retail node graph is used only on 4 bases; missing helipads / flags / bases degrade gracefully
facts.fact: From BOTS-REVIEW rows t3-custom-A01.A06, t3-custom-path-A01/A02, t3A-08 (code read in the game source tree source + 3D's custom 6v6 log; HIGH for code). (1) NAVIGATION: the walking planner (ma2_bot_path.c grid A*, 2 m cells) ALWAYS runs on an obstacle grid built at match start from the live terrain + colliders (core.c ensure_nav -> ma2_trav_build, then a fine prop pass), on every map, retail or custom. The coarse 20 m node graph (roam points, flank via-points, connectivity) is generated from that grid on any map whose base ships no 'Mech graph: log '[BOT-NAV] obstacle grid ok 508x508 . source=generated:gen_B670C477 nodes=2601 components 1'. (2) RETAIL GRAPH TIE: the nav graph is picked by the LOADING ARCHIVE (ma2_bot_mapid.c maps[] of 14 MP archives + core.c k_nav_archives; core.c ~1232-1247); a custom map reports its BASE archive, so ONLY on the 4 bases that ship a graph (In Your Face, New River City, Rush Hour, Witch Cauldron) does a custom map get the RETAIL graph (roam/flank picks then use retail ground while paths still follow the real terrain; row t3A-08, proposed fix: skip the shipped graph on a [SCENARIO] custom map). An unknown cache id -> terrain-match against the 4 shipped graphs (accepted at score >= 0.5 and 0.2 ahead of the next), else a graph is generated and cached as %LOCALAPPDATA%\MechAssault2\BotNav\gen_<terrain fingerprint>.map (edited terrain = new fingerprint). Otherwise the bot code is map-agnostic: no retail UIDs, template ids, coordinates or map names (features are found BY CLASS: MAFlagCTF, MACheckpoint, MASnatchItDataCore, MAPowerUp, MACollectionArea, MABuilding; fixed tank guns by property comp+0xBC/0xC0 = 0). 'Home' is wherever the bot first spawned (brain.c ~2485), not the team base. The optional stuck-memory file (RECOMP_BOT_STUCK_MEMORY=1, off) is keyed by archive name so custom maps would pollute the retail map's file. (3) LANES: discovered from the live terrain at t >= 1 s in TEAM modes: plan team-centroid -> enemy-centroid on the obstacle grid, add a danger corridor, re-plan twice -> up to 3 lanes ([BOT-LANES]), each bot takes one; none when the bases are < 300 m apart or in FFA modes. (4) FALLBACKS: helipad = any MABuilding with an MACollectionArea child (core.c ~2363, ma2_bot_pad_add); the editor palette's 'Military VTOL pad' carries one. A damaged VTOL (hp < 20-45 % by skill) heads for an armour pack within 300 m (no enemy within 120 m), else the nearest pad within 2.5 km; with neither it just fights on (brain.c ~1697-1726); ground units do not use pads. Objective scoring runs only when both sides' pieces exist (brain_obj.c ~47-57, 269-283): CTF with no flags / Snatch It with no bases or cores scores 0 and the match plays as Team Destruction (no freeze); the editor already flags those as Must fix. The game does not require a helipad, so a 'no VTOL pad near the base' Check warning is only a suggestion (row t3-custom-A05). Confidence HIGH for code; one proof pending (damaged VTOL on a no-pad map).
facts.how_to_use: Use for editor docs on what a custom MP map needs for bots (pads, flags, bases) and why terrain edits are safe for bot walking; test maps (id 0DAA6085) and bots_custom_stripped.ma2map (id 1C6565DE).

facts.title: Bot swap churn (BattleArmor start) and two editor-map problems: pads gave no vehicle in Team Destruction, pilots stall 5-12 m from an editor-placed 'Mech
facts.fact: From BOTS-REVIEW rows t3B-08, t3-custom-06, t3-custom-07. (1) SWAP CHURN (t3B-08): a BattleArmor (or a dying vehicle) heading for a 'Mech swap does not reserve it: claims are made only for MA2_ORD_GET_VEHICLE (ma2_bots_core.c:2796-2806) and order_swap (ma2_bot_brain.c:2259-2297) drives with travel/eject orders, so several BattleArmors chase the same free 'Mech; the first in takes it and the rest re-pick and set off again. ctf.log: 641 swap-go + 101 swap-eject notes, 7 of 11 BA bots start a swap at t=1.2 and are still BattleArmor at t=31, only 9 swaps complete in 180 s; snatch.log 16 stuck episodes, 6 swaps. Proposed fix: make the swap target a claim too (export swap_veh) and let pick_swap skip claimed vehicles. (2) EDITOR MAP, NO VEHICLES (t3-custom-06): on 3D's editor map t3d_allmodes (vehicle pads only: BattleArmor, Loki, Guided-Missile turret; no parked vehicles; players on foot) Team Destruction had NO vehicle entity at run time (0 [BOT-HULL], 0 [BOT-VEHPICK], all 11 bots pilots for 180 s) while CTF on the BattleArmor-start copy had 'Mechs, VTOLs and turrets (46 [BOT-HULL]); likely the pads/their vehicles sit only in the CTF/BaseWar/Snatch game-type groups of the editor kit, or a pad only spawns when asked (UNPROVEN; editor idea: Check warns 'Team Destruction: no vehicle will exist'). (3) EDITOR MAP, BOARDING (t3-custom-07): on bots_custom_full pilots on foot reach the editor-placed 'Mech but stall 5-12 m from the hull without tapping Y, then silently drop it (4 of 5 arrivals stalled in custfull_td.log, 2 more in custfull_ctf.log; bot 0 frozen 2 s 5.7 m from hull 018A9020 at 236,616 with dest = entry 241,624 behind it); retail runs board 574/574. Suspected cause: the editor's vehicle-on-pad placement height / stand collision blocks the pilot (unproven).
facts.how_to_use: Relevant to editor testing: before blaming bots for a vehicle-less custom map, check which game-type group the pad/vehicle belongs to; item (2)/(3) are the open editor-side leads.

facts.title: Bot skill (CONFIRMED in real matches): Bot Skill's accuracy knob does nothing (A/B), the g_tune[48] bug is real in a 2nd match, friendly-fire hold ~30 % of engaged time, Alpha Strike never happens
facts.fact: UPDATES to bots-skill-tuning-correction-accuracyradius-not-on-fire-path-elite-not-2x, bots-skill-effect-audit-. bots-combat-audit-. (BOTS-REVIEW rows t4-A2 A/B, t4-A3 UPDATE, t4-A5 UPDATE, t4-A10, t4-B4/B5 UPDATE; evidence, and B-recruit-notune\; HIGH measured, one run each for the A/B). (1) DIRECT A/B on the installed game 35CBBE2C, same map/mode/bots (UnderCover copy, Team Destruction 5v6 + idle human, all bots Recruit), 180 game s each: skill tune ON (radius x2, delay x1.6): 11 bots dealt 40,475 dmg from 821 shots (1.12 shots per engaged s); RECOMP_BOT_SKILL_TUNE=0 (authored values): 40,585 dmg from 1,203 shots (1.51 per engaged s). The tune cuts shot calls by about a third but damage is unchanged, so Recruit bots are as deadly as untuned ones: the Bot Skill accuracy knob does nothing (matches the 124-run aggregate; consequence of the fire path ignoring AccuracyRadius). NOTE: authored FireDelay is not always 1.50: 0.50 / 1.50 / 3.00 by vehicle with AccuracyRadius 5.00 everywhere; some tuned bodies carry EngageRadius 250 / 350 / 1200. (2) g_tune[48] BUG CONFIRMED: 4C's 6v6 played two matches in one game session; match 1 tuned 52 distinct vehicles (> 48 slots); 28 s into match 2 two Green bots' vehicles 02375020 and 02390020 (same slot 34) evicted each other 858 + 857 re-tunes, AccuracyRadius grew 5 -> 10 -> 20 . 2e38, FireDelay up to 4e25; Bot 2 (Green 'Mech) fired 59 shots / 554 dmg in match 1's first 60 s but 1 shot / 65 dmg in match 2. So from the 2nd match without restarting the game some Green bots barely fire. (3) Friendly-fire hold in a full 6v6 (match 1, t=440): hold frames per engaged second per bot 4.0-50.8, median ~18 (~30 % of engaged time on average, ~85 % for bot 9, Elite BattleArmor: 3950 hold frames vs 258 shots). (4) Alpha Strike NEVER happens: 0 [BOT-ALPHA] lines in the 7.4 min + 60 s DIAG 6v6 and in all 296 archived bot runs; alpha_logic needs alpha_ready (weapon classes 0-2 all at top level), bots do not collect upgrades toward it and each hit drops a level (brain.c:1316-1384). (5) Sight and skill re-confirmed on the fresh 6v6: of 827 target picks 102 start beyond 400 m and 34 beyond 475 m (max 582 m); [BOT-KILL] credits per slot Recruit 5.2, Regular 3.3, Veteran 6.2, Elite 5.3; Elites spent only 51 % of samples in a 'Mech (Regular 78 %).
facts.how_to_use: Use these measured numbers when anyone asks whether bot Skill matters or why bots rarely Alpha Strike.

facts.title: Custom-map bot proofs: all 3 lanes used, no-heal-pad is safe, and on a 'stripped' editor map nobody boards in Team Destruction (pad entry zones unarmed, map-data cause)
facts.fact: UPDATES to bots-on-custom-maps-. and bots-swap-claims-.-editor-map-vehicle-boarding-problems (BOTS-REVIEW rows t3-custom-path-A04/A05, t3-custom-08/09; 3D's g3 runs in bots-t3d\). (1) FAN-OUT PROVEN (custfull2_td, Team Destruction 5v6 + player, 165 s, DIAG): [BOT-LANES] found exactly the 3 lanes built in the editor ('3 lane(s) from 156,509 to 869,507 (corridor 128 m) in 15 ms'; main = central valley, side +1 apex 498,332 = south lake/bridge lane, side -1 apex 668,662 = north hills lane); traffic in x 400-650: central 252 samples (7 bots), south 57 (2), north 52 (2), 0 on the walls; only 5 no-progress stalls, 1 pilot wedged 30 s by its own base (t3A-07 class). (2) NO HEAL PAD PROVEN SAFE (t3-custom-09): on bots_custom_stripped (no pads, no power-ups) no [BOT-PAD] and no goal=repair; the one low-HP VTOL went goal=retreat at hp 0.13-0.03, fled and fought, was shot down at t=43: no hover, no freeze. The 4 'Mechs EXIST (BOT-HULL kind=2 at 225,378 / 791,404 / 236,616 / 743,285) but none is ever usable (0 'Mech picks vs 11 on custfull2_td): bot-side 'usable' needs free, alive, an ACTIVE entry zone (MACrateGenerator armed / live MATriggerPoint; ma2_bot_brain.c:1174-1183, ma2_bot_entry.c:84-104) and own or neutral nation; the strip (deleting every MAPowerUp/MAPowerupDrop incl. ones nested in spawners / mission-type groups) evidently removed what arms the Team Destruction pads; bots then try the 2 VTOLs (one claim each) and 9 drop to hunt at t=0.3. Players would hit the same dead pad. Editor implication: deleting power-ups/salvage must not touch pad internals; Check should warn 'This vehicle pad cannot be boarded: its entry zone has no crate generator/trigger point'. Proof pending: RECOMP_TEST_DUMP_NEAR=791,404,15,5 on custstrip_td vs custfull2_td should list the pad's children (expect MACrateGenerator + MATriggerPoint in full, missing/unarmed in stripped). Bot-side gap: nothing logs WHY a vehicle is unusable (proposed one-shot [BOT-VEHSKIP]).
