facts.how_to_use: Use for editor docs: what arms a vehicle pad, and what an editor-built TD map needs so that players and bots can board; test maps bots_custom_full / bots_custom_stripped.

facts.title: NeuroHack is effectively never attempted by BattleArmor bots: G_HACK score drops to 0 the moment the target turns on the BA (13 hack decisions in 442 s, 0 clamps)
facts.fact: BOTS-REVIEW row t4-C2 (4C long 6v6 UnderCover copy, 442 s, 11 bots; code HIGH, run counts measured). The BA's G_HACK utility exists only while the target 'Mech is < 45 m, or < 120 m AND shooting someone else (ma2_bot_brain.c:1849-1863), so it drops to 0 the moment the target turns on the BA or the BA is pushed back; no hysteresis applies to a 0 score (brain.c:1917-1919 hysteresis only if s > 0); cover (0.95 when att >= 2), powerup (1.0-1.15) and attack then win. The controller clamp needs < 11 m (ctrl.c:2005) and is never reached. Evidence: 13 '-> hack' decisions in 442 s, median dwell 0.5 s (max 5.4 s), exits to cover x3 / powerup x4 / attack x5 / support x1; [BOT-SUM] clamp=0/0 for all 11 bots (one 0/1); 0 [BOT-CLAMP], 0 [BOT-HACKED], 0 QTE cues in the whole match. So BA bots jet around and plink at '[text omitted]' 'Mechs never need their QTE defence. Proposed fix: commit to a hack once chosen (keep G_HACK while the target lives within ~120 m for up to ~12 s) - RISK: it re-enables the clamp -> hack -> re-board path that crashed long1 at t=298 in 0x2B1xxx after 37 repeat cycles (open issue; the 20 s / 30 s rate limits added since were never verified because clamps no longer happen) -> needs a 15 min BA-heavy soak first.
facts.how_to_use: Use when asked why bots never NeuroHack or why the QTE never appears in bot matches; do not re-enable the clamp path without a soak test.

facts.title: Bot long-match stability/perf (long 6v6): hull-profile cache thrash after 48 hulls, BOT-STALL false positive at match end, fps halves over a long match (cause unknown), health check OK
facts.fact: (1) C1 HULL-CACHE THRASH: vehicle_extent keeps 48 slots g_ext[48] (ma2_bots_core.c:2180, 2201-2214) that are never freed when a vehicle dies and never reset between matches; after 48+ hulls a new one takes slot (actor>>4)%48, so two LIVE parked hulls with the same slot evict each other and are re-measured (~100 rays, 4-7 ms each) every 12 ms window for the rest of the match. Seen: 54 distinct hulls by t=375; 02403910 + 02212E10 both slot 1 -> 339 [BOT-HULL] re-measures EACH; [BOT-PERF] 'world view' 5 -> 61-68 ms/s and rays 1.1K -> 6.1K/s from t=375 to the end (t=442); match 2 thrashes from t<55 (37 re-measures each from stale entries). Effect: ~+4 ms per frame of game-thread time after a few minutes and from the start of every rematch. Same family as the g_tune[48] bug (bots-skill-confirmed-in-real-matches-.). Proposed fix: free a slot when its actor is gone, clear g_ext at match start, LRU eviction or 128 slots. Fix: clear g_beat at match end and re-arm the budget per match. (3) C4 FPS: frame rate falls by about half over a long 6v6 (~110 fps at t=10 -> 55-75 fps from t=90; [BOT-CAMS] drawn-frame deltas t=10:113, 50:91, 100:68, 200:62, 300:68, 440:72) while the bots' own cost stays flat (10-14 % of one core, ~1.5-2 ms/frame; brain 25-55 ms/s, ctrl 45-95 ms/s), so it is NOT the bot brain; cause unknown (wreck/effect build-up, hull thrash only from t=375, or GPU shared with other trees' games in a hidden 1280x960 window); proposed control run: 0v0 + idle human vs 5v6 with RECOMP_BOT_PERF=1 RECOMP_PERF=1. (4) C5 HEALTH CHECK OK: no crash, no real stall, no fault, no log spam; the rematch (Game Over -> Enter -> Briefing 12/12 -> new match) recreates all 11 bots cleanly; memory flat (private 561 MB at t=40, 665 after match 1, 658 in match 2); every bot logger ([HUMAN-HP], [DEATH], [STAT], [BOT-CAMS], [OBJ-SCORE], [BOT-HULL]) is behind RECOMP_BOT_DIAG and UNIMPL is capped at 50 lines, so a normal player's log stays small (DIAG run: 2.5 MB per 5 min).

facts.title: Bots review updates: CTF guard leaves the flag for an unusable armour pack, NeuroHack blocked by the on-ground gate (0 clamp tries in a 330 s BA soak), hull thrash needs 48+ hulls, D5 stall intermittent
facts.fact: UPDATES (BOTS-REVIEW rows t4-D1/D5/D3-D7 UPDATE and t4-C2/C1 UPDATE; evidence + d4-ctf-bogged-end.png). (1) D1 CONFIRMED on a second map and mode (CTF 6v6, Bogged Down Remix copy, 8 min, hidden g4 run): bot6, a Battle Armor flag GUARD (obj=def/guard) at hp 1.00, left the CTF objective at t=408 because the kill-drop rule scores the power-up 1.00 against the objective 0.80; it chased a 2000 armour pack at 852,1679, then a 1286 pack at 833,1616 for 20 s, stood still 12.5 m from the second one for 6 s and went back to fighting at t=428 (typed trips in the match: 10 bot-seconds at full health toward armour, 1 hurt bot toward a weapon upgrade). A defender wandering off the flag for a pickup it cannot use leaves its base open; proposed: never let a power-up beat an objective guard/carry role unless the pickup is usable and within 30 m. (2) D5 NOT repeated in the CTF run: all 5 badly hurt pushes (score 1.70) held and healed, so the UnderCover 'dances next to the pack' stall depends on the map or contact (enemies near the pack): intermittent, confidence lowered, the 5 s no-progress drop is still a cheap guard. (3) D3/D7: no VTOL fetch happened in the CTF run (0 [BOT-CARGO]), so the VTOL ferry finding rests on the UnderCover log alone; 54 distinct non-parked pickups (22 armour) appeared in 8 min on Bogged Down (59 in 7 min on UnderCover): kill drops pile up toward the 32-entry view cap, but whether they are live at once is unmeasured (proposed: log the live pickup count in [BOT-SUM]). (4) C2 BA HACK SOAK (run2, same map/mode, RECOMP_BOT_FAV_KINDS red=BA blue=Mech, 330 s): still 0 clamp TRIES, 0 clamps, 0 NeuroHacks, 0 QTE cues. SECOND CAUSE besides the flapping goal: the one long hack (bot 8, t=121-132, 10.6 s) reached its target twice (5 m at t=129, 8 m at t=123) but both times mid-jet-hop (y 10-12 m above walking height), and ctrl_do_hack only tries the clamp when the BA's AI jump flag ai+0x240 is clear, i.e. on the ground (ma2_bot_ctrl.c:2005-2007); the hops (stop 2 m, overshoot, brain.c:2242) carry it past and it lands 25-32 m away, so the < 11 m + on-ground window never happens. Only 19 BA vehicle picks in 330 s (UnderCover has few BA hulls), so favouring BA alone cannot make a BA-heavy match. Proposed in addition to C2: walk or short-hop on the final approach (< 25 m), or try the claw while airborne when within 11 m horizontally and < 6 m vertically (the human claw path 0x17305C works from a jump; the clamp test sub_10239A decides); log [BOT-CLAMP] tries with the refusal reason. (5) C1 hull thrash did not appear in the 330 s run2 (fewer hulls seen, max 3 [BOT-HULL] per actor, flat 'world view' 4-8 ms/s): consistent with it needing 48+ hulls seen (mid/late match or a rematch). Confidence: code reads HIGH, run counts measured; D5 intermittent.

facts.title: Camouflage in the game (visibility, fade, countdown, shimmer, camo bodies) and exactly where the bots ignore it (rows t4-sk-B1/B4/B5)
facts.fact: Visibility rises to >= 0.65 when the unit takes a hit, fires or deals damage, decays at 0.65/s, and follows heat above 70 % (sub_1828D3, sub_182623). The game's own AI (sub_17B81E) sees a cloaked target only within 50 m (65 m in one caller mode) and a strictly cloaked one never. Camo bodies (-93): 'Mechs 6D18 / 7FAF (30 s camo, 15 s recharge), 7FAB (60 / 15), 808F (40 / 20); Rhommel tank 8C9D (60 / 20). WHERE THE BOTS IGNORE IT: none of this reaches the brain (Ma2PlayerView has no cloak field; core defense_blocks covers shield / absorber / AMS only, core.c:2058-2072); perceive (brain.c:486-515) tests no cloak; call-outs (535-548) too; and the controller fires on its own 4 Hz AI ray at the LIVE target position (ctrl_shot_los, ctrl.c:455-494, 2459-2527; brain.c:2660-2664 always copies b->tgt into out->target), wpn_value_vs zeroes only a STRICT cloak, so a non-strict cloaked unit at 300 m is still shot at and the native torso aim (sub_18AFDB) tracks the live position: bots turn their torsos to, and fire bursts , a cloaked player. No log has ever shown a cloaked unit against bots (no cloaked=1 in any [DEF-VS] line under) and no hook makes the human cloak. Existing pieces for a future proof: RECOMP_DEFENSE_TEST=<s> (a bot in a 'Mech/tank taps its defence every s seconds, defense.c:798-808), RECOMP_BOT_FAV_KINDS, RECOMP_TEST_HUMAN_BOARD (core.c:3734-3755), RECOMP_DEFENSE_PROBE=1 ([DEF-VS] cloaked=%d/%d), RECOMP_DEFENSE_CATALOG=1. PROPOSED (not built): Ma2PlayerView cloak 0/1/2 + cloak_shimmer; cloak_spot(b,p,d) per skill (CLOAKED range 12/20/35/55 m with chance 0.15/0.30/0.50/0.80 per sight re-check; STRICT 0/0/10/25 m chance 0/0/0.30/0.50; shimmer x1.3, Elite a further x1.25); memory when a target cloaks (engage grace 0/0/0.8/1.5 s, search memory 4/7/12/20 s, dead-reckon 1/2/3/4 s); fire only at a visible target; skip radar for cloak != 0; proof hook RECOMP_TEST_CLOAK="<who>:<t0>". Rows t4-sk-B1.B5 hold the full design (these are design, not facts). UPDATE (4B, row t4-sk-B4 UPDATE): given the open radar result (radar-blip-test-sub-204133-reads-no-camo-field-caller-prefilter-unchecked) there is no evidence retail hides a camo blip, so skipping the bots' radar for cloaked units is a DESIGN choice (honour the cloak), not retail parity; alternative if parity matters: keep the radar for cloaked units with a coarse error (+-40 m) and no use as a firing position.
facts.how_to_use: Use for camo behaviour facts; do not treat the proposed spot ranges as game behaviour.

facts.title: Bot skill behaviours measured (3 matches): peek/cover/dodge/notice scale with skill but cost shooting time, so Elites deal no more damage; Alpha, NeuroHack and 'finish' never show
facts.fact: Per skill Recruit/Regular/Veteran/Elite: PEEK episodes 0.08/0.06/0.14/0.32; ->cover 0.00/0.34/0.46/0.54; ->retreat 0.32/0.40/0.26/0.49; jump-jet dodges 0.46/1.00/4.13/2.98; incoming shots noticed ([BOT-INCOMING]) 0.7/2.1/10.3/15.3; ->support 0.00/1.20/0.84/0.82; ->hunt 2.46/2.36/2.04/2.17; [THREAT] target switches 3.6/4.5/4.1/4.6; Alpha Strike charges 0 at every skill; time engaged 33/32/27/25 %; time in a 'Mech 40/67/46/63 %, on foot 15/12/18/18 %; damage per min 811/1205/1200/1082 (22/32/35/30). WHY ELITES DEAL LESS (code ma2_bot_brain.c:133-138 k_skill,1659,1680,2047-2062,2711-2717): (a) retreat_hp is INVERTED: 0.12/0.17/0.27/0.32 (+0.05 BA, +0.15 VTOL), so Elites leave a losing fight at 32 % hp (45 %+ in a VTOL) while Recruits fight to 12 %; (b) cover_use 0/0.5/0.85/1.0: an outnumbered Elite ALWAYS breaks off to cover (8 s re-roll); (c) peek-and-hide: the SHOOT phase shrinks with skill (1.5-2.5 s minus 0.15*skill) but the HIDE phase does not (1.8-3.0 s), so an Elite peek is ~60 % hidden vs ~53 % for a Recruit, and Elites start 4x more peeks (BA 0.3 + 0.2*skill); (d) dodge hops 0.2/0.7/1.2/1.8 per 10 s (x2 when hit) interrupt aim/fire, plus 'support' moves (0.8/min). FEATURES THAT NEVER SHOW: Alpha Strike 0 charges at every skill (alpha_logic needs a clear shot, a target worth it and nobody shooting us); NeuroHack QTE skill (qte_frac / qte_miss) never exercised (see bots-neurohack-never-attempted-.); smart focus fire / finish: 0 'finish' picks in [THREAT] in 3 logs and target switches per minute are the same at every skill (3.6-4.6) though smart bots get a x1.25 keep bonus; hunt-the-leader is highest for Recruits (2.46/min). Proposed (design): Elite = better at the same fight (retreat_hp flat ~0.18, cover only when force < 0.6, peek window tied to weapon reload, dodge only on incoming shots).
facts.how_to_use: Use with bots-skill-confirmed-in-real-matches-. when explaining why Elite bots are not stronger; table = bot-per-minute means.

facts.title: Bot peek-and-hide (audit): BA/'Mech peek is a short shuffle ended in 1-2 s by other goals; the VTOL pass-and-hide works and scales; tanks and pilots never peek
facts.fact: (1) BA/'Mech: a BattleArmor hide spot is a median 5.1 m from its shoot spot (ring r1 = 5 m; 'Mechs 9-17 m); an episode lasts 4.5-4.9 s of the planned 18-30 s with only 0.14-0.25 completed hide->shoot cycles per peek at every skill; it starts on a random 6 s roll (BA want 0.3 + 0.2*skill; 'Mech only when hurt/outnumbered) and flips on random 1.5-3 s timers that ignore the weapon. Share of BA time in peek: Green 6.4 %, Regular 5.2 %, Veteran 15.4 %, Elite 16.7 % ('Mechs <= 1.7 %); BA peeks 133/149/123/238, completed cycles 19/36/26/49. (2) VTOL pass-and-hide WORKS and scales: hides per firing pass 0.06/0.30/0.52/0.74 (vt_cover 0.10/0.35/0.65/0.85; [BOT-VTOLSTAT] hides/tries/passes Green 3/3/50, Regular 29/38/98, Veteran 28/31/54, Elite 105/116/141); the hide search is real (30/55/80 m rings, AI ray blocked, never over a roof) but timing is random (firing pass 1.5-3.5 s, hide 6 s) whatever the guns' reload. (3) Tanks and on-foot pilots never peek: peek_order returns early for tank / VTOL / pilot (brain.c:2049); tanks only stop-and-shoot (strafe_hold 60 %). (4) Interruption: a peek is ended within 1-2 s by goal re-evaluation: support, hack, cover, powerup and hunt all outscore attack's hysteresis while the bot is hidden (the target is not visible so attack scores lower; support only fires when !t->visible); example run1 bot10 t=162-175 (peek-shoot -> support +3 s -> attack -> hack -> cover -> powerup). Proposed (design, row 3d): time peek to the weapon (reload_s = max(fire_ms/1000, FireDelay); slow group >= 0.9 s; catalogue fire_ms: mortar 1050, gauss/crossbow 2500, warhammer 3000 (burst 3), javelin 1000, laser 225, PPC 150-250, MG 100) and treat 'in a peek cycle' as visible for scoring.
facts.how_to_use: Use to explain why BA bots twitch instead of ducking, and which weapon timing facts (fire_ms values) matter for a fix.

facts.title: CTF flag-carrier reaction (measured): every skill switches to hunt the thief in ~0.9 s because objective goals ignore reaction time and use the live carrier position
facts.fact: Rows t4-sk-D1.D4. Per skill (bot-pickups / goal switched to hunt the carrier, median s / THREAT target switched to the carrier, median s / first hit on the carrier, median s): Recruit 19 / 9 (0.9) / 4 (20.4) / 3 (0.2); Regular 20 / 5 (0.9) / 5 (11.7) / 4 (3.6); Veteran 13 / 8 (0.8) / 2 (19.5) / 0; Elite 20 / 16 (0.9) / 1 (15.5) / 5 (1.7); an all-Regular run on the same map: 67 / 27 (0.7) / 14 (20.3) / 11 (15.7). So the goal switch is equally fast at every skill (about one evaluation period); skill only changes HOW MANY go (Elite 80 %, Recruit 47 %); first hits depend on who was already close. CAUSES (code): (1) the hunt goal is scored in obj_ctf on every evaluation from the objective view with the carrier's LIVE position (w->players[ti].pos), with no perception, memory or sight check (brain_obj.c:93-105, 342-343), so every bot 'knows' at once; (2) no reaction time gates objective goals: k_skill.reaction (0.90/0.55/0.30/0.12 s) only gates target switches in choose_target; (3) skill weight prio[4] = 0.85/1.0/1.15/1.3 is multiplied by obj_zeal, a per-bot random 0.75-1.25 (brain.c:2454), so the persona spread equals the whole Recruit-to-Elite spread; the only clear skill effect is 'aces turn back' (Veteran+ attackers within 250 m: sc 0.9 instead of 0); (4) the carrier bonus in choose_target (obj_bonus x1.2/1.45/1.75/2.05) rarely decides: it needs an engageable (seen) carrier within reach x1.3 and still sits behind the reaction 'wait'; the THREAT target moved to the carrier only 12 times in 72 bot-pickups (Elite 1 of 20); hits on the carrier come from the hunt ORDER (o->target = enemy within 20 m of the hunt point), and the carrier's score is low when it does not shoot back (pot x0.3, t4-A1). Proposed (design, D4): per-skill NOTICE delay (Elite 0.3-0.6 s . Recruit 4-6 s), hunt point from memory not live position, skill-dominant priorities, Veteran+ switch to a visible carrier at once. UPDATE: goal switch to hunt 1.1 s (all Regular), 0.2 s (all Veteran), 0.7 s for Recruit, Regular and Elite alike (Mixed); the all-Recruit and all-Elite runs had no pickups. Consistent: no skill ordering in the reaction time.
facts.how_to_use: Use when asked why a Recruit turns on the flag thief as fast as an Elite; links to the live-position hunt cheat (bots-knowledge-audit-.).

facts.title: Retail HUD radar: the per-entry blip test sub_00204133 only gates on RadarDist (no camo/team/alive read); whether a caller pre-filters camo units is UNCHECKED (open)
facts.fact: Research-. Bodies are in generated recomp code (made at install time, not in the repository) (the the game source tree gen folder has only prototypes and call sites). sub_000DD8B9 (recomp_0022.c:28941-28975) is NOT the blip builder: it is a POSITION ACCESSOR (ecx = object; returns the pointer at [obj+0x90] if set, else delegates through [obj+0x8C], else the static zero vector at 0x5283D8); called from recomp_0053.c with ecx = [this+0x194]. sub_00204133 (recomp_0053.c:21479-~21600) is the per-entry radar test: entry gate: if [this+0x194] == 0 return (21499-21500); DISTANCE GATE: squared distance from the reference point (arg [ebp+8]) to the position from sub_000DD8B9 is compared with RadarDist^2, RadarDist = [this+0x18C]; if d^2 >= R^2 it jumps to 0x00204258 and skips the emit (~21566); emit: scales the offset by 1/R and calls sub_00205CC1 with eax = this+0x19C (~21590; looks like the list insert, inferred). Neither function reads +0x24 / +0x28 / +0x50 / +0x54 (camo visibility / alpha / countdown / fade), team, alive, or any flag byte. VERDICT: NOT FOUND in these two functions = no camo test there (code-confirmed for them). NOT checked: the caller loop around 0x002047D4 (it may pre-filter camo units before calling 0x00204133), what object sits at HUD+0x194 (unit list vs blip list), and the full body of sub_00205CC1 and its callees 0x00205E56 / 0x00205E34 / 0x00205CF3 (its visible conditions do not touch the camo fields). Settling it in game needs a camo unit at a known distance with the radar traced (a RECOMP_* trace on 0x00204133). Confidence MEDIUM; the bots fix t4-sk-B4(c) 'skip radar for cloak != 0' stays an inference.
facts.how_to_use: Answer to 4B: do not claim the retail radar hides camo units; no test in the per-entry radar function says so. Next step if it matters: read the caller at 0x002047D4 and what fills the list at HUD+0x194.

facts.title: Fixed-skill runs (all Elite vs all Recruit, 5v6 Team Destruction): Elite damage/min only +11 %, because Elites are engaged 32 % of the time vs 45 %
facts.fact: Two 5.2 min Undercover Team Destruction 5v6 runs with EVERY bot the same skill, DIAG on (run4-all-recruit\stderr.txt; skillstat.py). Elite vs Recruit per bot: engaged 32 % vs 45 % of the time; damage per min 1282 vs 1153 (+11 % only, although Elites have 0.12 s vs 0.90 s reaction and 85 vs 55 deg FOV); shots per min 37 vs 30; peeks 0.37 vs 0.09 per min; ->cover 0.32 vs 0.00; ->support 1.59 vs 0.00; dodges 1.48 vs 0.28; incoming fire noticed 12.1 vs 0.8; retreat 0.32 vs 0.39 per min (Recruits retreat too: their 12 % threshold is hit because they stay in fights); time in a 'Mech 55 % vs 54 % (so the 51 %-vs-78 % 'Mech gap in the Mixed audit is roster noise, not a skill effect, in TD on Undercover); target switches 4.9 vs 4.3 per min; Alpha Strike 0 in both; one Elite BattleArmor clamp in 5 min ([BOT-CLAMP] x1, no completed hack), 0 for Recruits. Skill changes behaviour clearly (five counters move 4-15x) but an Elite spends 13 points less of the match engaged, which eats almost all of its aim/reaction edge. Proposed success test (design): rerun the two fixed-skill runs after the fix: Elite engaged >= Recruit and damage/min >= 1.4x Recruit.
facts.how_to_use: Use as the measured baseline before any bot skill retune; mode matters (TD vs CTF: Elite Mech time differs).

facts.title: A projectile in flight carries its template uid at +0x30, the same value as its fire group's MAWpnGrp +0x7C (so per-weapon projectile speed can be learned in flight)
facts.fact: From 4A, confidence HIGH as an inference from two existing wiki facts: the spawn-from-template function 0x161D77 stores 'node+0x30 = uid', and a runtime-created entity's +0x30 = its TemplateID. So a projectile in flight carries its template uid at +0x30, which equals the uid of the fire group's MAWpnGrp +0x7C (wpn_template looks the template up by that uid). The smoke's [F41-PSPD] lines (RECOMP_BOT_DIAG) will give measured speeds per template to check those fields against; if F41 shows speeds_learnt = 0 or lead_shots = 0 the +0x30 key is wrong. Status: inference, runtime check pending. The learnt-speed table is capped at 64 entries and filled up in the smoke (optional F41 follow-up).
facts.how_to_use: When you need a projectile entity's weapon template: read +0x30 and compare with MAWpnGrp +0x7C / the template uid list. Verify with [F41-PSPD] lines before relying on speed fields.

facts.title: Bots baseline C0 (15 runs, 5 map/mode sets): boarding, Mech time, damage/min, kills, fps medians per map with seed noise
facts.fact: Per-map MEDIANS (n=3), then the seed spread: (kf = Killing Field copy, Team Destruction) boarding attempts 25, board_ok 95 %, board median 7.5 s, first 'Mech 8.1 s, time in a 'Mech 59.6 %, damage 721 per bot-min, 14 kills (2.7/min), sim fps 33 (first minute 51, last 47). (nrc = New River City copy, TD) 30 attempts, 97 %, 6.7 s, 8.1 s, 48.5 %, 1094, 18 kills (3.34/min), fps 79.5 (93 first / 64 last). (nrcctf = New River City CTF) 35 attempts, 92 %, 7.0 s, 8.2 s, 58.2 %, 1008, 23 kills (4.27/min), fps 79.6 (59 / 81). (uc = Under Cover copy, TD) 35 attempts, 97 %, 8.6 s, 12.2 s (slowest: city map), 54.5 %, 1400, 25 kills (4.82/min), fps 57 (67 / 40). facts.title: MAMech torso yaw: 3-axis rotation controller at actor+0x2B8; current angle actor+0x31C (likely), target +0x358, velocity +0x368; written by sub_0018AFDB -> sub_002AE360 -> sub_002AE200
facts.fact: Research-. A MAMech embeds a 3-axis rotation controller at actor+0x2B8 (constructed by sub_002AC380, vtable 0x4930B8, destructor sub_002AC800). Its sub-objects: +0x40 = current state (vt 0x4934B8; actor+0x2F8) and +0x7C = target/velocity state (same vtable; actor+0x334); a speed/scale float sits at +0xCC. vt 0x4934B8 slot +0x20 = sub_002B2830 reads [obj+0x24] = actor+0x31C (axis 0 = yaw); slots +0x30/+0x38 read +0x2C/+0x38 (the other axes). Target yaw is written by slot +0x24 (sub_002B2840) to [+0x24] = actor+0x358; velocity by slot +0x44 (sub_0006C790) to [+0x34] = actor+0x368. Writer chain for bot/AI torso aim: sub_0018AFDB(eax=ai, arg=target) takes the actor from [ai+0x20], builds the direction vector (target pos - own pos), applies sub_0017AC19, then calls sub_002AE360(ecx=dirvec, eax=0, dl=1, 1.0, esi = actor+0x2B8 when [actor+0x400] != 0 else [actor+0x8C]); mode 0 computes atan2(dir.x, dir.z) * const at 0x524A08 and calls sub_002AE200(ecx=ctrl, eax=0, yaw), which limits/normalises the yaw (sub_002ACB30), writes it as target through [esi+0x7C] vt+0x24, reads the current yaw through [esi+0x40] vt+0x20, computes a turn step (sub_002ACF40) times [esi+0xCC] and writes it as velocity through vt+0x44. The bots' only torso call is sub_18AFDB (ma2_bot_ctrl.c:499). The integrator tick (candidates sub_002AD120 / sub_002AC9C0) was not verified. So actor+0x31C is MOST LIKELY the torso yaw (current angle) and the readout of 4A is probably the controller's limit-folded/absolute angle, not an animation phase; but the sign/range behaviour (never negative, changes at rest) is unexplained. FreeTorsoRotation = qword bit 42 at +0x268 (existing wiki fact). Cheapest check: trace actor+0x31C, +0x358 and +0x368 in game while a bot torso-aims (target moves -> +0x358 should follow atan2 of the direction); also resolve what sub_002ACB30 does to the angle.
facts.how_to_use: For F40 read/trace actor+0x31C vs +0x358 with the target moving before using it as a torso-vs-leg yaw; do not call it an animation phase.

facts.title: Who hit me: the attacker is REC+0x0C (entity+0x24) inside the TakeDamage record, not stored on the victim; sub_13200F is not a kill-credit loop
facts.fact: (1) The victim stores NO last-attacker pointer (4A's researcher found none; no damage timestamp; no projectile-owner offset). REC+0xC0 = damageType (absorber index), REC+0xB0 = override amount, REC+0xB4 = flags (bit3 use +0xB0); REC+0xC4 is NOT the amount. (2) The 'hit index' 4A saw written to target+0x2E4/+0x108 is the resolver's out arg3 = attacker team/owner id (+0x2E4, +0x108, or parent+0x88): it is a team/owner id, not the attacker entity. (3) sub_13200F is NOT a kill-credit loop: it is called from sub_131D6C (a pickup latch, wiki 'sub_131D6C is a free function: one-shot pickup latch') and loops weapon groups 0.5 calling sub_DF238 with v = [entity+0x1E0] (the Alpha Strike/top-up and player-slot credit path); sub_131EB0 repair-on-kill is gated on [obj+0x1B0] and only called from 0x131DBA. The older label '0x131EB0 heals the killer' and 'destroy path -> 0x13200F' in t01/t12 text should be read with that correction. (4) Practical source for F73: hook the damage record at TakeDamage entry (read [REC+0x0C]-0x24 and out arg3) - covers bullets and splash only if they go through TakeDamage with an attacker link; beams/other paths are NOT verified. Needs an in-game trace of TakeDamage (REC+0x0C, +0xC0, return address) to confirm for each weapon kind.
facts.how_to_use: F73: read the attacker from REC+0x0C at TakeDamage entry; confirm per weapon kind with an in-game trace first.

facts.title: Measurement of the bots' leader focus (menace_of, RECOMP_BOT_LEADER_FOCUS, ma2_bot_brain.c: menace = clamp((ki
facts.fact: Measurement of the bots' leader focus (menace_of, RECOMP_BOT_LEADER_FOCUS, ma2_bot_brain.c: menace = clamp((kills - field average - 2) / 5, 0, 1.5), i.e. Two uses in code: (a) choose_target multiplies a candidate's score by 1 + lead_w[skill] x menace, lead_w 0.10/0.20/0.32/0.45 (Recruit.Elite), so at the cap 1.5 the factor is x1.15 / x1.30 / x1.48 / x1.675, small next to the finish (up to x2.5), busy (x1.5) and range/visibility factors; (b) the roam/hunt pick draws a weighted random enemy with weight 1 + hunt_w x menace, hunt_w 0.5/1/2/3. WHAT THE LOGS EXPOSE: only [BOT-HUNT] lines (DIAG on), one per hunt pick, with skill, the picked player, its kills, its menace and the total weight 'of N'. The target-choice candidate list (' [kind d in pot ttk s]') has the score but NOT the menace, and no log has the candidate set, so 'target share on the leader vs menace' and 'damage on the leader' CANNOT be computed. From 34 runs: 2727 hunt picks; 24 of 34 runs have at least one pick with menace > 0; share of hunt picks that were a menace > 0 player: Recruit 4.4 % (mean menace 0.38), Regular 4.7 % (0.27), Veteran 9.5 % (0.31), Elite 7.5 % (0.42); max menace seen 1.5 (a bot 10+ kills clear). So in these 5-minute 6v6 matches a clear leader exists only briefly and the push is rarely active. EXPECTED PICK PROBABILITY from the formula (6 live enemies, one leader): menace 0.5 -> leader picked Recruit 1.25/6.25 = 20 %, Regular 25 %, Veteran 33 %, Elite 2.5/7.5 = 33 % (uniform 17 %); menace 1.5 (cap) -> 26 / 33 / 44 / 52 %. It only decides who bots walk toward when nothing is in sight (roam, ~60-90 % of roam decisions), not who they shoot at once enemies are visible (there it is a x1.1-1.7 nudge). WOULD IT KEEP A MUCH STRONGER HUMAN'S MATCH CLOSE? Rough estimate (confidence LOW, no measurement): it saturates at 10 kills over the average, so a player 17 kills to 7 reaches the cap and then roughly 2 of the 5-6 enemy bots head for him when idle, plus a x1.1-1.7 target nudge; that is a real but moderate pressure (rough estimate +30-60 % incoming engagements), not a rubber band: it adds no handicap to damage, accuracy or spawn, and the kill/team score gap is mostly decided by team strength, so a very strong human would still win comfortably. Then the share of picks/damage on the leader vs its menace can be tabulated per skill. A test: one editor/retail run with the human playing hard (not idle) and RECOMP_BOT_LEADER_FOCUS=1 vs 0, compare the human's deaths per minute.

facts.title: fps over a long 6v6 is flat once fighting (80-100 on Under Cover); bots cost ~1.3 ms of an 11 ms frame; 0v0 does not start a Team Destruction match
facts.fact: F75 / t4-C4 result: the frame rate does not build up or fall over a long 6v6; it is set by how many units are fighting. Run A (5v6 = 11 bots + idle human): wall fps 80-100 after t~40 (dip to 53-69 at t~20-40 at first contact), median frame 10.7-12.2 ms, sim fps 87/59/79/88/89/89 at t=10/30/60/100/150/200. Run C (0v1 = one bot + idle human): 196-214 fps, 4.4-4.9 ms throughout. Run B (0v0) never started a match: Team Destruction will not start without an opponent (stuck at the Briefing Room). In run A the GPU draw time stays about 1 ms/frame, buffer upload about 0.5 ms; the bots' own CPU ([BOT-PERF]) is 110-120 ms per second = about 1.3 ms of an 11 ms frame, and the other ~8 ms over run C is the game's own simulation and render of 12 units fighting (effects, physics), not bot code. Nothing grows with match length (run A t=60 to 200: 79 to 89).
facts.how_to_use: When fps drops during a bots match, look at units in combat and other running games first; do not blame match length or the brain.

facts.title: Not It/NRC crash = delete(NULL) from the XACT update engine+0x5C list walk (no NULL guard), right after the +0x64 guard relink; same corrupt-XACT-list family
facts.fact: Crash analysis for 4D's notit-nrc-crash1. The crash is a delete(NULL): the faulting read is [ptr-0xB] with ptr = 0 inside the CRT heap block-size query, which tagged delete calls first. Guest stack decoded: 0x2BBC32 is in thunk 0x2BBC21 (20 B: pushes the CRT heap handle [0x534E1C], 0, ptr; calls sub_2BA13D, the _msize-style block-size query that does mov al,[ecx-0xB]); 0x2B83E7 in 0x2B83D0 (26 B, block-size dispatcher on the pool tag: bit 31 clear -> 2BBC21, set -> 2BBDEC); 0x12348 in 0x12330 (195 B, tagged delete wrapper: size 2B83D0, free 2B83B6, stats add via sub_1BE20; esi 0x84 / edi 0x6484A000 are the pool tag); 0x3DDEAC in 0x3DDE9E (15 B, delete(ptr) with fixed tag 0x6484A000); 0x3DFAA6 in 0x3DFA8D (33 B, node destructor sub_3E0E67 then delete when flag 1); 0x3E0ED8 in 0x3E0EC7 (21 B, Release: dec [obj+0x40], at 0 calls 3DFA8D(obj,1)); 0x3E3286 in 0x3E2FF5 (686 B, recomp_0097.c, per-node processor of the engine+0x5C list; the release is the call 0x3E0EC7 at 0x3E3281 with eax = the node); 0x3DEAFF in sub_003DEA53 (XACT per-frame update) right after call 0x3E2FF5 at 0x3DEAFA. 0x3E869C is a data address (the XACT lock pushed at 0xBBFB1), a stale stack word, not a frame. This is memory-heap code reached from the XACT update, not sound code. Walk order in sub_003DEA53: loop 1 walks edi+0x64 and calls 3DFCDF on node-8 (0x3DEAD9-0x3DEAEC); loop 2 walks edi+0x5C and calls 3E2FF5 on the raw [esi] link (0x3DEAEE-0x3DEB01). Neither loop checks for a NULL link: a zero link satisfies esi != head, so node 0 is processed. The guard's log line ('[XACT-LIST] engine list +0x64 head=009FACC4 relinked: invalid link at 00000000') matches loop 1; the crash came in loop 2 right after. VERDICT: very plausibly the known XACT list corruption (wiki xact-list-spin / xact-list-guard / xact-list-walk-freeze / xact-root-cause-open), now as a null free instead of a spin; the +0x5C walk is not covered by the guard (code-confirmed for the function identities and the [NULL-0xB] fault; the NULL node reaching the release is inferred). Possible low-cost mitigation (suggestion only, nothing changed): a NULL check in 3DDE9E and in the 0x3DEAF5 loop-2 walk; low guest memory reads without faulting, so the refcount at guest 0x40 is unknown. Open: does ma2_xact_list_repair also cover the +0x5C loop; what writes the links (root cause); a watchpoint on engine+0x5C and +0x64 link writes or a node-chain dump when the guard fires would settle it.
facts.how_to_use: When a crash/AV appears with [XACT-LIST] just before it, treat it as the XACT list corruption; the +0x5C loop at 0x3DEAEE-0x3DEB01 has no NULL guard.

facts.title: Bots crossbow/warhammer ~0 hits per shot: the bot fire path does pass the target (homing lost only to a jammer); likely a 1.5 s attribution-window counting artifact
facts.fact: Question from 4A/c4 (2026-10-27): the per-weapon table shows bots' crossbow and warhammer hitting ~0 per shot at every skill. Researcher read (no game run). (1) The bot fire path does NOT omit a lock/target handle: ai_fire (ma2_bot_ctrl.c:363-380, called at lines 520 and 557) passes the controller's target actor as the 5th argument of sub_18482E(ai, aimPt, weapon, target), like the campaign AI; sub_18482E has no separate lock field for the bot code to miss. Homing is dropped ONLY when the target has DefenseType 4 (target jamming: [target+0x21C] == 4 sets the flag at [ebp-1]; the lock target given to the barrel fire function sub_12B234 is target & mask = 0, and sub_17B222 aims at a plain point instead; code 0x1848D0 jammer test, 0x184A22-0x184A26 mask, call 0x184A55). That cannot explain ~0 for every skill unless many 4A targets were jammer-equipped or AMS-protected (active AMS destroys missiles crossing its volume; wiki: crossbow, javelin, warhammer are AMS-vulnerable, and missile hits per laser hit fell 0.077 -> 0.021 with an AMS up). (2) Lobbed shots (warhammer, mortar; weapon type is barrel+0x17C: 1 crossbow, 8 warhammer, 12 mortar) fire from the muzzle to ONE aim point = target->vtbl[0x134] plus the bots' inaccuracy offset; the bot path has no arc or clue code, so connection is decided by the game's own projectile code (not traced). (3) COUNTING ARTIFACT is the likeliest explanation but unconfirmed: the WACC ev instrumentation (commits 70445c1 and d2c32f4 in the t4A tree) was not found in the source trees searched; the existing damage_track in ma2_bots_core.c:3108 credits health drops to the shooter only within a time window ('engaged or fired within 1.5 s'); a missile that lands after the window or after the bot switched group would be credited to another weapon or none. The odd cells (crossbow Regular 0.43 / VTOL 0.48 vs Elite 0.0, 9-23 shots per cell) look like small-sample noise. Confidence: HIGH that the target is passed and homing is lost only to a jammer; MEDIUM that missiles are not lost to a missing lock; LOW on the counting-artifact cause. Cheap test: RECOMP_BOT_DIAG with one bot firing only a crossbow at a stationary undefended player; compare WACC ev with the player's health drops and projectile impacts; repeat with the attribution window widened (hits/shot should rise if it is an artifact).
facts.how_to_use: Do not retune missile aim from the WACC rows until the ev counting window is checked; test with a crossbow-only bot vs an undefended target.

facts.title: Crash xact-notit-4 (174273e, t=253.7): AI setmode(5) -> stop-in-place sub_183FAC -> sub_2AD5C0 reads max speed through a garbage body pointer (not XACT code)
facts.fact: The crash (AV fault Xbox VA 0x8D10C49F, guest stack 0x183FBE, 0x183C9B, 0x184137, 0x15D313) is in the game's AI movement controller, not in XACT. Chain: sub_15D2E9 (vtable+0x1C dispatcher) -> sub_1840A4 (move-step: calls MoveTo vtable+0x38, then at 0x18412B calls setmode(5) when the controller is in the stop state; skips it only if [0x4EAF98] matches) -> sub_183B9D (setmode, ecx = controller, eax = new mode, stores mode at +0x12C) -> sub_183FAC (enter-mode-5 handler: edx = [ctrl+0x24] = the body/actor, eax=1, push 0; calls sub_2AD5C0; then reads [[ctrl+0x20]+0x28] , if it differs from [0x4EAF98], calls a vtable+0xC method of [[[ctrl+0x20]+0x8C]+0x10C] with a zeroed vec3) -> sub_2AD5C0 (set forward speed as percent of max: cvtsi2ss(percent) * [body+0xBC] * [0x493B44], clamped against [body+0xC0]). The fault is the first body read: [body+0xBC] with body = [ctrl+0x24] = ~0x8D11C3E3, a non-pointer (host region 0x8D11C000 is unmapped, outside guest RAM). Controller esi = 0x023B9200 is an ordinary guest-heap AI component (same range as the bot vehicles 0x023D5A10, 0x024B0320), so its +0x24 field was stale/overwritten: the controller (or the heap block under it) was freed and reused, or the body was torn down, while the AI tick still held it. Context: two bots were killed 1 s earlier (BOT-KILL t=252.7 bots 1 and 9) and bot 4 retargeted a vehicle at t=253.7. The XACT guard in 174273e only runs inside the XACT list walks (+0x44/+0x64/+0x5C), writes nothing outside the XACT node it cuts, and logged 0 [XACT-LIST] lines in this run, so it did not execute before the crash. A direct code path from the XACT guard cut to this crash does not exist; the only possible link is memory corruption (a freed XACT-pool block, allocator id 0x84, that overlaps or was recycled into the AI block, or a write through a stale XACT pointer into a recycled block). UPDATE: seen ONCE in 13 Not It NRC runs (5 on a67af79 + 8 on guard exes), 1 s after BOT-KILL of bots 1 and 9; not reproduced since. a stale AI controller after a kill. Root cause unknown.
facts.how_to_use: Treat as a separate AI stale-controller use-after-free candidate. With the ce2470b tracer (XMemFree ring + [XACT-UAF]), after a crash like this look up who freed the block covering the crash controller (esi in the crash line, 0x023B9200 here) in the free ring: an XACT-pool free covering it = XACT-related, any other free = AI/vehicle teardown bug. Dump 0x20 bytes of the controller (+0x20/+0x24/+0x12C) at crash time. Compare with the a67af79 baseline crash stacks to see whether it is the same stack (it would then predate the XACT guard).

facts.title: XACT objects are freed by the game's own XMemFree sub_00012330 (allocator id 0x84 -> pool [0x50BA38]), never by xbox_HeapFree; XMemFree rejects NULL
facts.fact: XACT engine objects are freed through the game's own XMemFree sub_00012330(ptr, attrs): the allocator id is attrs byte 2, and 0x84 selects the XACT pool [0x50BA38] via sub_0001BE20. These frees never reach the host's xbox_HeapFree, so a UAF hook on xbox_HeapFree alone cannot see XACT block frees. The game's XMemFree does not accept NULL: sub_002B83D0 reads [ptr-0xB], so XMemFree(NULL) faults. Node offsets inside the XACT objects: the +0x44 list node = obj+0x58, the +0x64 node = obj+8, the +0x5C node = obj+0.
facts.how_to_use: To trace XACT use-after-free, hook sub_00012330 (as the t4c-xact ce2470b tracer does) and filter on attrs byte 2 == 0x84; a free of an object that still has a linked node (obj+0x58 / obj+8 / obj+0) is the bug. Skip and log XMemFree(NULL) rather than calling it.
